Job title: Lead Management Specialist
Location: US - Remote
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  
 
Job Overview: 
The Lead Management Specialist serves as the primary point of contact for all inbound inquiries received via digital channels (web forms, web chat) and phone. This role focuses on speed, professionalism, and qualification accuracy to convert inbound interest into well-defined, sales-ready opportunities. This position partners closely with Application Engineering, Inside and Outside Sales and cross-functional teams to ensure high-quality lead handling, adherence to service level agreements, and a best-in-class customer experience. The role is foundational in developing strong commercial skills and serves as an entry point into broader sales, marketing, or commercial excellence career paths. This level owns budgetary quoting within approved templates and commercial guardrails. The role does not own opportunities beyond qualification and handoff.
 
 Responsibilities:

  • Respond to all inbound inquiries within established SLAs
  • Conduct structured discovery using approved qualification frameworks
  • Capture complete and accurate customer information and qualification notes in CRM
  • Convert qualified leads into Opportunities, assign correct owners, and ensure clear documentation
  • Execute structured nurture of inbound leads, including quote reminders and clarifications
  • Provide budgetary quotes within approved templates and scope
  • Maintain high data-quality standards in CRM across leads, opportunities, and activities, incl., quote logs, customer responses and next-step documentation to support Sales
  • Update dispositions accurately (Won, Lost) in alignment with Opportunity Owners
  • Support Marketing with feedback on lead quality, campaign alignment, and customer trends
  • Escalate complex technical, pricing pr product-fit questions to the appropriate sales or technical team.
  • Participate in team huddles, 1:1 development check-ins and alignment meetings
  • Provide structure feedback on inbound lead quality and recurring customer questions
  • Identify opportunities to improve response templates, qualification questions, or routing rules
 
Requirements: 
  • 1+ years of experience in Lead Management, sales development, customer support, or related role
  • Fluency in English
  • Fluency in Spanish
 
Competencies:
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • High attention to detail and accuracy in CRM usage
  • Ability to multitask in a fast-paced, high-volume environment
  • Customer-centric mindset with strong problem-solving skills
  • Coachable, dependable, and organized
  • Willingness to work 9am-5pm Pacific Time
 
Preferences: 
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred (Business, Communications, Marketing, Engineering, or related field)
 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements
  • US- Remote with Willingness to work 9am-5pm Pacific Time

 
Pay Range
The total pay range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is $60,000-70,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive discretionary annual bonuses and incentive compensation.
 
What we Offer
 At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment — as well as for our individual well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support needed to take charge of your health and future. 
 
Our benefits include healthcare coverage (medical, prescription, dental, and vision), wellness programs, life insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off, and an employee stock program, among other offerings. These benefits, combined with our pay transparency and inclusive culture, reflect our commitment to supporting you at work and beyond.
 
TO APPLY: Please apply via our website https://careers.irco.com by Nov 04, 2026 in order to be considered for this position.

Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Electrical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization                
Location:  Sidney, OH
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in this true ground-floor opportunity. The Electrical Design Engineer, Power Generation Containerization will help design, integrate, and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the electrical architecture, system integration, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.

The Electrical Design Engineer will own key aspects of the electrical design and integration of large generator systems, including generator enclosures, power connections, controls access, electrical equipment layout, and overall packaged-system integration. These are not small commercial generators, but large-scale diesel generator systems designed to provide critical backup power for data center environments where reliability, uptime, and continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from design and integration through validation, manufacturing readiness, and commercialization. The role will partner closely with the Mechanical Engineer, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, suppliers, project management, and the Sidney plant to ensure the complete packaged solution meets both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings electrical design experience in power generation, large generator systems, data center electrical infrastructure, mission-critical backup power, industrial equipment, or modular/containerized power systems. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, 2MW+ systems, diesel generator sets, and environments where code compliance, serviceability, and reliability are critical is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.

Responsibilities:

Electrical System Design

  • Design electrical systems for containerized and modular power generation packages supporting data center applications.

  • Develop electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, wiring drawings, cable schedules, panel layouts, and system architecture documentation.

  • Design and integrate:

    • Diesel and natural gas generator systems

    • Generator paralleling systems

    • Switchgear and switchboards

    • Medium- and low-voltage distribution equipment

    • Automatic transfer switches (ATS)

    • UPS interfaces

    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)

    • Auxiliary systems including HVAC, lighting, monitoring, and fire protection

  • Perform electrical calculations including:

    • Load flow analysis

    • Equipment sizing

    • Short-circuit studies

    • Voltage drop calculations

    • Protective device coordination

Data Center Power Solutions

  • Develop solutions that support mission-critical data center reliability requirements including N, N+1, and 2N architectures.

  • Support integration with customer electrical infrastructure and utility interconnection requirements.

  • Design systems to meet data center expectations for uptime, maintainability, scalability, and serviceability.

  • Collaborate with customers and internal stakeholders to evaluate custom power generation and backup power solutions.

  • Support electrical integration for modular and prefabricated power systems used in hyperscale and colocation data centers.

Product Development & Standardization

  • Drive development of standardized containerized power generation platforms for data center markets.

  • Create and maintain engineering specifications, design standards, and best practices.

  • Conduct design reviews and support FMEA, reliability analysis, and risk assessments.

  • Evaluate emerging technologies including hybrid power systems, energy storage, microgrids, and renewable energy integrations.

Testing, Validation & Commissioning

  • Support prototype development, testing, and validation activities.

  • Develop and review Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) procedures and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) protocols.

  • Participate in commissioning and startup activities for customer projects.

  • Troubleshoot electrical integration issues during manufacturing, deployment, and field operation.

Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work directly with data center customers, consultants, contractors, and equipment suppliers.

  • Provide technical leadership during project execution and customer design reviews.

  • Support sales and business development teams with technical proposals and engineering evaluations.

  • Coordinate with manufacturing and sourcing teams to ensure successful product implementation.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline. 
  • 3+ years of progressive electrical design experience ideally in power generation, critical facilities, industrial systems, modular infrastructure, or related industries. 
  • 3+ years experience interpreting electrical specifications and customer technical requirements.
  • 2+ years experience designing power distribution systems and power generation equipment.
  • 2+ years of proficienct experience in AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, SolidWorks Electrical, or similar design platforms.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in: 
    • Generator systems 
    • Electrical protection and coordination 
    • Low-voltage and medium-voltage power distribution 
    • Electrical codes and standards

 

 

Core Competencies:

  • Emergency and standby power systems

  • Generator controls and synchronization

  • Utility interconnection

  • Switchgear and switchboards

  • Protective relaying and system coordination

  • Medium-voltage distribution systems

  • Containerized power solutions

  • Energy storage integration

  • Mission-critical infrastructure

  • Data center electrical architecture


Preferences:

  • 5+ years of experience supporting data center, mission-critical, or power generation industries.

  • Experience with:

    • Data center electrical infrastructure

    • Generator paralleling systems

    • Medium-voltage switchgear

    • Microgrid applications

    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)

  • Knowledge of data center design practices and redundancy architectures.

  • Familiarity with PLC controls, SCADA systems, and power monitoring systems.

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.

  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers such as Microsoft, AWS, Google, Meta, or other colocation providers.

 

 

Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH

  • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm


Pay Range - The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. About ILC Dover
ILC Dover is a global leader in engineered products that protect people, products, and brands. From space exploration and defense systems to pharmaceutical and industrial applications, ILC Dover delivers mission?critical solutions where performance, reliability, and safety matter most. ILC Dover offers competitive compensation and benefits within a collaborative, engineering?driven culture that values innovation, teamwork, and technical excellence.

Job Overview: 
The Project Engineer supports the successful execution of engineering and production programs related to Extravehicular Activity (EVA) spacesuit systems by coordinating cross-functional teams, tracking progress, and ensuring timely achievement of key program milestones. This role assists in planning, organizing, and managing projects across spacesuit hardware development, integration, and production activities, working closely with engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to deliver flight-critical hardware on schedule, within scope, and within budget.
This position is based at the Frederica, Delaware manufacturing facility and directly supports the development, assembly, integration, testing, and sustainment of EVA spacesuit systems, with a primary focus on the Space Suit Assembly (SSA) in support of NASA programs. The Project Engineer plays a key role in managing the full hardware lifecycle—from design release through fabrication, production, verification, and delivery—ensuring alignment with NASA requirements and strict adherence to human spaceflight safety and quality standards.

Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and monitor EVA spacesuit hardware projects from design release through production, integration, and delivery
  • Serve as a liaison between engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to ensure alignment on production priorities, requirements, and schedules
  • Support execution of spacesuit assembly and integration activities at the Frederica site, ensuring readiness for build, test, and delivery
  • Ensure hardware fabrication and production efforts are completed on schedule and within budget constraints
  • Gather and manage technical, manufacturing, and program data to support requirements definition, build readiness, and production execution
  • Lead hardware failure investigations for spacesuit components and assemblies; facilitate root cause analysis (RCA) and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) across engineering and factory operations
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication with program managers and stakeholders regarding risks, issues, and impacts to cost, schedule, or technical performance
  • Interface with NASA customers to communicate project status, technical progress, risks, and key milestones through formal reviews, reports, and coordination meetings
  • Support integration, test, and verification activities for EVA hardware, ensuring compliance with NASA program requirements and certification standards
  • Assist with transition of hardware from development into production, including coordination of build plans, work instructions, and configuration control
  • Support project planning activities across proposal, contract execution, and program lifecycle phases for EVA spacesuit programs
  • Conduct routine tasks as directed in support of EVA program execution


*This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications:
  • Must be able to access shared government program databases (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident)
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field

Core Competencies: 
  • Experience in manufacturing, engineering, or product development environment preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and interface control documents (ICDs)
  • Interest in project management and product development (PMP or CAPM a plus)
  • Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking abilities
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic knowledge of project management methodologies and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project)
  • Strong collaboration, problem-solving skills, and ability to work effectively in team environments (including navigating constructive conflict)
  • Experience with hardware development lifecycle including design, build, test, and qualification phases
  • Experience supporting or participating in hardware failure investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation preferred

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
  • Fully Site Based in Frederica, DE
  • Availability to travel up to 25 % of the time (e.g., customer visits, training at our technical centers, trade shows, etc.).
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to wet or humid conditions (non-weather); fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals.  The employee is frequently exposed to work near moving mechanical parts.  The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Title: Manufacturing Technician, Field Services
Location: Sedalia, MO (Hybrid)
 
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview: 
Build it. Prove it. Start it up. On the floor and in the field, this isn’t a stay-in-one-place technician role. As our Manufacturing Systems Technician, you’ll operate in two worlds—splitting your time between hands-on fabrication in our Sedalia facility (~70%) and field support (~20–30%). From cutting and assembling PVC/CPVC systems (with some stainless in the mix), this is precision, hands-on work where what you build is exactly what ships—no separation between effort and outcome. The other 20–30% of the time, you’re on-site, in front of the customer, watching your system come to life.

You’ll verify installations, run wet and leak testing, and troubleshoot in real time—making the call when something’s off and fixing it before it slows the project down. When things don’t go to plan—and sometimes they won’t—you’re the one who figures it out and keeps everything moving. We’re not standing still either. We’re expanding and actively scaling, with a strong pipeline of projects already lined up. You won’t be stepping into maintenance mode—you’ll be stepping into build mode, where your impact is visible from day one. If you read mechanical drawings, system layouts, without hesitation, work confidently in fabrication, and communicate clearly when it matters—especially under pressure—you’ll do well here. More importantly, this is for someone who takes ownership when the system is live, not just when it’s on paper.  
Bottom line: This role is built for someone who wants to go beyond building parts—someone who takes pride in building complete systems and seeing them through to successful startup and real-world performance.

Responsibilities
  • Operate fabrication equipment including saws, drills, routers, CNC machines, and injection molding equipment to cut, drill, and assemble PVC/CPVC components.
  • Measure, fit, and assemble parts according to shop drawings, blueprints, and work orders.
  • Perform machine setups, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting to support efficient production operations.
  • Conduct quality inspections to ensure products meet company standards and specifications.
  • Maintain accurate production records and report material usage, equipment issues, or production concerns.
  • Collaborate with team members to meet daily production goals, schedules, and deadlines.
  • Load and unload shipments, pick and pack orders, and assist with inventory management activities.
  • Support field installations and system startups for aeration equipment, including inspections and functional verification.
  • Assist with troubleshooting and communicate effectively with contractors, supervisors, and engineering teams during startup activities.
  • Follow all workplace safety procedures while maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work environment.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, field experience with equipment installation, startup, troubleshooting.
  • 1+ years experience reading drawings, blue prints, basic system layouts

Core Competencies 
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings, blueprints, and system layouts with strong mechanical aptitude and experience using hand tools, power tools, and production equipment.
  • Commitment to quality workmanship with strong attention to detail and adherence to production and inspection standards.
  • Strong problem-solving and time management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and resolve issues efficiently.
  • Proficient computer and communication skills for documentation, reporting, production tracking, and collaboration across teams.
  • Adaptable, dependable, and eager to learn new skills while supporting evolving production and field operations.

Preferences: 
  • Experience in pipe fabrication, plumbing, aeration systems, or plastics manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with PVC solvent welding, mechanical fittings, or aeration diffuser systems.
  • OSHA 10/30 safety training.

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • Based at our site in Sedalia, MO
  • National Field Travel up to 30% 
  • Travel expenses covered to include company Vehicle use

What We Offer: 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. Job Title: Mechanical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization                
Location:  Sidney, OH
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in a true ground-floor opportunity. The Mechanical Engineer – Power Generation Containerization will help design and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the mechanical architecture, product platform, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.  

The Mechanical Engineer will own key aspects of the mechanical design and integration of these large generator systems, including structural assemblies, enclosures, cooling systems, fuel and base tanks, equipment layouts, and overall mechanical packaging. These are complex systems built around large diesel engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, controls, and serviceable layouts designed to provide critical backup power where uptime and cooling continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from concept and CAD design through manufacturing readiness and commercialization. The role will work closely with electrical engineering, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, project management, sales, and the Sidney plant to ensure solutions meet both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings mechanical design experience in power generation, large industrial equipment, modular systems, or complex packaged equipment. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, large diesel generators, 2MW+ systems, cooling systems, fuel tanks, enclosures, or applicable UL requirements is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.


Responsibilities: 
Mechanical Design & Engineering
  • Design containerized and modular power generation solutions for data center backup and prime power applications.
  • Develop 3D models, detailed drawings, assemblies, fabrication packages, and engineering documentation using CAD software.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Generator enclosures and power modules
    • ISO container-based power systems
    • Structural support systems and equipment skids
    • Fuel storage and fuel delivery systems
    • Air intake and exhaust systems
    • Ventilation and cooling systems
    • Acoustic attenuation systems
    • Fire protection interfaces
    • Service access and maintenance provisions
  • Perform engineering calculations related to structural integrity, airflow, cooling performance, vibration, noise attenuation, and equipment support.

Data Center Solutions Engineering
  • Design power generation enclosures and modules to support mission-critical data center applications.
  • Ensure equipment layouts support uptime, maintainability, safe operations, and rapid serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to develop custom solutions that meet data center site constraints and operational requirements.
  • Support designs for N, N+1, and 2N redundancy architectures.
  • Evaluate and optimize designs for deployment within hyperscale and colocation environments.

Thermal Management & Cooling
  • Develop cooling and ventilation solutions for high-performance generator systems.
  • Perform airflow analysis and thermal assessments to ensure proper equipment operation across varying environmental conditions.
  • Support integration of HVAC equipment, engine cooling packages, and auxiliary thermal management systems.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cooling efficiency and reduce energy consumption.

Product Development & Standardization
  • Support development of standardized containerized power generation platforms.
  • Drive design improvements focused on reliability, manufacturability, quality, cost, and serviceability.
  • Participate in design reviews, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and root cause investigations.
  • Evaluate new technologies, materials, and manufacturing methods to improve product performance.

Manufacturing & Testing Support
  • Provide engineering support for prototype builds and production manufacturing.
  • Resolve mechanical design issues during fabrication, assembly, and field deployment.
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), validation testing, and commissioning activities.
  • Review supplier drawings and support qualification of mechanical components and assemblies.

Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Collaborate with electrical, controls, acoustics, and thermal engineering teams to ensure complete system integration.
  • Participate in technical reviews with customers, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.
  • Support sales and project teams with technical evaluations, proposals, and feasibility assessments.
  • Assist field service organizations with troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.

Requirements
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive mechanical development design experience ideally in power generation, industrial equipment, modular systems, heavy equipment, or related industries.
  • 2+ years experience with 3D CAD software such as SolidWorks, Creo, CATIA, Inventor, or similar platforms, with bility to develop engineering documentation and manufacturing drawings.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in:
    • Structural design
    • Sheet metal fabrication
    • Welded assemblies
    • Airflow and ventilation systems
    • Thermal management principles
    • Mechanical packaging concepts

    Core Competencies
    • Power generation equipment packaging
    • Containerized power solutions
    • Structural and mechanical design
    • Thermal management systems
    • Airflow and ventilation engineering
    • Acoustic engineering and noise reduction
    • Fuel system integration
    • Vibration isolation
    • Design for manufacturability (DFM)
    • Reliability and maintainability engineering
    • Data center infrastructure requirements
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

    Preferences:
    • 5+ years of experience in power generation, mission-critical infrastructure, modular construction, or data center industries.
    • Experience designing:
      • Generator enclosures
      • Containerized equipment packages
      • Cooling systems
      • Fuel systems
      • Acoustic attenuation solutions
    • Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
    • Knowledge of ISO container standards and transportation requirements.
    • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers.
    • Understanding of engine cooling systems, exhaust systems, and vibration isolation.
    • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.

    Travel & Work Arrangements
    • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
    • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

    Pay Range - The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

    What We Offer 
    At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

    Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

job.title: Engineering Technician
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand and ILC Dover is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.


 

 

Job Summary: 

 

The Engineering Technician performs technical analyses, conducts experiments and testing, collects and documents data, and supports engineers in product development, prototype fabrication, suit testing and continuous improvement initiatives. This position works independently on complex assignments and contributes to product quality, reliability, and operational excellence.

 

*Essential Job Functions:

  • Demonstrate and promote compliance with all company safety policies, procedures, and standards.
  • Assist engineers with the analysis, testing, troubleshooting, and support of machines, tools, equipment, and mechanical systems.
  • Repair, rework, or modify mechanical assemblies to ensure compliance with operational specifications and tolerances.
  • Fabricate and assemble mechanical prototypes from blueprints, engineering drawings, schematics, and sketches.
  • Conduct functional, operational, structural, leakage, and reliability testing of prototype and production units using required Ground Support Equipment (GSE).
  • Collect, analyze, document, and report test data and any anomalies found.
  • Support root cause investigations, corrective actions, and failure analysis activities.
  • Maintain accurate documentation, reports, and records related to testing, troubleshooting, and product evaluations.
  • Perform complex tasks and completes assignments with minimal or no supervision.
  • Exercise independent judgment while working within established procedures and engineering standards.
  • Support suit demonstrations and testing activities utilizing required GSE.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

 

*This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

 

  • Must be able to access shared database with government programs and NASA facilities required to support testing activities (i.e., U.S. Citizen or U.S. Person)
  • Requires high school diploma or trade school certification
  • 3+ years of relevant technical, manufacturing, testing, or engineering support experience.
  • Ability to safely use hand tools, power tools, testing equipment, and GSE.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with peers, cross-functional teams, and external customers.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proven ability to gather, document, analyze, and report technical information.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate degree in Engineering Technology or a related technical discipline.
  • Relevant technical certifications, specialized training, or industry-recognized credentials.
  • Experience supporting aerospace, manufacturing, product development, testing, or laboratory environments.

 

 

Work Environment: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

This position is performed in a manufacturing and testing environment where the use of required personal protective equipment (PPE) is mandatory. Employees will frequently work near moving mechanical equipment and may occasionally be exposed to wet or humid conditions, airborne particulates, fumes, and hazardous chemicals. The work environment generally has a moderate noise level.

 

Physical Demands: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

The employee must be able to perform physical activities including sitting, standing, walking, reaching, bending, stooping, kneeling, and crouching on a frequent basis. The role requires working in production and testing environments for extended periods and occasionally lifting or moving materials weighing up to 50 pounds. Visual abilities required include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to focus and adjust vision as needed to safely perform job duties.

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in this true ground-floor opportunity. The Electrical Design Engineer, Power Generation Containerization will help design, integrate, and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the electrical architecture, system integration, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.

The Electrical Design Engineer will own key aspects of the electrical design and integration of large generator systems, including generator enclosures, power connections, controls access, electrical equipment layout, and overall packaged-system integration. These are not small commercial generators, but large-scale diesel generator systems designed to provide critical backup power for data center environments where reliability, uptime, and continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from design and integration through validation, manufacturing readiness, and commercialization. The role will partner closely with the Mechanical Engineer, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, suppliers, project management, and the Sidney plant to ensure the complete packaged solution meets both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings electrical design experience in power generation, large generator systems, data center electrical infrastructure, mission-critical backup power, industrial equipment, or modular/containerized power systems. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, 2MW+ systems, diesel generator sets, and environments where code compliance, serviceability, and reliability are critical is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.

Responsibilities:
Electrical System Design
  • Design electrical systems for containerized and modular power generation packages supporting data center applications.
  • Develop electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, wiring drawings, cable schedules, panel layouts, and system architecture documentation.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Diesel and natural gas generator systems
    • Generator paralleling systems
    • Switchgear and switchboards
    • Medium- and low-voltage distribution equipment
    • Automatic transfer switches (ATS)
    • UPS interfaces
    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
    • Auxiliary systems including HVAC, lighting, monitoring, and fire protection
  • Perform electrical calculations including:
    • Load flow analysis
    • Equipment sizing
    • Short-circuit studies
    • Voltage drop calculations

job.description:

Job Overview 

The Contract Manager, North America will support business growth by reviewing, drafting, and negotiating commercial and federal government contracts while protecting Ingersoll Rand from legal, financial, operational, and compliance risk. This role will partner closely with Sales, Customer Care, Finance, Operations, Legal, Compliance, and other stakeholders to deliver practical, timely guidance, strengthen contract governance, and improve the end-to-end contracting process. 

The successful candidate will combine sound judgment, customer focus, attention to detail, and an ownership mindset. The role will also serve as a key resource for U.S. federal contracting matters, including interpretation of applicable Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and agency supplement requirements, management of required clauses and flow-downs, and support for audit-ready contract administration. 

Responsibilities 

•  Review, draft, revise, and negotiate a broad range of customer-facing agreements, including sales contracts, master agreements, purchase orders, non-disclosure agreements, amendments, and other commercial documents, with a focus on enabling growth while appropriately managing risk. 

•  Lead contract review for U.S. federal, state, and municipal government customers, evaluating solicitations, representations and certifications, contract terms, and applicable FAR, Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and other agency-specific requirements. 

•  Identify, interpret, and coordinate required government contract clauses and subcontract flow-downs, partnering with Legal, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Finance, Supply Chain, Trade Compliance, Quality, and Operations to confirm obligations are understood and executable. 

•  Advise business partners on federal contracting risks and requirements, including compliance, records, audits, government property, intellectual property and data rights, cybersecurity, domestic sourcing, pricing, changes, claims, disputes, and closeout, as applicable to the contract. 

•  Partner directly with customers and internal stakeholders to negotiate legal terms, resolve contract issues, communicate status, and drive timely decisions and approvals in accordance with company policy and delegated authority. 

•  Maintain and continuously improve standard contract templates, playbooks, clause libraries, policies, approval workflows, and contract management materials, with clear standards for both commercial and government contracting. 

•  Develop and deliver practical training for Sales and other customer-facing teams on contract review requirements, risk identification, escalation protocols, federal contract obligations, and compliant contract administration. 

•  Use data, operating rhythms, and continuous improvement methods to strengthen cycle time, visibility, consistency, recordkeeping, and audit readiness across the contract lifecycle, while supporting disputes, investigations, and corrective actions when needed. 

Requirements 

•  Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience, with 3 or more years of experience reviewing and negotiating commercial contracts, government contracts, or related legal terms and conditions. 

•  Working knowledge of contract law and demonstrated ability to interpret complex contractual requirements, assess risk, and translate legal concepts into practical business guidance. 

•  Experience supporting U.S. federal, state, and municipal contracts or subcontracts, including familiarity with FAR requirements. 

•  Strong written and verbal communication, organization, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage confidential information and multiple priorities in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. 

•  Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Word and Excel, and experience using contract lifecycle management, ERP, or related business systems. 

Core Competencies 

Ownership Mindset: Takes accountability, anticipates risk, and follows through. 

Customer Focus: Enables timely business outcomes with clear, practical guidance. 

Integrity and Judgment: Applies policy consistently and escalates appropriately. 

Continuous Improvement: Simplifies processes and builds scalable, repeatable solutions. 

Collaboration and Influence: Builds trusted partnerships across functions and levels. 

Execution Excellence: Balances pace, detail, and quality across competing priorities. 

Preferences 

•  Experience supporting a manufacturer, industrial business, or other complex, matrixed organization. 

•  Juris Doctor, paralegal credential, contracts certification, or other relevant advanced education or certification.

Job Title: Electrical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization                
Location:  Sidney, OH
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in this true ground-floor opportunity. The Electrical Design Engineer, Power Generation Containerization will help design, integrate, and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the electrical architecture, system integration, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.

The Electrical Design Engineer will own key aspects of the electrical design and integration of large generator systems, including generator enclosures, power connections, controls access, electrical equipment layout, and overall packaged-system integration. These are not small commercial generators, but large-scale diesel generator systems designed to provide critical backup power for data center environments where reliability, uptime, and continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from design and integration through validation, manufacturing readiness, and commercialization. The role will partner closely with the Mechanical Engineer, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, suppliers, project management, and the Sidney plant to ensure the complete packaged solution meets both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings electrical design experience in power generation, large generator systems, data center electrical infrastructure, mission-critical backup power, industrial equipment, or modular/containerized power systems. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, 2MW+ systems, diesel generator sets, and environments where code compliance, serviceability, and reliability are critical is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.

Responsibilities:
Electrical System Design
  • Design electrical systems for containerized and modular power generation packages supporting data center applications.
  • Develop electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, wiring drawings, cable schedules, panel layouts, and system architecture documentation.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Diesel and natural gas generator systems
    • Generator paralleling systems
    • Switchgear and switchboards
    • Medium- and low-voltage distribution equipment
    • Automatic transfer switches (ATS)
    • UPS interfaces
    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
    • Auxiliary systems including HVAC, lighting, monitoring, and fire protection
  • Perform electrical calculations including:
    • Load flow analysis
    • Equipment sizing
    • Short-circuit studies
    • Voltage drop calculations
    • Protective device coordination
Data Center Power Solutions
  • Develop solutions that support mission-critical data center reliability requirements including N, N+1, and 2N architectures.
  • Support integration with customer electrical infrastructure and utility interconnection requirements.
  • Design systems to meet data center expectations for uptime, maintainability, scalability, and serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal stakeholders to evaluate custom power generation and backup power solutions.
  • Support electrical integration for modular and prefabricated power systems used in hyperscale and colocation data centers.
Product Development & Standardization
  • Drive development of standardized containerized power generation platforms for data center markets.
  • Create and maintain engineering specifications, design standards, and best practices.
  • Conduct design reviews and support FMEA, reliability analysis, and risk assessments.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies including hybrid power systems, energy storage, microgrids, and renewable energy integrations.
Testing, Validation & Commissioning
  • Support prototype development, testing, and validation activities.
  • Develop and review Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) procedures and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) protocols.
  • Participate in commissioning and startup activities for customer projects.
  • Troubleshoot electrical integration issues during manufacturing, deployment, and field operation.
Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Work directly with data center customers, consultants, contractors, and equipment suppliers.
  • Provide technical leadership during project execution and customer design reviews.
  • Support sales and business development teams with technical proposals and engineering evaluations.
  • Coordinate with manufacturing and sourcing teams to ensure successful product implementation.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline. 
  • 3+ years of progressive electrical design experience ideally in power generation, critical facilities, industrial systems, modular infrastructure, or related industries. 
  • 3+ years experience interpreting electrical specifications and customer technical requirements.
  • 2+ years experience designing power distribution systems and power generation equipment.
  • 2+ years of proficienct experience in AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, SolidWorks Electrical, or similar design platforms.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in: 
    • Generator systems 
    • Electrical protection and coordination 
    • Low-voltage and medium-voltage power distribution 
    • Electrical codes and standards


Core Competencies:
  • Emergency and standby power systems
  • Generator controls and synchronization
  • Utility interconnection
  • Switchgear and switchboards
  • Protective relaying and system coordination
  • Medium-voltage distribution systems
  • Containerized power solutions
  • Energy storage integration
  • Mission-critical infrastructure
  • Data center electrical architecture

Preferences:

  • 5+ years of experience supporting data center, mission-critical, or power generation industries.
  • Experience with:
    • Data center electrical infrastructure
    • Generator paralleling systems
    • Medium-voltage switchgear
    • Microgrid applications
    • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
  • Knowledge of data center design practices and redundancy architectures.
  • Familiarity with PLC controls, SCADA systems, and power monitoring systems.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.
  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers such as Microsoft, AWS, Google, Meta, or other colocation providers.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
  • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

Pay Range - The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

The Mechanical Engineer – Power Generation Containerization will help design and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the mechanical architecture, product platform, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.  

The Mechanical Engineer will own key aspects of the mechanical design and integration of these large generator systems, including structural assemblies, enclosures, cooling systems, fuel and base tanks, equipment layouts, and overall mechanical packaging. These are complex systems built around large diesel engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, controls, and serviceable layouts designed to provide critical backup power where uptime and cooling continuity are essential.  As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from concept and CAD design through manufacturing readiness and commercialization. The role will work closely with electrical engineering, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, project management, sales, and the Sidney plant to ensure solutions meet both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

Responsibilities: 
Mechanical Design & Engineering
  • Design containerized and modular power generation solutions for data center backup and prime power applications.
  • Develop 3D models, detailed drawings, assemblies, fabrication packages, and engineering documentation using CAD software.
  • Design and integrate:
    • Generator enclosures and power modules
    • ISO container-based power systems
    • Structural support systems and equipment skids
    • Fuel storage and fuel delivery systems
    • Air intake and exhaust systems
    • Ventilation and cooling systems
    • Acoustic attenuation systems
    • Fire protection interfaces
    • Service access and maintenance provisions
  • Perform engineering calculations related to structural integrity, airflow, cooling performance, vibration, noise attenuation, and equipment support.

Data Center Solutions Engineering
  • Design power generation enclosures and modules to support mission-critical data center applications.
  • Ensure equipment layouts support uptime, maintainability, safe operations, and rapid serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to develop custom solutions that meet data center site constraints and operational requirements.
  • Support designs for N, N+1, and 2N redundancy architectures.
  • Evaluate and optimize designs for deployment within hyperscale and colocation environments.

Thermal Management & Cooling
  • Develop cooling and ventilation solutions for high-performance generator systems.
  • Perform airflow analysis and thermal assessments to ensure proper equipment operation across varying environmental conditions.
  • Support integration of HVAC equipment, engine cooling packages, and auxiliary thermal management systems.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cooling efficiency and reduce energy consumption.

Product Development & Standardization
  • Support development of standardized containerized power generation platforms.
  • Drive design improvements focused on reliability, manufacturability, quality, cost, and serviceability.
  • Participate in design reviews, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and root cause investigations.
  • Evaluate new technologies, materials, and manufacturing methods to improve product performance.

Manufacturing & Testing Support
  • Provide engineering support for prototype builds and production manufacturing.
  • Resolve mechanical design issues during fabrication, assembly, and field deployment.
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), validation testing, and commissioning activities.
  • Review supplier drawings and support qualification of mechanical components and assemblies.

Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Collaborate with electrical, controls, acoustics, and thermal engineering teams to ensure complete system integration.
  • Participate in technical reviews with customers, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.
  • Support sales and project teams with technical evaluations, proposals, and feasibility assessments.
  • Assist field service organizations with troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.

Requirements
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive mechanical development design experience ideally in power generation, industrial equipment, modular systems, heavy equipment, or related industries.
  • 2+ years experience with 3D CAD software such as SolidWorks, Creo, CATIA, Inventor, or similar platforms, with bility to develop engineering documentation and manufacturing drawings.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in:
    • Structural design
    • Sheet metal fabrication
    • Welded assemblies
    • Airflow and ventilation systems
    • Thermal management principles
    • Mechanical packaging concepts

    Core Competencies
    • Power generation equipment packaging
    • Containerized power solutions
    • Structural and mechanical design
    • Thermal management systems
    • Airflow and ventilation engineering
    • Acoustic engineering and noise reduction
    • Fuel system integration
    • Vibration isolation
    • Design for manufacturability (DFM)
    • Reliability and maintainability engineering
    • Data center infrastructure requirements
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

    Preferences:
    • 5+ years of experience in power generation, mission-critical infrastructure, modular construction, or data center industries.
    • Experience designing:
      • Generator enclosures
      • Containerized equipment packages
      • Cooling systems
      • Fuel systems
      • Acoustic attenuation solutions
    • Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
    • Knowledge of ISO container standards and transportation requirements.
    • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers.
    • Understanding of engine cooling systems, exhaust systems, and vibration isolation.
    • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.

    Travel & Work Arrangements
    • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
    • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm

They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows. 

Responsibilities:

  • Suggests, evaluates, implements & manages multiple manufacturing projects from beginning to end
  • Evaluates, develops and implements machining processes on current or future assets
  • Implements capital equipment including evaluation, selection, run-offs, and implementation
  • Maintains manufacturing best practices including precision machining, lean manufacturing, and machine tool / tooling technologies
  • Evaluates non-conforming material and provides proper disposition
  • Leads special projects including NPD, insourcing, productivity and capital procurement
  • Designs tooling, gages and fixtures using 3D modeling software
  • Develops manufacturing routings internal and sub-con operations
  • Leads machine tool installations throughout the entire process
  • Supports production efforts through troubleshooting manufacturing issues
  • Ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards
  • Supports safety and environmental practices
  • Performs other duties assigned by immediate supervisor
Requirements: 

  • 4+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering.
  • Strong analytical ability to solve issues such as manufacturing problems and dimensional or calculation errors.
  • 1+ years of experience using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • 1+ years of experience in advanced engineering drawings including GD&T and tolerance analysis.
Core Competencies:

  • Technical Expertise: knowledge of manufacturing processes and technologies. 
  • Solid understanding of electro-mechanical assembly and machining processes and overall business operations.
  • Problem-Solving: Analytical skills to develop effective solutions. 
  • Project Management: Ability to manage projects from start to finish efficiently. 
  • Collaboration: Experience working with cross-functional teams. 
  • Continuous Improvement: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.   
  • Attention to Detail: To ensure quality and compliance. 
  • Innovation: Creative thinking to introduce new manufacturing solutions. 
  • Leadership: Ability to train and guide production staff. 
  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols. 
Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Industrial or Mechanical engineering highly preferred. 
  • Comprehensive understanding of machine tool operations.
  • In-depth knowledge of CNC Programming, CAD / CAM / CAE, MS Office Software, and MS Project.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and carry out root cause analysis.
  • Ability to communicate at all levels internally, customers and suppliers.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Techniques and ability to create standard work.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • Proficient in gear or helical grinding.
  • Understanding of rotary screw compressors and/or centrifugal compressors.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Onsite with up to 15% travel.

The Manufacturing Engineer is tasked with designing and refining manufacturing methods to boost productivity while maintaining high-quality standards and ensuring safety protocols. They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows. 

Responsibilities:

  • Suggests, evaluates, implements & manages multiple manufacturing projects from beginning to end
  • Evaluates, develops and implements machining processes on current or future assets
  • Implements capital equipment including evaluation, selection, run-offs, and implementation
  • Maintains manufacturing best practices including precision machining, lean manufacturing, and machine tool / tooling technologies
  • Evaluates non-conforming material and provides proper disposition
  • Leads special projects including NPD, insourcing, productivity and capital procurement
  • Designs tooling, gages and fixtures using 3D modeling software
  • Develops manufacturing routings internal and sub-con operations
  • Leads machine tool installations throughout the entire process
  • Supports production efforts through troubleshooting manufacturing issues
  • Ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards
  • Supports safety and environmental practices
  • Performs other duties assigned by immediate supervisor
Requirements: 

  • 4+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering.
  • Strong analytical ability to solve issues such as manufacturing problems and dimensional or calculation errors.
  • 1+ years of experience using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • 1+ years of experience in advanced engineering drawings including GD&T and tolerance analysis.
Core Competencies:

  • Technical Expertise: knowledge of manufacturing processes and technologies. 
  • Solid understanding of electro-mechanical assembly and machining processes and overall business operations.
  • Problem-Solving: Analytical skills to develop effective solutions. 
  • Project Management: Ability to manage projects from start to finish efficiently. 
  • Collaboration: Experience working with cross-functional teams. 
  • Continuous Improvement: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.   
  • Attention to Detail: To ensure quality and compliance. 
  • Innovation: Creative thinking to introduce new manufacturing solutions. 
  • Leadership: Ability to train and guide production staff. 
  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols. 
Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Industrial or Mechanical engineering highly preferred. 
  • Comprehensive understanding of machine tool operations.
  • In-depth knowledge of CNC Programming, CAD / CAM / CAE, MS Office Software, and MS Project.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and carry out root cause analysis.
  • Ability to communicate at all levels internally, customers and suppliers.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Techniques and ability to create standard work.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • Proficient in gear or helical grinding.
  • Understanding of rotary screw compressors and/or centrifugal compressors.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Onsite with up to 15% travel.

Job Overview
The Advanced Manufacturing Engineer will support the development and execution of manufacturing strategies by optimizing production capabilities, implementing new technologies, and improving operational efficiency. This onsite role partners closely with cross-functional teams to drive manufacturing readiness, support new product introductions, manage capital investments, and deliver scalable, cost-effective production solutions. The position plays a key role in advancing site technology roadmaps, improving productivity, and ensuring successful implementation of complex manufacturing projects.


Responsibilities:

  • Develop technology road map for manufacturing location to maximize machine utilization and productivity while minimizing cost.
  • Assist in Make vs Buy decision on product introduction, i2v, and footprint plans with the goal of fixed overhead rationalization and leverage of core competencies.
  • Provide technical input on capital expense needs tied to manufacturing startup of project future state and processes.
  • Lead manufacturing project development and implementation activities through IRPX program gates.
  • Procure tooling, machines, and equipment necessary to support approved site capacity and capability roadmap and deliver capable and well documented manufacturing processes.
  • Ensure operator and maintenance training for new production equipment meets standards and final sign-off requirements.
  • Serve in a highly cross-functional environment with engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, product management, and suppliers to optimize cost competitiveness and manufacturability.
  • Serve as a critical stakeholder of large, complex programs with significant impact to the business.
 

Requirements:

  • Bachelor Degree in Engineering required.
  • 10+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in a similar capital intensive, highly engineered product business.

Preferences:

  • Self-starter capabilities with strong technical and leadership skills.
  • Excellent communication, project management, and analytical skills with the ability to develop and deliver technical information to team members, suppliers, and stakeholders.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position is based at a manufacturing plant that will be their primary focus and will also support specific projects at other plants that may not have a full time AME.
  • May require travel 10-25%.

Job Title: Centrifugal Service Technician 

Location: Dallas, TX; San Antonio, TX; Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ; Las Vegas, NV; Tulsa, OK; and Edmond, OK

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
     

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 5 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range 
The pay range for this role is $35.00-$65.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.
