Job Title: QA Technician 

Location: Monroe, LA


About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  


Job Overview:
This role will be responsible for providing quality support through knowledge of inspection procedures and tools, and ability to troubleshoot within in a manufacturing facility. A Quality Technician works with a team to ensure all products meet established quality standards. The ideal candidate is adaptable, a team player, a great communicator, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

 

Responsibilities: 

  • Operate CMMs and precision measurement tools, including micrometers, calipers, thread gauges, and comparators.
  • Interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and GD&T requirements to ensure product compliance.
  • Perform inspections including PPAP, FAI, in-process, floor-sample, and vendor-part inspections.
  • Conduct process audits, identify defects/nonconformances, document findings, and enter data into ERP systems.
  • Maintain accurate quality records, inspection reports, calibration documentation, and ISO-related records.
  • Ensure measurement equipment is calibrated, maintained, and traceable; support investigations involving measurement issues.
  • Collaborate with quality and production teams on workflow improvements, root-cause analysis, NCMs, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Follow ISO, EHS, PPE, safety, 5S, and workplace procedures while maintaining a clean, organized, and compliant work area.

 

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED)
  • 2+ years’ experience in quality experience

Preference: 
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Ability to read and understand the bill of materials and work order instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials, Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel)

Core Competencies

  • Communication
  • Efficiency
  • Productivity
  • Accuracy
  • Teamwork
  • Integrity

Title: Manufacturing Technician, Field Services
Location: Sedalia, MO (Hybrid)
 
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview: 
Build it. Prove it. Start it up. On the floor and in the field, this isn’t a stay-in-one-place technician role. As our Manufacturing Systems Technician, you’ll operate in two worlds—splitting your time between hands-on fabrication in our Sedalia facility (~70%) and field support (~20–30%). From cutting and assembling PVC/CPVC systems (with some stainless in the mix), this is precision, hands-on work where what you build is exactly what ships—no separation between effort and outcome. The other 20–30% of the time, you’re on-site, in front of the customer, watching your system come to life.

You’ll verify installations, run wet and leak testing, and troubleshoot in real time—making the call when something’s off and fixing it before it slows the project down. When things don’t go to plan—and sometimes they won’t—you’re the one who figures it out and keeps everything moving. We’re not standing still either. We’re expanding and actively scaling, with a strong pipeline of projects already lined up. You won’t be stepping into maintenance mode—you’ll be stepping into build mode, where your impact is visible from day one. If you read mechanical drawings, system layouts, without hesitation, work confidently in fabrication, and communicate clearly when it matters—especially under pressure—you’ll do well here. More importantly, this is for someone who takes ownership when the system is live, not just when it’s on paper.  

Bottom line: This role is built for someone who wants to go beyond building parts—someone who takes pride in building complete systems and seeing them through to successful startup and real-world performance.

Responsibilities
  • Operate fabrication equipment including saws, drills, routers, CNC machines, and injection molding equipment to cut, drill, and assemble PVC/CPVC components.
  • Measure, fit, and assemble parts according to shop drawings, blueprints, and work orders.
  • Perform machine setups, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting to support efficient production operations.
  • Conduct quality inspections to ensure products meet company standards and specifications.
  • Maintain accurate production records and report material usage, equipment issues, or production concerns.
  • Collaborate with team members to meet daily production goals, schedules, and deadlines.
  • Load and unload shipments, pick and pack orders, and assist with inventory management activities.
  • Support field installations and system startups for aeration equipment, including inspections and functional verification.
  • Assist with troubleshooting and communicate effectively with contractors, supervisors, and engineering teams during startup activities.
  • Follow all workplace safety procedures while maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work environment.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, field experience with equipment installation, startup, troubleshooting.
  • 1+ years experience reading drawings, blue prints, basic system layouts

Core Competencies 
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings, blueprints, and system layouts with strong mechanical aptitude and experience using hand tools, power tools, and production equipment.
  • Commitment to quality workmanship with strong attention to detail and adherence to production and inspection standards.
  • Strong problem-solving and time management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and resolve issues efficiently.
  • Proficient computer and communication skills for documentation, reporting, production tracking, and collaboration across teams.
  • Adaptable, dependable, and eager to learn new skills while supporting evolving production and field operations.

Preferences: 
  • Experience in pipe fabrication, plumbing, aeration systems, or plastics manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with PVC solvent welding, mechanical fittings, or aeration diffuser systems.
  • OSHA 10/30 safety training.

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • Based at our site in Sedalia, MO
  • National Field Travel up to 30% 
  • Travel expenses covered to include company Vehicle use

Job Summary:
The GCMS Laboratory Technician plays a critical role in the accurate, timely, and reliable analysis of compressed air and gas samples using GC-MS technologies. This position is responsible for executing quantitative chemical analyses, verifying, maintaining, and troubleshooting laboratory instrumentation, and ensuring full compliance with ISO 17025 quality standards. The technician collaborates closely with cross Functional laboratory teams to support daily operations, uphold data integrity, and contribute to the continuous improvement of laboratory processes. This role requires strong technical expertise, disciplined adherence to SOPs, and a commitment to delivering high-quality results in a fast paced, production focused laboratory environment.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform daily hands-on operations in the GC-MS lab, including building calibration curves, sample prep and loading, and parts and consumables inventory management
  • Plan and execute instrument maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair in a high-volume production environment
  • Coordinate effectively with other laboratory teams to ensure timely and accurate completion of testing and reporting of results
  • Identify deviations, investigate root causes, and effectively communicate any analysis issues that may affect the integrity of results
  • Adhere strictly to standard operating procedures and quality control requirements
  • Design method improvements and validate new processes, software, and equipment
  • Maintain a clean, safe, and audit-ready work environment
  • Other related duties as assigned


Basic Qualifications:

  • B.S. degree in Chemistry or Biochemistry
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience performing GC-MS maintenance, troubleshooting, and operational support


Key Competencies:

  • Working knowledge of statistical principles and data evaluation methods used in analytical chemistry
  • Strong technical communication skills, including the ability to document findings and convey complex information clearly
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives


Preferences: 

  • Experience with GC-MS for both gas and liquid phase analyses and chemical extraction techniques
  • Proficiency with chromatographic data systems (ChemStation, Open Lab)
  • 5 years’ experience in an ISO 17025 regulated commercial laboratory
  • Experience working in high-volume, production-focused laboratories with strict turnarounds times
  • Familiarity with root cause analysis tools (fishbone diagrams, 5 whys)


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be based at our site in Austin, TX no travel.

Job Title: Supply Chain Specialist

Location: GXA – On-site at GXA Location; Fairburn, GA
 
About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Summary
The Supply Chain Specialist is responsible for supporting inventory accuracy, logistics operations, and supply chain execution within our third-party logistics (3PL) network. This role works closely with internal stakeholders, suppliers, and logistics providers to ensure efficient material flow, inventory integrity, and compliance with established business controls.
The Supply Chain Specialist will coordinate inventory processes including cycle counting, physical inventories, inventory classification maintenance, discrepancy resolution, and inventory reporting. This position will also support continuous improvement initiatives designed to enhance operational efficiency, improve inventory accuracy, reduce costs, and support customer satisfaction.
 
Responsibilities
  • Monitor and support third-party logistics (3PL) provider performance by reviewing service levels, inventory accuracy metrics, and adherence to established operational requirements.
  • Analyze inventory data and prepare reports on inventory levels, inventory turns, shortages, excess inventory, and other key performance indicators.
  • Investigate and resolve inbound receiving discrepancies by working with suppliers, warehouse personnel, and internal stakeholders to ensure timely correction of errors.
  • Coordinate and support cycle count activities, including schedule adherence, variance investigation, and inventory record reconciliation and annual Physical Inventory activities to ensure accurate inventory documentation.
  • Maintain and update ABC/XYZ inventory classifications to support effective inventory planning and management strategies.
  • Partner with procurement, planning, operations, and customer service teams to optimize inventory availability while minimizing excess stock and shortages.
  • Ensure inventory transactions are processed in accordance with SOX requirements, company policies, and Accounting Limitation of Authority (LOA) guidelines.
  • Support inventory-related audits by gathering documentation, validating inventory records, and assisting with corrective action implementation.
  • Participate in continuous improvement projects focused on inventory accuracy, warehouse efficiency, material flow, and process standardization.
  • Conduct root cause analysis on inventory discrepancies and implement corrective actions to improve inventory performance.
  • Collaborate with customer service and warehouse operations to resolve inventory-related issues, including stockouts, shipping discrepancies, and material availability concerns.
  • Support Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to reduce waste and improve operational performance.
  • Assist with returns processing and inventory disposition activities, ensuring accurate inventory adjustments and proper documentation.
  • Coordinate activities associated with obsolete and excess inventory, including identification, reporting, and disposition recommendations.

Requirements:
  • 2+ years of experience in logistics, supply chain, inventory control, warehouse operations, materials planning, or related disciplines.
  • 1+ years of experience working with ERP systems, preferably Oracle R12.

Core Competencies
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
  • Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong organizational and follow-through skills.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate across functions and build productive working relationships.
  • Self-motivated and proactive with a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Knowledge of inventory management principles and supply chain processes.
  • Proficiency in ERP systems and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Experience supporting process improvement initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies preferred.
  • Ability to identify trends, analyze data, and recommend practical solutions to improve operational performance.
  • Ability to learn Oracle navigation to resolve supplier AP and invoicing issues
  • Ability to learn Oracle navigation to assist Warehouse management with priority shipments

Preference: 
 
  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Business Administration, Operations Management, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and data analysis tools.
  • Experience utilizing reporting and analytics tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Alteryx, KNIME, SQL, or similar systems is preferred.
  • Knowledge of inventory control practices, cycle counting, physical inventory processes, and warehouse operations.
  • APICS CPIM, CSCP, or related certification is preferred.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully onsite based

We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview: 
Build it. Prove it. Start it up. On the floor and in the field, this isn’t a stay-in-one-place technician role. As our Manufacturing Systems Technician, you’ll operate in two worlds—splitting your time between hands-on fabrication in our Sedalia facility (~70%) and field support (~20–30%). From cutting and assembling PVC/CPVC systems (with some stainless in the mix), this is precision, hands-on work where what you build is exactly what ships—no separation between effort and outcome. The other 20–30% of the time, you’re on-site, in front of the customer, watching your system come to life.

You’ll verify installations, run wet and leak testing, and troubleshoot in real time—making the call when something’s off and fixing it before it slows the project down. When things don’t go to plan—and sometimes they won’t—you’re the one who figures it out and keeps everything moving. We’re not standing still either. We’re expanding and actively scaling, with a strong pipeline of projects already lined up. You won’t be stepping into maintenance mode—you’ll be stepping into build mode, where your impact is visible from day one. If you read mechanical drawings, system layouts, without hesitation, work confidently in fabrication, and communicate clearly when it matters—especially under pressure—you’ll do well here. More importantly, this is for someone who takes ownership when the system is live, not just when it’s on paper.  

Bottom line: This role is built for someone who wants to go beyond building parts—someone who takes pride in building complete systems and seeing them through to successful startup and real-world performance.

Responsibilities
  • Operate fabrication equipment including saws, drills, routers, CNC machines, and injection molding equipment to cut, drill, and assemble PVC/CPVC components.
  • Measure, fit, and assemble parts according to shop drawings, blueprints, and work orders.
  • Perform machine setups, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting to support efficient production operations.
  • Conduct quality inspections to ensure products meet company standards and specifications.
  • Maintain accurate production records and report material usage, equipment issues, or production concerns.
  • Collaborate with team members to meet daily production goals, schedules, and deadlines.
  • Load and unload shipments, pick and pack orders, and assist with inventory management activities.
  • Support field installations and system startups for aeration equipment, including inspections and functional verification.
  • Assist with troubleshooting and communicate effectively with contractors, supervisors, and engineering teams during startup activities.
  • Follow all workplace safety procedures while maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work environment.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, field experience with equipment installation, startup, troubleshooting.
  • 1+ years experience reading drawings, blue prints, basic system layouts

Core Competencies 
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings, blueprints, and system layouts with strong mechanical aptitude and experience using hand tools, power tools, and production equipment.
  • Commitment to quality workmanship with strong attention to detail and adherence to production and inspection standards.
  • Strong problem-solving and time management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and resolve issues efficiently.
  • Proficient computer and communication skills for documentation, reporting, production tracking, and collaboration across teams.
  • Adaptable, dependable, and eager to learn new skills while supporting evolving production and field operations.

Preferences: 
  • Experience in pipe fabrication, plumbing, aeration systems, or plastics manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with PVC solvent welding, mechanical fittings, or aeration diffuser systems.
  • OSHA 10/30 safety training.

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • Based at our site in Sedalia, MO
  • National Field Travel up to 30% 
  • Travel expenses covered to include company Vehicle use

They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows. 

Responsibilities:

  • Suggests, evaluates, implements & manages multiple manufacturing projects from beginning to end
  • Evaluates, develops and implements machining processes on current or future assets
  • Implements capital equipment including evaluation, selection, run-offs, and implementation
  • Maintains manufacturing best practices including precision machining, lean manufacturing, and machine tool / tooling technologies
  • Evaluates non-conforming material and provides proper disposition
  • Leads special projects including NPD, insourcing, productivity and capital procurement
  • Designs tooling, gages and fixtures using 3D modeling software
  • Develops manufacturing routings internal and sub-con operations
  • Leads machine tool installations throughout the entire process
  • Supports production efforts through troubleshooting manufacturing issues
  • Ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards
  • Supports safety and environmental practices
  • Performs other duties assigned by immediate supervisor
Requirements: 

  • 4+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering.
  • Strong analytical ability to solve issues such as manufacturing problems and dimensional or calculation errors.
  • 1+ years of experience using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • 1+ years of experience in advanced engineering drawings including GD&T and tolerance analysis.
Core Competencies:

  • Technical Expertise: knowledge of manufacturing processes and technologies. 
  • Solid understanding of electro-mechanical assembly and machining processes and overall business operations.
  • Problem-Solving: Analytical skills to develop effective solutions. 
  • Project Management: Ability to manage projects from start to finish efficiently. 
  • Collaboration: Experience working with cross-functional teams. 
  • Continuous Improvement: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.   
  • Attention to Detail: To ensure quality and compliance. 
  • Innovation: Creative thinking to introduce new manufacturing solutions. 
  • Leadership: Ability to train and guide production staff. 
  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols. 
Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Industrial or Mechanical engineering highly preferred. 
  • Comprehensive understanding of machine tool operations.
  • In-depth knowledge of CNC Programming, CAD / CAM / CAE, MS Office Software, and MS Project.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and carry out root cause analysis.
  • Ability to communicate at all levels internally, customers and suppliers.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Techniques and ability to create standard work.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • Proficient in gear or helical grinding.
  • Understanding of rotary screw compressors and/or centrifugal compressors.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Onsite with up to 15% travel.

  • Knowledge of basic design and manufacturing datum development and its effect in manufacturing processes. 
  • Ability to utilize engineering principles to develop robust manufacturing processes the first time
  • Fluent knowledge of Manufacturing Engineering, Machining, assembly and quality control processes
  • Strong leadership skills to drive engineering principles and processes
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Knowledge of new model launch requirements and processes to ensure flawless launch goals
  • Extensive PC Skills: Excel, Word, Access, Microsoft Project.

  • Demonstrated abilities in tool, fixture and gage design.
  • Demonstrated understanding of inspection tools, techniques and their application to engineering requirements.
  • Must be a self-starter with high initiative and able to work with little supervision.
  • Must work well with others in a team environment supporting operations team.
  • Strong project management skills.
  • Understanding of production control and demand pull systems highly desirable.

Qualifications:

  • BS degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial or Mechanical engineering.
  • 3+ years of experience in the following areas: final assembly and testing,
  • 3+ years of experience with engineering-related software

Core Competencies:

  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to interact with all levels of the organization.
  • Energy and passion for delivering results in a fast-paced, data-driven environment.

job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.





Responsibilities 

•  Partner with global, regional, and business-unit leadership to provide strategic legal advice on commercial priorities, enterprise initiatives, and complex matters. 

•  Lead the drafting, review, negotiation, and management of commercial agreements, including sales, supply, distribution, services, technology, confidentiality, procurement, and other strategic arrangements. 

•  Advise on mergers and acquisitions, investments, integrations, restructurings, and other corporate transactions, coordinating due diligence, documentation, approvals, and post-close legal activities as needed. 

•  Provide guidance on corporate governance, entity management, board and secretarial matters, intercompany arrangements, delegations of authority, and related enterprise requirements. 

•  Monitor legal and regulatory developments across relevant jurisdictions and partner with Compliance, Finance, Tax, Human Resources, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Trade Compliance, Supply Chain, and other functions to translate requirements into practical business actions. 

•  Manage litigation, investigations, claims, and external legal inquiries, including the selection, direction, budgeting, and performance management of outside counsel. 

•  Develop and improve legal templates, playbooks, policies, training, and operating processes that increase consistency, cycle time, risk visibility, knowledge sharing, and compliance across the enterprise. 

•  Build strong relationships across the global Legal team and broader organization, sharing expertise, supporting regional colleagues, and contributing to enterprise-wide legal priorities and continuous improvement initiatives. 

Requirements 

•  J.D. degree and license to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction. 

•  Demonstrated expertise in commercial and contract law, including significant experience drafting and negotiating complex commercial agreements. 

•  Broad legal capability across corporate, transactional, regulatory, compliance, governance, privacy, dispute, and risk-management matters, with the judgment to engage specialist counsel when appropriate. 

•  Exceptional written communication, legal drafting, negotiation, and executive advisory skills. 

•  Proven ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, influence across cultures and functions, and deliver pragmatic solutions in a fast-paced global organization. 

Core Competencies 

Ownership Mindset: Takes accountability, follows through, and acts in the best interests of the enterprise. 

Global Perspective: Works effectively across cultures, jurisdictions, functions, and business models. 

Commercial Judgment: Balances legal risk with practical, customer-focused business solutions. 

Integrity and Courage: Applies sound judgment, protects trust, and raises concerns constructively. 

Collaboration and Influence: Builds durable relationships and aligns stakeholders without relying on authority. 

Execution Excellence: Brings discipline, responsiveness, and clarity to complex, high-priority work. 

Preferences 

•  Experience in an in-house legal department supporting a global industrial, manufacturing, technology, or other complex matrixed organization. 

•  Experience advising senior leaders and boards on corporate governance, compliance, and enterprise risk matters globally.  

•  Experience supporting mergers and acquisitions, integration, or other strategic corporate transactions across multiple jurisdictions. 

  • Experience in Life Sciences businesses including understanding of FDA and related regulations for medical equipment

Job Title: Associate Product Manager

Location: Remote – USA 

About Us:

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:

The Associate Product Manager will support and increasingly own the development and execution of growth strategies for the Positive Displacement Blower portfolio, with a strong emphasis on blower packages, packaged systems, and configured solutions. This role serves as a key member of the Product Management team and is designed as a development path toward full Product Manager responsibility, including ownership of package strategy, commercial performance, product requirements, lifecycle decisions, and cross-functional execution. The position will focus on pricing strategy, market share growth, competitive positioning, new product development, and product portfolio optimization while partnering closely with Sales, Engineering, Operations, Marketing, and Finance.

Responsibilities:

  • Own product strategy and portfolio performance by supporting strategic plans, roadmaps, lifecycle management, revenue growth, profitability, and market share objectives.
  • Serve as the product owner for assigned blower packages, managing product families, configurations, options, accessories, requirements, documentation, positioning, and differentiation.
  • Drive pricing and profitability improvements through pricing analysis, margin management, discount/concession reviews, competitive benchmarking, and collaboration with Sales and Finance.
  • Strengthen market and competitive positioning by tracking market share, customer needs, industry trends, competitor products/pricing, and identifying growth opportunities.
  • Support new product development and innovation from concept through commercialization, including business cases, customer research, requirements, launch readiness, sales enablement, and post-launch performance.
  • Enable commercial excellence by partnering with Sales, supporting customer visits and voice-of-customer activities, developing value propositions and sales tools, and providing product and competitive training.
  • Use business analytics to guide decisions by monitoring bookings, revenue, profitability, win rates, market share, forecasts, and product performance through dashboards and management reporting.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives and continuous improvement across Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Marketing, Finance, and Sales, including cost reduction, value engineering, productivity, and customer-experience improvements.

Requirements:

Title: Manufacturing Technician, Field Services,
Location: Sedalia, MO (Hybrid)
 
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview: 
Build it. Prove it. Start it up. On the floor and in the field, this isn’t a stay-in-one-place technician role. As our Manufacturing Systems Technician, you’ll operate in two worlds—splitting your time between hands-on fabrication in our Sedalia facility (~70%) and field support (~20–30%). From cutting and assembling PVC/CPVC systems (with some stainless in the mix), this is precision, hands-on work where what you build is exactly what ships—no separation between effort and outcome. The other 20–30% of the time, you’re on-site, in front of the customer, watching your system come to life.

You’ll verify installations, run wet and leak testing, and troubleshoot in real time—making the call when something’s off and fixing it before it slows the project down. When things don’t go to plan—and sometimes they won’t—you’re the one who figures it out and keeps everything moving. We’re not standing still either. We’re expanding and actively scaling, with a strong pipeline of projects already lined up. You won’t be stepping into maintenance mode—you’ll be stepping into build mode, where your impact is visible from day one. If you read mechanical drawings, system layouts, without hesitation, work confidently in fabrication, and communicate clearly when it matters—especially under pressure—you’ll do well here. More importantly, this is for someone who takes ownership when the system is live, not just when it’s on paper.  

Bottom line: This role is built for someone who wants to go beyond building parts—someone who takes pride in building complete systems and seeing them through to successful startup and real-world performance.

Responsibilities
  • Operate fabrication equipment including saws, drills, routers, CNC machines, and injection molding equipment to cut, drill, and assemble PVC/CPVC components.
  • Measure, fit, and assemble parts according to shop drawings, blueprints, and work orders.
  • Perform machine setups, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting to support efficient production operations.
  • Conduct quality inspections to ensure products meet company standards and specifications.
  • Maintain accurate production records and report material usage, equipment issues, or production concerns.
  • Collaborate with team members to meet daily production goals, schedules, and deadlines.
  • Load and unload shipments, pick and pack orders, and assist with inventory management activities.
  • Support field installations and system startups for aeration equipment, including inspections and functional verification.
  • Assist with troubleshooting and communicate effectively with contractors, supervisors, and engineering teams during startup activities.
  • Follow all workplace safety procedures while maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work environment.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, field experience with equipment installation, startup, troubleshooting.
  • 1+ years experience reading drawings, blue prints, basic system layouts

Core Competencies 
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings, blueprints, and system layouts with strong mechanical aptitude and experience using hand tools, power tools, and production equipment.
  • Commitment to quality workmanship with strong attention to detail and adherence to production and inspection standards.
  • Strong problem-solving and time management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and resolve issues efficiently.
  • Proficient computer and communication skills for documentation, reporting, production tracking, and collaboration across teams.
  • Adaptable, dependable, and eager to learn new skills while supporting evolving production and field operations.

Preferences: 
  • Experience in pipe fabrication, plumbing, aeration systems, or plastics manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with PVC solvent welding, mechanical fittings, or aeration diffuser systems.
  • OSHA 10/30 safety training.

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • Based at our site in Sedalia, MO
  • National Field Travel up to 30% 
  • Travel expenses covered to include company Vehicle use

Responsibilities:  

  • Designs and coordinates standard manufacturing processes.
  • Plans or improves production methods including flow, tooling, assembly methods and production equipment.
  • Estimates production times and optimum staffing for production schedules.
  • Determines the development or purchase of capital equipment.
  • Interacts with design, manufacturing and suppliers.
  • Creates production processes and documents through routings, bills of materials and standard work.
  • Assists internal and external suppliers with process problems and troubleshoots to find root cause.
  • Oversee fixture design and manufacture.      
  • Ensures final process is capable and stable. 
  • Evaluates non-confirming parts and provides proper disposition.
  • Leads and participates in Lean Manufacturing improvement events using all available tools and techniques.
  • Implement cost reduction ideas.
  • Ensures safety designed into all processes and implements safety corrective actions required to eliminate safety risks
  • Project management.
  • Develop, test, modify, and create solutions to technical problems. 
  • Directing and coordinating production, operations, quality assurance, testing, or maintenance processes
  • Creating project specifications and detailed plans.

Core Competences:
  • Ability to quickly determine root cause utilizing 8D’s and 5 -Why tools. 
  • Ability to quickly assess manufacturing issues related to design and tolerancing
  • Knowledge of basic design and manufacturing datum development and its effect in manufacturing processes. 
  • Ability to utilize engineering principles to develop robust manufacturing processes the first time
  • Fluent knowledge of Manufacturing Engineering, Machining, assembly and quality control processes
  • Strong leadership skills to drive engineering principles and processes
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Knowledge of new model launch requirements and processes to ensure flawless launch goals
  • Extensive PC Skills: Excel, Word, Access, Microsoft Project.
  • Ability to resolve multiple conflicts between widely varying personalities.
  • Requires cross functional communication, simultaneous engineering and reporting
  • Demonstrated abilities in tool, fixture and gage design.
  • Demonstrated understanding of inspection tools, techniques and their application to engineering requirements.
  • Must be a self-starter with high initiative and able to work with little supervision.
  • Must work well with others in a team environment supporting operations team.
  • Strong project management skills.
  • Understanding of production control and demand pull systems highly desirable.

Qualifications:

  • BS degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial or Mechanical engineering.
  • 3+ years of experience in the following areas: final assembly and testing,
  • 3+ years of experience with engineering-related software

Core Competencies:

  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to interact with all levels of the organization.
  • Energy and passion for delivering results in a fast-paced, data-driven environment.
  • Strong attention to detail

The Advanced Manufacturing Engineer will support the development and execution of manufacturing strategies by optimizing production capabilities, implementing new technologies, and improving operational efficiency. Responsibilities:

  • Develop technology road map for manufacturing location to maximize machine utilization and productivity while minimizing cost.
  • Assist in Make vs Buy decision on product introduction, i2v, and footprint plans with the goal of fixed overhead rationalization and leverage of core competencies.
  • Provide technical input on capital expense needs tied to manufacturing startup of project future state and processes.
  • Lead manufacturing project development and implementation activities through IRPX program gates.
  • Procure tooling, machines, and equipment necessary to support approved site capacity and capability roadmap and deliver capable and well documented manufacturing processes.
  • Ensure operator and maintenance training for new production equipment meets standards and final sign-off requirements.
  • Serve in a highly cross-functional environment with engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, product management, and suppliers to optimize cost competitiveness and manufacturability.
  • Serve as a critical stakeholder of large, complex programs with significant impact to the business.
 

Requirements:

  • Bachelor Degree in Engineering required.
  • 10+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in a similar capital intensive, highly engineered product business.

Preferences:

  • Self-starter capabilities with strong technical and leadership skills.
  • Excellent communication, project management, and analytical skills with the ability to develop and deliver technical information to team members, suppliers, and stakeholders.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position is based at a manufacturing plant that will be their primary focus and will also support specific projects at other plants that may not have a full time AME.

job.description:

Job Title: Global Product Manager, Advance Dispense and Piston Pumps            
Location:  Remote (NC or USA Eastcoast) 
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Help Build What’s Next in Industrial Automation.  ARO Fluid Management, a premier global industrial brand within Ingersoll Rand, is ready to take advanced dispense to the next level—and we’re looking for the product leader who can help define where we go next.

The Global Product Manager, Advanced Dispense and Piston Pumps will lead a proven portfolio while accelerating one of the business’s biggest growth opportunities: two-component (2K) dispensing applications.  This is more than a traditional product-management role. The opportunity is to take ARO’s proven piston-pump technology and help transform it into scalable, repeatable advanced-dispense solutions that move, meter, mix and apply adhesives, sealants, foams, coatings, lubricants and other critical materials with precision. These solutions support automotive assembly, battery production, solar manufacturing, marine, coatings, lubrication and automated manufacturing—including applications that may not even be on the roadmap yet.

As Global Product Manager, you’ll define and execute the full portfolio strategy and lifecycle, with a strong focus on finding new applications, customers, markets, channels and system opportunities. You’ll work closely with customers to understand how they manufacture, uncover unmet needs, translate the voice of the customer and market into clear product requirements, and partner with Engineering to turn opportunities into scalable products, systems and services.  Serving as the global connector across Sales, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Marketing, Service, regional teams and customers, you’ll shape product roadmaps, lead new-product development and gate reviews, analyze global market and business data, and develop the application stories and commercial tools that help sales teams win.  You’ll also ensure the portfolio remains competitive, profitable and aligned with evolving customer applications, market needs and industrial standards. As an individual contributor with significant global influence, success will depend on your ability to build alignment across functions, influence without authority and turn strategy into action.

We’re looking for a product leader who is curious, commercially minded, technically credible and growth-oriented—someone willing to step into an unfamiliar application, ask the right questions, engage customers and technical experts, test assumptions, learn quickly and challenge the status quo.  With Advanced Dispense positioned as a significant strategic growth area for ARO, this highly visible role offers the opportunity to partner closely with business leadership and help shape the next generation of industrial fluid handling and automation.

If you share our passion for inspiring progress—for bringing about bold shifts in how people, economies and societies operate—then you belong with Ingersoll Rand. Progress begins with you.

Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Roadmap:
  • Develop and maintain strategic product roadmaps for Piston Pumps and Advanced Dispense applicable portfolio in IR.
  • dentify new market and application opportunities.
  • Create an exceptional growth focus by enhancing product portfolio and solution extensions specifically for Advanced Dispense applications.
 
Product Lifecycle Management:
  • Oversee the full lifecycle from ideation through end?of?life decisions.
  • Ensure product quality, reliability, and cost competitiveness.
 
Market, Application, and Competitive Analysis:
  • Conduct market research on Advanced Dispense applications and competitors.
  • Benchmark performance and pricing to guide differentiation.
 
Cross Functional Leadership:
  • Lead cross-functional products, solutions, and service development process.
  • Collaborate with Engineering to define requirements and performance targets.
  • Partner with Operations and Supply Chain to ensure manufacturability and cost efficiency.
 
Commercial & Channel Enablement:
  • Support customers, end-users, distributors, sales teams, internal teams with technical?commercial guidance / expertise.
  • Develop pricing and positioning strategies, structures, sales tools, and product value messaging.
    • Collaborate with marketing on product launches and technical content.
    • Enable sales teams with technical training and competitive messaging.
 
Performance & Profitability Management:
  • Monitor and influence key KPIs such as sales, margin, costs, and market share.
  • Lead cost reduction, SKU optimization, and portfolio performance initiatives.

Requirements
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related technical field. 
  • 5+ years of progressive product management experience, ideally within pumps, pumping systems, fluid handling, automated dispensing, industrial automation, engineered systems, or a related industrial equipment market. 
  • 3+ years of experience developing product roadmaps, managing product lifecycles, and leading new product development or stage-gate initiatives. 
  • 3+ years of experience conducting market, customer, or application discovery and converting identified needs into actionable product or system requirements. 
  • 3+ years of experience leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing stakeholders without direct authority in a matrixed organization. 
  • 3+ years of experience analyzing product, market, customer, and financial data to identify opportunities and support product-strategy decisions. 
  • 2+ years of experience working with globally distributed teams, customers, suppliers, or manufacturing operations.

Core Competencies
  • Global Product Strategy and Lifecycle Management: Ability to develop and execute global product strategies, roadmaps, portfolio priorities, and lifecycle plans that drive sustainable growth.
  • Market Discovery and Customer Insight: Ability to investigate new markets and applications, engage customers and industry experts, identify unmet needs, and translate insights into growth opportunities.
  • Technical-to-Commercial Translation: Ability to convert pump, fluid-handling, dispensing, and application requirements into scalable solutions, compelling value propositions, and effective sales-enablement tools.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership and Influence: Ability to align global Sales, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Marketing, and Service teams and drive execution without direct authority.
  • Data-Driven Business-Case Development: Ability to analyze market, customer, product, competitive, and financial data to prioritize opportunities and build fact-based business cases and investment recommendations.

Preferences:
  • MBA or other relevant advanced degree.
  • Experience with piston pumps, reciprocating pumps, pumping systems, pump design, system components, or industrial fluid-handling equipment.
  • Experience with automated manufacturing applications involving adhesives, sealants, foams, coatings, lubricants, paints, greases, or other industrial fluids.
  • Experience with advanced dispensing, metering, dosing, mixing, or two-component, or 2K, systems.
  • Experience with Qlik, Snowflake, Power BI, Tableau, or comparable business-intelligence and data-analysis platforms.
  • Experience applying artificial intelligence or automation tools to data analysis, product selection, sales enablement, or market research.

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This is a Remote, USA only role based from North Carolina or the Eastern Time zone 
  • Travel Potential is upto 20% to include periodic travel to the Mooresville Solutions Center
 
Pay Range
The pay range for this role, excluding incentive opportunities, is $130,000 - $185,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Title: Manufacturing Technician, Field Services
Location: Sedalia, MO (Hybrid)
 
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview: 
Build it. Prove it. Start it up. On the floor and in the field, this isn’t a stay-in-one-place technician role. As our Manufacturing Systems Technician, you’ll operate in two worlds—splitting your time between hands-on fabrication in our Sedalia facility (~70%) and field support (~20–30%). From cutting and assembling PVC/CPVC systems (with some stainless in the mix), this is precision, hands-on work where what you build is exactly what ships—no separation between effort and outcome. The other 20–30% of the time, you’re on-site, in front of the customer, watching your system come to life.

You’ll verify installations, run wet and leak testing, and troubleshoot in real time—making the call when something’s off and fixing it before it slows the project down. When things don’t go to plan—and sometimes they won’t—you’re the one who figures it out and keeps everything moving. We’re not standing still either. We’re expanding and actively scaling, with a strong pipeline of projects already lined up. You won’t be stepping into maintenance mode—you’ll be stepping into build mode, where your impact is visible from day one. If you read mechanical drawings, system layouts, without hesitation, work confidently in fabrication, and communicate clearly when it matters—especially under pressure—you’ll do well here. More importantly, this is for someone who takes ownership when the system is live, not just when it’s on paper.  

Bottom line: This role is built for someone who wants to go beyond building parts—someone who takes pride in building complete systems and seeing them through to successful startup and real-world performance.

Responsibilities
  • Operate fabrication equipment including saws, drills, routers, CNC machines, and injection molding equipment to cut, drill, and assemble PVC/CPVC components.
  • Measure, fit, and assemble parts according to shop drawings, blueprints, and work orders.
  • Perform machine setups, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting to support efficient production operations.
  • Conduct quality inspections to ensure products meet company standards and specifications.
  • Maintain accurate production records and report material usage, equipment issues, or production concerns.
  • Collaborate with team members to meet daily production goals, schedules, and deadlines.
  • Load and unload shipments, pick and pack orders, and assist with inventory management activities.
  • Support field installations and system startups for aeration equipment, including inspections and functional verification.
  • Assist with troubleshooting and communicate effectively with contractors, supervisors, and engineering teams during startup activities.
  • Follow all workplace safety procedures while maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work environment.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, field experience with equipment installation, startup, troubleshooting.
  • 1+ years experience reading drawings, blue prints, basic system layouts

Core Competencies 
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings, blueprints, and system layouts with strong mechanical aptitude and experience using hand tools, power tools, and production equipment.
  • Commitment to quality workmanship with strong attention to detail and adherence to production and inspection standards.
  • Strong problem-solving and time management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and resolve issues efficiently.
  • Proficient computer and communication skills for documentation, reporting, production tracking, and collaboration across teams.
  • Adaptable, dependable, and eager to learn new skills while supporting evolving production and field operations.

Preferences: 
  • Experience in pipe fabrication, plumbing, aeration systems, or plastics manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with PVC solvent welding, mechanical fittings, or aeration diffuser systems.
  • OSHA 10/30 safety training.

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • Based at our site in Sedalia, MO
  • National Field Travel up to 30% 
  • Travel expenses covered to include company Vehicle use

What We Offer: 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

About Us:

Job Overview:
In this role as a Manufacturing Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of production processes. The Manufacturing Engineer is tasked with designing and refining manufacturing methods to boost productivity while maintaining high-quality standards and ensuring safety protocols. They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows. 

Responsibilities:

  • Suggests, evaluates, implements & manages multiple manufacturing projects from beginning to end
  • Evaluates, develops and implements machining processes on current or future assets
  • Implements capital equipment including evaluation, selection, run-offs, and implementation
  • Maintains manufacturing best practices including precision machining, lean manufacturing, and machine tool / tooling technologies
  • Evaluates non-conforming material and provides proper disposition
  • Leads special projects including NPD, insourcing, productivity and capital procurement
  • Designs tooling, gages and fixtures using 3D modeling software
  • Develops manufacturing routings internal and sub-con operations
  • Leads machine tool installations throughout the entire process
  • Supports production efforts through troubleshooting manufacturing issues
  • Ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards
  • Supports safety and environmental practices
  • Performs other duties assigned by immediate supervisor

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Industrial or Mechanical engineering. 
  • 4+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering.

Core Competencies:

  • Technical Expertise: knowledge of manufacturing processes and technologies. 
  • Problem-Solving: Analytical skills to develop effective solutions. 
  • Project Management: Ability to manage projects from start to finish efficiently. 
  • Collaboration: Experience working with cross-functional teams. 
  • Continuous Improvement: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.   
  • Attention to Detail: To ensure quality and compliance. 
  • Innovation: Creative thinking to introduce new manufacturing solutions. 
  • Leadership: Ability to train and guide production staff. 
  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols. 
  • Strong analytical ability to solve issues such as: manufacturing problems and dimensional or calculation errors.
  • Solid understanding of electro-mechanical assembly and machining processes and overall business operations.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • Comprehensive understanding of machine tool operations.
  • In-depth knowledge of CNC Programming, CAD / CAM / CAE, MS Office Software, and MS Project.
  • Competent in advanced engineering drawings including GD&T and tolerance analysis.

Preferences:

  • Ability to prioritize tasks, and carry out root cause analysis.
  • Ability to communicate at all levels internally, customers and suppliers.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Techniques and ability to create standard work.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • Proficient in gear or helical grinding.
  • Understanding of rotary screw compressors and/or centrifugal compressors.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Onsite with up to 15% travel.

Job Title: Centrifugal Service Technician 

Location: Dallas, TX; San Antonio, TX; Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ; Las Vegas, NV; Tulsa, OK; and Edmond, OK

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
     

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 5 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range 
The pay range for this role is $35.00-$65.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Title: Manufacturing Technician, Field Services,
Location: Sedalia, MO (Hybrid)
 
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview: 
Build it. Prove it. Start it up. On the floor and in the field, this isn’t a stay-in-one-place technician role. As our Manufacturing Systems Technician, you’ll operate in two worlds—splitting your time between hands-on fabrication in our Sedalia facility (~70%) and field support (~20–30%). From cutting and assembling PVC/CPVC systems (with some stainless in the mix), this is precision, hands-on work where what you build is exactly what ships—no separation between effort and outcome. The other 20–30% of the time, you’re on-site, in front of the customer, watching your system come to life.

You’ll verify installations, run wet and leak testing, and troubleshoot in real time—making the call when something’s off and fixing it before it slows the project down. When things don’t go to plan—and sometimes they won’t—you’re the one who figures it out and keeps everything moving. We’re not standing still either. We’re expanding and actively scaling, with a strong pipeline of projects already lined up. You won’t be stepping into maintenance mode—you’ll be stepping into build mode, where your impact is visible from day one. If you read mechanical drawings, system layouts, without hesitation, work confidently in fabrication, and communicate clearly when it matters—especially under pressure—you’ll do well here. More importantly, this is for someone who takes ownership when the system is live, not just when it’s on paper.  

Bottom line: This role is built for someone who wants to go beyond building parts—someone who takes pride in building complete systems and seeing them through to successful startup and real-world performance.

Responsibilities
  • Operate fabrication equipment including saws, drills, routers, CNC machines, and injection molding equipment to cut, drill, and assemble PVC/CPVC components.
  • Measure, fit, and assemble parts according to shop drawings, blueprints, and work orders.
  • Perform machine setups, routine maintenance, and troubleshooting to support efficient production operations.
  • Conduct quality inspections to ensure products meet company standards and specifications.
  • Maintain accurate production records and report material usage, equipment issues, or production concerns.
  • Collaborate with team members to meet daily production goals, schedules, and deadlines.
  • Load and unload shipments, pick and pack orders, and assist with inventory management activities.
  • Support field installations and system startups for aeration equipment, including inspections and functional verification.
  • Assist with troubleshooting and communicate effectively with contractors, supervisors, and engineering teams during startup activities.
  • Follow all workplace safety procedures while maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work environment.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, field experience with equipment installation, startup, troubleshooting.
  • 1+ years experience reading drawings, blue prints, basic system layouts

Core Competencies 
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings, blueprints, and system layouts with strong mechanical aptitude and experience using hand tools, power tools, and production equipment.
  • Commitment to quality workmanship with strong attention to detail and adherence to production and inspection standards.
  • Strong problem-solving and time management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and resolve issues efficiently.
  • Proficient computer and communication skills for documentation, reporting, production tracking, and collaboration across teams.
  • Adaptable, dependable, and eager to learn new skills while supporting evolving production and field operations.

Preferences: 
  • Experience in pipe fabrication, plumbing, aeration systems, or plastics manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with PVC solvent welding, mechanical fittings, or aeration diffuser systems.
  • OSHA 10/30 safety training.

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • Based at our site in Sedalia, MO
  • National Field Travel up to 30% 
  • Travel expenses covered to include company Vehicle use

  • Continuous Improvement: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.

  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols.

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Industrial or Mechanical engineering highly preferred. 
  • Comprehensive understanding of machine tool operations.
  • In-depth knowledge of CNC Programming, CAD / CAM / CAE, MS Office Software, and MS Project.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and carry out root cause analysis.
  • Ability to communicate at all levels internally, customers and suppliers.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Techniques and ability to create standard work.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.

Job Overview:

The Manufacturing Engineer is tasked with designing and refining manufacturing methods to boost productivity while maintaining high-quality standards and ensuring safety protocols. They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows. 

Responsibilities:

  • Suggests, evaluates, implements & manages multiple manufacturing projects from beginning to end
  • Evaluates, develops and implements machining processes on current or future assets
  • Implements capital equipment including evaluation, selection, run-offs, and implementation
  • Maintains manufacturing best practices including precision machining, lean manufacturing, and machine tool / tooling technologies
  • Evaluates non-conforming material and provides proper disposition
  • Leads special projects including NPD, insourcing, productivity and capital procurement
  • Designs tooling, gages and fixtures using 3D modeling software

  • Innovation: Creative thinking to introduce new manufacturing solutions. 
  • Leadership: Ability to train and guide production staff. 
  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols.

Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
     

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 5 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required.

The pay range for this role is $35.00-$65.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Can be located at one of our Compression Systems manufacturing locations in United States


About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup.
