Job Title: Service Technician  
Location: Staunton/Lynchburg/Roanoke, VA area

About Us  

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview

  • The Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Industrial Technologies and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 
     

Responsibilities

  • Ensure the correct installation, maintenance, and field repair of the equipment manufactured and sold by Ingersoll Rand at the purchaser's location. 

  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the field installation and repair requirements of this equipment. 

  • Provide technical advice and be able to train customers, potential customers, field salesmen, and field service trainees.

  • Diagnose problems, recommend corrective action in this unsupervised environment and submit clear, accurate records and/or oral reports to the manufacturing facility. 

  • Maintain a high degree of integrity in handling business affairs.

  • Maintain proper written and oral communication skills to transfer information related to service work in a concise and logical manner. 

  • Submit detailed technical reports on each service call in a legible fashion, suitable for billing customers. 

  • Submit accurate, detailed & timely expense account records along with timecards on a weekly basis. Maintain good financial records and practices to manage company business matters, credit cards, and if required, a company car.

Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems. Experience on compressed air systems/centrifugal technologies/solid controls background is a plus. While not required, those with knowledge in the service, diagnosis, and startup of both rotary and centrifugal air compressors, including dryers, cooling towers, and filtration systems are encouraged to apply. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required. .

Core Competencies 

  • Must possess a mechanic's set of tools; specialty tools will be provided. 

  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years

  • This position requires working in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards. 
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Customer service skills such as conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner. 
  • Mechanical competency to be able to learn, diagnose, and troubleshoot compressor systems and machinery. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Preferences

  • Desired degree program in Electrical/Electronic Technology or HVAC with basic knowledge of some or all of the following: AC/DC circuits, wiring diagrams/schematics, motors/controls, PLCs, HVAC electricity, controls, refrigeration systems and/or refrigerant certification. Military experience and/or sufficient mechanical working experience is a plus. Candidates who possess this knowledge or skills but have not completed a formal program may be considered. 

  • EPA 608 /F-GAS 303/2008/CE/ISHRAE Certification Preferred (Refrigeration experience/certification a plus).

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position may require occasional travel for training. 1-2 times per year for one week at a time. (5-10%). 

  • This position is included in an on-call rotation with other service technicians in the local area to service customer emergencies in the evenings or on weekends. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required during scheduled on-call weeks.

Job title: Quality Engineer

Location: Lincolnshire, IL

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Quality Engineer (QE) ensures that products, manufacturing processes, and Quality Management System (QMS) activities meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role combines technical quality engineering with ownership of key QMS processes, including document control, training, record management, and audit readiness. The QE works cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, and other teams to support New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining operations, ensuring timely execution of validation, risk management, and quality deliverables. The role is also responsible for investigating and resolving nonconformances through CAPA, driving continuous improvement, and supporting the effectiveness of the electronic QMS (e.g., MasterControl) to ensure data integrity and efficient processes.


Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including document control, change management, quality records, electronic QMS (e.g., MasterControl), and training, ensuring compliance with FDA, ISO, and internal requirements.
  • Review and approve change controls; oversee calibration and equipment control programs; and drive continuous improvement of QMS processes and systems.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by ensuring compliance with validation (IQ/OQ/PQ), risk management, statistical analysis, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering to support sustaining manufacturing, change control, equipment maintenance, revalidation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Perform Device History Record (DHR) reviews; lead or support investigations for nonconformances and CAPAs; and drive root cause analysis, corrective actions, and right-first-time improvements.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk assessments and pFMEA, and ensure effective mitigation strategies.
  • Lead and support internal, customer, ISO, and FDA audits; represent Quality in customer and supplier interactions; and support supplier qualification and performance monitoring.
  • Support cross-functional and cross-site quality initiatives, special projects, and foster a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.



Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS) in Engineering, Quality, Life Sciences, or a related technical field
  • 1+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or a similar role within a medical device or regulated manufacturing environment


Preference: 

  • Working knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including document control, training systems, record retention, and audit support
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 requirements
  • Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) such as MasterControl or similar preferred
  • Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including development and revision of SOPs, work instructions, validation documents, and quality records
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Lead Auditor Certification is an advantage


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based, flexible working, hybrid, 50% travel across Europe, etc)


Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $65,000-$80,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

What we Offer

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Job Title: Project Manager

Location: Georgia, Tennessee, South Carolina

 

About Us 

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems. 

 

Job Summary 

  • Ingersoll Rand has a new exciting opportunity to join our organization as Project Manager you will manage all aspects of equipment projects, from beginning to end, with direct responsibility for project execution while leading a team, or teams, to accomplish specific objectives in a given time frame and with available resources. You will also be responsible for the administration, implementation, and management of control projects and accountable for assigned project’s scope of work, schedule, and budget. 

 

Responsibilities 

  • Performs construction plan review to meet customer requirements. Develops, evaluates, and discusses possible equipment solutions with appropriate Account Managers, Suppliers and customers.  

  • Coordinates selection, pricing, & integrates equipment, controls, & services for each project.  

  • Responsible for creating detailed cost estimates. Resolves major deviations from scope w/ team after Project Scope Validation.  

  • Responsible for identifying possible cost saving opportunities &/or risk items that will occur on various projects. Optimizes job costs by negotiating prices w/ vendors/sub-contractors through quotations for materials/services. Plans & analyzes assigned projects, establishes schedules & project parameters & sets procedures to accomplish system objectives, involving complex applications.  

  • Responsible for maintaining the accuracy of the forecasted cost at completion.  

  • Creates & makes revisions to project schedules including: generating tasks, estimates, dependencies; & milestones.  

  • Responsible for the preparation of material & vendor orders; recording the receipt of materials & approving payments.  

  • Responsible for entering equipment orders & issuing purchase orders for vendor orders. Generates work orders for equipment start-ups.  

  • Responsible for project cash-flow management: progress billing, collections support & monitoring, & resource management.  

  • Maintains customer satisfaction by investigating concerns, implementing corrective action, & communicating w/ customers & assigned staff.  

  • Responsible for the successful transition of warranty to the service process 
     

Basic Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, engineering technology or business management with 3-5 years of experience in estimating, engineering or construction management.  

  • Working knowledge of all facets of construction including mechanical, electrical, plumbing systems and knowledge with the operation of HVAC systems, electrical systems and temperature controls.  

  • Knowledge reading and understanding blueprints and construction plans and specifications.  

  • Experience with computer estimating and word processing software programs.  

 

Key Competencies 

  • Exceptional organization, communication (verbal and written), and follow-up skills with the ability to effectively manage a high volume of priorities and commitments with internal and external customers in a highly visible, fast-paced work environment.   

  • Strong interpersonal skills, able to follow standard processes and work autonomously while understanding when to escalate issues that require further review.   

  • Proven ability to collaborate, influence and support change with stakeholders across multiple levels of a global organization. 

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position may require travel: roughly 25%.

About Us

Job Overview

  • The Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Industrial Technologies and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities

  • Ensure the correct installation, maintenance, and field repair of the equipment manufactured and sold by Ingersoll Rand at the purchaser's location. 

  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the field installation and repair requirements of this equipment. 

  • Provide technical advice and be able to train customers, potential customers, field salesmen, and field service trainees.

  • Diagnose problems, recommend corrective action in this unsupervised environment and submit clear, accurate records and/or oral reports to the manufacturing facility. 

  • Maintain a high degree of integrity in handling business affairs.

  • Maintain proper written and oral communication skills to transfer information related to service work in a concise and logical manner. 

  • Submit detailed technical reports on each service call in a legible fashion, suitable for billing customers. 

  • Submit accurate, detailed & timely expense account records along with timecards on a weekly basis. Maintain good financial records and practices to manage company business matters, credit cards, and if required, a company car.

Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems. Experience on compressed air systems/centrifugal technologies/solid controls background is a plus. While not required, those with knowledge in the service, diagnosis, and startup of both rotary and centrifugal air compressors, including dryers, cooling towers, and filtration systems are encouraged to apply. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required. 

Core Competencies 

  • Must possess a mechanic's set of tools; specialty tools will be provided. 

  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years

  • This position requires working in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards. 
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Customer service skills such as conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner. 
  • Mechanical competency to be able to learn, diagnose, and troubleshoot compressor systems and machinery. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 

Preferences

  • Desired degree program in Electrical/Electronic Technology or HVAC with basic knowledge of some or all of the following: AC/DC circuits, wiring diagrams/schematics, motors/controls, PLCs, HVAC electricity, controls, refrigeration systems and/or refrigerant certification. Military experience and/or sufficient mechanical working experience is a plus. Candidates who possess this knowledge or skills but have not completed a formal program may be considered. 

  • EPA 608 /F-GAS 303/2008/CE/ISHRAE Certification Preferred (Refrigeration experience/certification a plus).

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position may require occasional travel for training. 1-2 times per year for one week at a time. (5-10%). 

  • This position is included in an on-call rotation with other service technicians in the local area to service customer emergencies in the evenings or on weekends. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required during scheduled on-call weeks.  

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $25.00-$40.00/hr. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

What we Offer

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. You will also be responsible for the administration, implementation, and management of control projects and accountable for assigned project’s scope of work, schedule, and budget.

  • Coordinates selection, pricing, & integrates equipment, controls, & services for each project.  

  • Responsible for creating detailed cost estimates. Resolves major deviations from scope w/ team after Project Scope Validation.  

  • Responsible for identifying possible cost saving opportunities &/or risk items that will occur on various projects. Optimizes job costs by negotiating prices w/ vendors/sub-contractors through quotations for materials/services. Plans & analyzes assigned projects, establishes schedules & project parameters & sets procedures to accomplish system objectives, involving complex applications.  

  • Responsible for maintaining the accuracy of the forecasted cost at completion.

  • Responsible for the preparation of material & vendor orders; recording the receipt of materials & approving payments.  

  • Responsible for entering equipment orders & issuing purchase orders for vendor orders. Generates work orders for equipment start-ups.  

  • Responsible for project cash-flow management: progress billing, collections support & monitoring, & resource management.  

  • Maintains customer satisfaction by investigating concerns, implementing corrective action, & communicating w/ customers & assigned staff.  

  • Responsible for the successful transition of warranty to the service process 
     

Basic Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, engineering technology or business management with 3-5 years of experience in estimating, engineering or construction management.  

  • Working knowledge of all facets of construction including mechanical, electrical, plumbing systems and knowledge with the operation of HVAC systems, electrical systems and temperature controls.  

  • Knowledge reading and understanding blueprints and construction plans and specifications.  

  • Experience with computer estimating and word processing software programs.  

 

Key Competencies 

  • Exceptional organization, communication (verbal and written), and follow-up skills with the ability to effectively manage a high volume of priorities and commitments with internal and external customers in a highly visible, fast-paced work environment.   

  • Strong interpersonal skills, able to follow standard processes and work autonomously while understanding when to escalate issues that require further review.   

  • Proven ability to collaborate, influence and support change with stakeholders across multiple levels of a global organization.

Job Title: Senior NPD Engineer 

Location: Buffalo, NY

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview

Ingersoll Rand is seeking an experienced NPD Engineer who can thrive inside an interactive and dynamic team where safety, quality, creativity, and continuous improvement are paramount. This role is for a seasoned engineer capable of independently owning complex design deliverables from concept through launch with minimal supervision. The experienced NPD Engineer leads detailed mechanical design, design verification, launch support, and continuous improvement of centrifugal compressor products. Principal responsibilities include translating customer, market, and product requirements into robust mechanical designs, driving engineering definition through CAD/PLM systems, and resolving complex technical problems while collaborating across Manufacturing, Quality, Sourcing, Tendering, and Service teams to deliver reliable, manufacturable, and cost-effective solutions.

Responsibilities:

  • Design ownership: Independently develop and release mechanical designs for centrifugal compressor systems and components, including 3D models, drawings, bills of material, and design documentation.
  • Product development leadership: Own the translation of product requirements into practical, validated design solutions, working directly with Product Management, Manufacturing, Quality, Sourcing, and Service teams and driving decisions to closure.
  • Technical accountability: Take responsibility for mechanical design definition, tolerance analysis, manufacturability, serviceability, and design documentation for new or improved products, applying engineering judgment to trade-offs.
  • Customer interaction: Serve as a technical point of contact for internal and external customers, effectively communicating design intent, technical constraints, trade-offs, and project status to audiences with varying technical backgrounds.
  • Product validation: Build centrifugal compressor prototypes to be used for pre-production testing and verification, implementing any lessons learned during the build into the design.
  • Travel: Ability to travel, including internationally, up to 5%.
Qualifications:

  • Bachelors in Mechanical Engineering
  • 5+ years of related design or product development experience with a strong foundation in mechanical design, machine design, mechanics of materials, manufacturing processes, and/or engineering fundamentals, with a proven track record of delivering released designs.
Preferences:
  • Demonstrated experience with centrifugal compressor components, pressure-containing equipment, rotating equipment, or packaged equipment design is highly desirable.
  • Proficiency with finite element analysis, tolerance analysis, design automation, and/or computer programming is a plus.
  • Hands-on proficiency with CAD and PLM systems (NX and Teamcenter) is strongly preferred.
Core Competencies:

  • Strong working knowledge of computer systems and basic Microsoft Office.
  • Strong command of the English language and the ability to clearly communicate in writing and speech with peers, leadership, and internal/external customers.
  • Ability to quickly understand, condense, and organize complex information to make sound, independent engineering decisions.
  • Self-motivated, responsible, detail-oriented, and personable, with the confidence to own outcomes.
  • Ability to work collaboratively while independently owning significant deliverables and reliably managing stress, change, and pressure with professionalism.
  • Ability to perform critical mental tasks such as decision-making, prioritizing, organizing, and exercising sound judgment to align work with business objectives.
Travel & Work Arrangements / Requirements

  • The location for this position is Buffalo, NY. 4 days onsite, 1 day remote.
Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $85,000-$95,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

  • Maintain a high degree of integrity in handling business affairs.

  • Maintain proper written and oral communication skills to transfer information related to service work in a concise and logical manner. 

  • Submit detailed technical reports on each service call in a legible fashion, suitable for billing customers. 

  • Submit accurate, detailed & timely expense account records along with timecards on a weekly basis. Maintain good financial records and practices to manage company business matters, credit cards, and if required, a company car.

Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems. Experience on compressed air systems/centrifugal technologies/solid controls background is a plus. While not required, those with knowledge in the service, diagnosis, and startup of both rotary and centrifugal air compressors, including dryers, cooling towers, and filtration systems are encouraged to apply. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required. .

Core Competencies 

  • Must possess a mechanic's set of tools; specialty tools will be provided. 

  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years

  • This position requires working in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards. 
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Customer service skills such as conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner. 
  • Mechanical competency to be able to learn, diagnose, and troubleshoot compressor systems and machinery. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Preferences

  • Desired degree program in Electrical/Electronic Technology or HVAC with basic knowledge of some or all of the following: AC/DC circuits, wiring diagrams/schematics, motors/controls, PLCs, HVAC electricity, controls, refrigeration systems and/or refrigerant certification. Military experience and/or sufficient mechanical working experience is a plus. Candidates who possess this knowledge or skills but have not completed a formal program may be considered. 

  • EPA 608 /F-GAS 303/2008/CE/ISHRAE Certification Preferred (Refrigeration experience/certification a plus).

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position may require occasional travel for training. 1-2 times per year for one week at a time. (5-10%). 

  • This position is included in an on-call rotation with other service technicians in the local area to service customer emergencies in the evenings or on weekends. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required during scheduled on-call weeks.

Job Title:  Field Service Technician
Location: Blandon, PA  (Hybrid with travel)

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview:
Excelsior Blower Systems, a proud Ingersoll Rand brand, has been a powerhouse in engineered air solutions delivering decades of proven performance, reliability, and innovation. Backed by a legacy of excellence, we’re trusted across industries for systems that perform under pressure and consistently exceed expectations.  We’re looking for a hands-on Field Service Technician who thrives in the field and takes pride in keeping critical equipment running at peak performance. In this role, you’ll be the expert customers rely on—installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing Ingersoll Rand positive displacement (PD) blower systems, including controls and VFDs, directly at customer sites. You’ll play a vital role in delivering responsive, high-impact service that supports customers’ operational needs.  
Your work won’t stop in the field. You’ll also install controls and wiring for PD blower systems at our facility, applying your electromechanical expertise across the full equipment lifecycle. If you already bring PD blower experience, you’ll hit the ground running. If not, you bring a strong foundation in rotating equipment, motor and electrical troubleshooting, alignment, system-level diagnostics, and reading schematics and P&IDs—and the drive to master the rest. This is a role for someone who enjoys solving real-world problems, working independently, and making a visible impact every day. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Install, commission, and start up positive displacement (PD) blower packages, vacuum/pressure systems, and associated rotating equipment per OEM specifications and site requirements.

  • Configure, program, and troubleshoot variable frequency drives (VFDs) and soft starters (parameter setup, PID loops, accel/decel profiles, motor protection, fieldbus/communication interfaces such as Modbus/TCP, EtherNet/IP).

  • Diagnose and repair electrical controls including relays, contactors, motor starters, overloads, interlocks, safety circuits, and control transformers.

  • Perform control panel wiring and field terminations (24 VDC control, 120/480 VAC power, grounding/bonding, signal wiring, shielded cable practices); read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and P&IDs.

  • Install and integrate instrumentation (pressure, temperature, vibration, flow, differential pressure transmitters, proximity sensors, limit switches) and calibrate as required.

  • Execute mechanical service tasks (coupling alignment—laser or dial, belt tensioning, blower timing, bearing replacement, seal changes, lubrication, fastener torque verification).

  • Conduct vibration and performance checks; identify root cause of abnormal noise, heat, vibration, or amperage draw (airflow restrictions, leaks, misalignment, cavitation, resonance).

  • Troubleshoot system issues end-to-end across electrical, mechanical, and controls, including motor diagnostics (insulation resistance, megger testing, continuity), VFD/motor matching, and load-related faults.

  • Perform field measurements and documentation (voltage/current, phase balance, harmonics, airflow/pressure, vibration readings) and produce detailed service reports with parts lists and recommended follow-up.

Requirements:

  • High School diploma or GED
  • 5+ years of relevant / equivalent technical experience: millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service.
  • 2+ years of electromechanical experience
Core Competencies

  • Strong electromechanical troubleshooting skills, including rotating equipment such as motors, gearboxes, compressors, mixers, blowers, and pumps; electronic power conversion (AC to DC) and related faults/alarms (GF, OC, OV, UV, OL, OH); and PLC troubleshooting, including I/O, hardware, and software checks.
  • Clear and concise verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, employees, and Sales Representatives.
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot issues, resolve conflicts, make sound decisions, and appropriately escalate problems in dynamic environments.
  • Strong organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills with the ability to meet deadlines and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Valid driver’s license held for at least 12 months with a satisfactory driving record. No major or frequent violations, including DUI within the past 5 years, hit-and-run, license suspension, reckless/careless driving, or multiple minor violations/preventable collisions within the past 3 years.
Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is 40% onsite shop repairs and up to 60% travel for field work
  • Possible minimal travel to Canada, Puerto Rico, and/or Mexico
  • Paid travel time at full hourly rate
  • Company vehicle and gas provided

Location: Buffalo, NY

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview

Ingersoll Rand is seeking an experienced NPD Engineer who can thrive inside an interactive and dynamic team where safety, quality, creativity, and continuous improvement are paramount. This role is for a seasoned engineer capable of independently owning complex design deliverables from concept through launch with minimal supervision. The experienced NPD Engineer leads detailed mechanical design, design verification, launch support, and continuous improvement of centrifugal compressor products. Principal responsibilities include translating customer, market, and product requirements into robust mechanical designs, driving engineering definition through CAD/PLM systems, and resolving complex technical problems while collaborating across Manufacturing, Quality, Sourcing, Tendering, and Service teams to deliver reliable, manufacturable, and cost-effective solutions.

Responsibilities:

  • Design ownership: Independently develop and release mechanical designs for centrifugal compressor systems and components, including 3D models, drawings, bills of material, and design documentation.
  • Product development leadership: Own the translation of product requirements into practical, validated design solutions, working directly with Product Management, Manufacturing, Quality, Sourcing, and Service teams and driving decisions to closure.
  • Technical accountability: Take responsibility for mechanical design definition, tolerance analysis, manufacturability, serviceability, and design documentation for new or improved products, applying engineering judgment to trade-offs.
  • Customer interaction: Serve as a technical point of contact for internal and external customers, effectively communicating design intent, technical constraints, trade-offs, and project status to audiences with varying technical backgrounds.
  • Product validation: Build centrifugal compressor prototypes to be used for pre-production testing and verification, implementing any lessons learned during the build into the design.
  • Travel: Ability to travel, including internationally, up to 5%.
Qualifications:

  • Bachelors in Mechanical Engineering
  • 5+ years of related design or product development experience with a strong foundation in mechanical design, machine design, mechanics of materials, manufacturing processes, and/or engineering fundamentals, with a proven track record of delivering released designs.
Preferences:
  • Demonstrated experience with centrifugal compressor components, pressure-containing equipment, rotating equipment, or packaged equipment design is highly desirable.
  • Proficiency with finite element analysis, tolerance analysis, design automation, and/or computer programming is a plus.
  • Hands-on proficiency with CAD and PLM systems (NX and Teamcenter) is strongly preferred.
Core Competencies:

  • Strong working knowledge of computer systems and basic Microsoft Office.
  • Strong command of the English language and the ability to clearly communicate in writing and speech with peers, leadership, and internal/external customers.
  • Ability to quickly understand, condense, and organize complex information to make sound, independent engineering decisions.
  • Self-motivated, responsible, detail-oriented, and personable, with the confidence to own outcomes.
  • Ability to work collaboratively while independently owning significant deliverables and reliably managing stress, change, and pressure with professionalism.
  • Ability to perform critical mental tasks such as decision-making, prioritizing, organizing, and exercising sound judgment to align work with business objectives.
Travel & Work Arrangements / Requirements

  • The location for this position is Buffalo, NY. 4 days onsite, 1 day remote.
Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $85,000-$95,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title:  Field Service Technician
Location: Blandon, PA  (Hybrid with travel)

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview:
Excelsior Blower Systems, a proud Ingersoll Rand brand, has been a powerhouse in engineered air solutions delivering decades of proven performance, reliability, and innovation. Backed by a legacy of excellence, we’re trusted across industries for systems that perform under pressure and consistently exceed expectations.  We’re looking for a hands-on Field Service Technician who thrives in the field and takes pride in keeping critical equipment running at peak performance. In this role, you’ll be the expert customers rely on—installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing Ingersoll Rand positive displacement (PD) blower systems, including controls and VFDs, directly at customer sites. You’ll play a vital role in delivering responsive, high-impact service that supports customers’ operational needs.  
Your work won’t stop in the field. You’ll also install controls and wiring for PD blower systems at our facility, applying your electromechanical expertise across the full equipment lifecycle. If you already bring PD blower experience, you’ll hit the ground running. If not, you bring a strong foundation in rotating equipment, motor and electrical troubleshooting, alignment, system-level diagnostics, and reading schematics and P&IDs—and the drive to master the rest. This is a role for someone who enjoys solving real-world problems, working independently, and making a visible impact every day. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Install, commission, and start up positive displacement (PD) blower packages, vacuum/pressure systems, and associated rotating equipment per OEM specifications and site requirements.

  • Configure, program, and troubleshoot variable frequency drives (VFDs) and soft starters (parameter setup, PID loops, accel/decel profiles, motor protection, fieldbus/communication interfaces such as Modbus/TCP, EtherNet/IP).

  • Diagnose and repair electrical controls including relays, contactors, motor starters, overloads, interlocks, safety circuits, and control transformers.

  • Perform control panel wiring and field terminations (24 VDC control, 120/480 VAC power, grounding/bonding, signal wiring, shielded cable practices); read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and P&IDs.

  • Install and integrate instrumentation (pressure, temperature, vibration, flow, differential pressure transmitters, proximity sensors, limit switches) and calibrate as required.

  • Execute mechanical service tasks (coupling alignment—laser or dial, belt tensioning, blower timing, bearing replacement, seal changes, lubrication, fastener torque verification).

  • Conduct vibration and performance checks; identify root cause of abnormal noise, heat, vibration, or amperage draw (airflow restrictions, leaks, misalignment, cavitation, resonance).

  • Troubleshoot system issues end-to-end across electrical, mechanical, and controls, including motor diagnostics (insulation resistance, megger testing, continuity), VFD/motor matching, and load-related faults.

  • Perform field measurements and documentation (voltage/current, phase balance, harmonics, airflow/pressure, vibration readings) and produce detailed service reports with parts lists and recommended follow-up.

Requirements:

  • High School diploma or GED
  • 5+ years of relevant / equivalent technical experience: millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service.
  • 2+ years of electromechanical experience

Core Competencies

  • Strong electromechanical troubleshooting skills, including rotating equipment such as motors, gearboxes, compressors, mixers, blowers, and pumps; electronic power conversion (AC to DC) and related faults/alarms (GF, OC, OV, UV, OL, OH); and PLC troubleshooting, including I/O, hardware, and software checks.
  • Clear and concise verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, employees, and Sales Representatives.
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot issues, resolve conflicts, make sound decisions, and appropriately escalate problems in dynamic environments.
  • Strong organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills with the ability to meet deadlines and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Valid driver’s license held for at least 12 months with a satisfactory driving record. No major or frequent violations, including DUI within the past 5 years, hit-and-run, license suspension, reckless/careless driving, or multiple minor violations/preventable collisions within the past 3 years.

Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is 40% onsite shop repairs and up to 60% travel for field work
  • Possible minimal travel to Canada, Puerto Rico, and/or Mexico
  • Paid travel time at full hourly rate
  • Company vehicle and gas provided

What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Location: Phoenix, AZ

About Us  

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview

  • The Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Industrial Technologies and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 
     

Responsibilities

  • Ensure the correct installation, maintenance, and field repair of the equipment manufactured and sold by Ingersoll Rand at the purchaser's location. 

  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the field installation and repair requirements of this equipment. 

  • Provide technical advice and be able to train customers, potential customers, field salesmen, and field service trainees.

  • Diagnose problems, recommend corrective action in this unsupervised environment and submit clear, accurate records and/or oral reports to the manufacturing facility. 

  • Maintain a high degree of integrity in handling business affairs.

  • Maintain proper written and oral communication skills to transfer information related to service work in a concise and logical manner. 

  • Submit detailed technical reports on each service call in a legible fashion, suitable for billing customers. 

  • Submit accurate, detailed & timely expense account records along with timecards on a weekly basis. Maintain good financial records and practices to manage company business matters, credit cards, and if required, a company car.

Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems. Experience on compressed air systems/centrifugal technologies/solid controls background is a plus. While not required, those with knowledge in the service, diagnosis, and startup of both rotary and centrifugal air compressors, including dryers, cooling towers, and filtration systems are encouraged to apply. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required. .

Core Competencies 

  • Must possess a mechanic's set of tools; specialty tools will be provided. 

  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years

  • This position requires working in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards. 
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Customer service skills such as conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner. 
  • Mechanical competency to be able to learn, diagnose, and troubleshoot compressor systems and machinery. 
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Preferences

  • Desired degree program in Electrical/Electronic Technology or HVAC with basic knowledge of some or all of the following: AC/DC circuits, wiring diagrams/schematics, motors/controls, PLCs, HVAC electricity, controls, refrigeration systems and/or refrigerant certification. Military experience and/or sufficient mechanical working experience is a plus. Candidates who possess this knowledge or skills but have not completed a formal program may be considered. 

  • EPA 608 /F-GAS 303/2008/CE/ISHRAE Certification Preferred (Refrigeration experience/certification a plus).

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position may require occasional travel for training. 1-2 times per year for one week at a time. (5-10%). 

  • This position is included in an on-call rotation with other service technicians in the local area to service customer emergencies in the evenings or on weekends. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required during scheduled on-call weeks.

  • Collaborate with engineering teams to determine testing methods and troubleshoot product and process issues.
  • Analyze test data and prepare clear, concise technical reports.

  • Ensure compliance with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements while maintaining a clean and organized work environment.

  • Minimum 1 year of experience in a laboratory, testing, or technical environment, preferably within manufacturing or engineering.
  • Experience with laboratory testing, equipment calibration, and maintenance.
  • Strong technical, mechanical, and mathematical aptitude.
  • Knowledge of laboratory safety, quality standards, and regulatory compliance requirements.
  • Ability to analyze data and prepare technical documentation and reports.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Technical competence in Fluid Power systems, including hydraulics, pneumatics, and electromechanical systems.



Core Competencies

  • Problem-solving and troubleshooting.
  • Attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Collaboration and teamwork.
  • Continuous learning and adaptability.
  • Strong technical and mechanical comprehension

 
Preferences:  

  • Associate degree in Engineering Technology, Mechanical Technology, Electronics, or a related technical field.
  • Experience supporting testing and troubleshooting activities in both laboratory and manufacturing environments.
  • Experience working with vacuum pump products or related industrial equipment.

Title: Manager, P2P Procurement Excellence
Location:  Remote,  US
 

Job Overview:
The Procure-to-Pay Manager leads the operational backbone of a global, digital and AI-enabled procurement organization. As Ingersoll Rand continues to scale and standardize procurement operations across regions, this role owns the buying experience from requisition through purchase order and clean handoff into the ERP – ensuring transactions are fast, compliant, low-touch, and accurate before they reach downstream finance processes. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys running an operation well while continuously re-engineering how it works

Responsibilities:

  • Own day-to-day Procure-to-Pay (P2P) operations from requisition through purchase order issuance, ensuring clean and complete ERP integration.
  • Manage buying channel strategy and enablement, including guided buying, hosted and punchout catalogs, and channel compliance.
  • Lead supplier onboarding and transactional enablement while maintaining accurate supplier master data.
  • Administer and configure P2P systems and workflows across platforms such as Coupa, Jaggaer, and SAP Ariba, including release and upgrade readiness.
  • Define and maintain P2P standard operating procedures, user training, and business-wide support models.
  • Monitor and report key operational KPIs, including cycle time, touchless order rate, catalog coverage, PO accuracy, and ERP integration success.
  • Partner with IT, Finance Systems, and Category teams to drive automation, process simplification, and AI-enabled workflow improvements.
  • Support the expansion and standardization of P2P processes across additional regions and business units.


Requirements:

  • 5+ years of experience in Procurement Operations, Procure-to-Pay, eProcurement systems, Supply Chain, or Shared Services Hands-on experience configuring, administering, or supporting an enterprise eProcurement or P2P platform
  • Bachelor's degree required


Core Competencies:

  • Operational rigor and process discipline paired with a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Change management and user adoption expertise. Data-driven decision making and structured problem solving.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities across time zones and business units


Preferences:

  • Experience working in global, matrixed, or shared services environments
  • Exposure to multi-ERP landscapes and system integration between procurement and finance platforms. Background in catalog enablement, supplier enablement, or transactional procurement transformation.
  • Familiarity with the full Source-to-Pay lifecycle and where P2P connects to sourcing and contracting
  • Process improvement certification or training (Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent
  • Experience introducing automation or AI-assisted workflows into transactional processes
  • Comfort operating both strategically and in the detail of day-to-day execution

Pay Range: The pay range for this role is $90,000-$120,000 excluding incentive opportunities. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Title: Materials Planning Manager
Location:  Mocksville, NC (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
This is a high-impact leadership opportunity at our Mocksville manufacturing plant, where the Materials Planning team plays a critical role in keeping production moving and customers supplied. Mocksville is entering an exciting period of growth, with new products and additional Gardner Denver product lines expected to transition into the facility. The Materials Planning Manager will have a visible and direct impact on production flow, inventory health, product-launch success, customer delivery, and the plant’s ability to scale effectively.  

As the Materials Planning Manager, you will lead and develop a team of buyer/planners supporting a diverse operation that includes pack assembly, rotary assembly, remanufacturing, and machine shop activity.  The plant manages a broad supplier base and a complex mix of short lead-time, book-and-turn orders and long lead-time, engineer-to-order projects. This is not a desk-only leadership position. You will remain close to the operation, helping the team anticipate supply gaps and drive execution across promise-date accuracy, past-due purchase orders, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, inventory turns, and over-entitlement reduction. You will also maintain a small hands-on purchasing portfolio supporting gears, pinions, and bull gears.  

We are looking for a hands-on materials, purchasing, or planning leader who can see around corners, bring discipline to a complex ERP/MRP environment, and turn competing priorities into clear execution. The right leader will combine urgency and accountability with empathy—staying connected to the team, coaching both experienced and developing buyer/planners, identifying risks early, and helping employees navigate the daily pressures of manufacturing materials management. If you thrive in a fast-moving manufacturing environment and want your leadership to make a meaningful operational difference, this role offers the opportunity to strengthen planning discipline, improve inventory performance, support successful product launches, and ensure the right parts arrive at the right time.

Responsibilities

Materials Planning and Supply Continuity:

  • Lead site material planning activities to ensure the timely availability of materials required to support production operations.
  • Own the stocking and replenishment strategy for all site raw materials.
  • Lead the site inventory optimization strategy, balancing material availability, inventory investment, and operational requirements.
  • Serve as the escalation point when Material Planners are unable to resolve supply, delivery, inventory, or supplier-related issues effectively.

Team Leadership and Development:
  • Lead, coach, and develop the Materials Planning team, establishing clear expectations for performance, accountability, and execution.
  • Ensure team members are properly trained and effectively utilizing ERP/MRP tools, planning processes, and Ingersoll Rand standard work.
  • Support employee development through regular coaching, structured training, and individual development plans.

Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement:
  • Champion Lean principles and continuous improvement across Materials Planning functions.
  • Strengthen planning discipline, standard work, problem-solving, and root-cause corrective action practices.
  • Drive improvements in material availability, inventory performance, planning accuracy, and overall team productivity.

Cross-Functional Leadership:
  • Serve as the Materials Planning liaison across Production, Procurement, Supplier Quality, Quality Assurance, Engineering, Accounts Payable, Finance, and other functional groups.
  • Coordinate resolution of issues involving supplier quality, goods received not invoiced, invoice discrepancies, engineering changes, new product development, and other material-related business needs.
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to identify supply risks, resolve constraints, and support production, product launches, and customer delivery requirements.

Team's Responsibilities - 
  • Material Planning and Inventory Management
    • Maintain material plans within the planning time fence to ensure continuity of supply.
    • Review open material requirements and proactively identify shortages, supply gaps, and inventory risks.
    • Maintain optimal inventory levels and appropriate safety stock for assigned parts.
    • Maintain accurate ABC classifications and other planning inputs required for the Plan for Every Part process.
    • Communicate forecasts, demand requirements, and replenishment plans to suppliers.
    • Maintain accurate item-master lead times based on supplier performance, process improvements, current constraints, product-family demand, and business priorities. 
  • Purchasing and Supplier Management
    • Perform timely and cost-conscious procurement of production, inventory, and maintenance, repair, and operations materials.
    • Review and analyze requisitions to confirm required quantities, specifications, delivery dates, and other purchasing requirements.
    • Monitor supplier performance related to delivery, quality, responsiveness, and pricing.
    • Expedite, de-expedite, or adjust purchase orders as needed to align material availability with production demand.
    • Promptly communicate supplier delivery, quality, pricing, or capacity concerns and drive timely resolution.
    • Escalate recurring or significant supplier-performance issues to Procurement and Materials Planning leadership.
  • Shortage Management and Production Support
    • Proactively identify and manage material shortages, including documenting root causes and supporting corrective actions.
    • Coordinate with Production Planners when materials cannot be delivered as promised and develop alternative supply or scheduling solutions.
    • Analyze material and capacity availability to support accurate customer promise dates for sales orders.
    • Work with applicable functional groups to resolve complex delivery requirements, competing priorities, and material constraints.
  • Quality, Invoice, and Transaction Resolution
    • Partner with Quality Assurance and Supplier Quality to resolve supplier-related quality issues.
    • Coordinate with suppliers and Accounting to resolve invoicing, receipt, pricing, and payment discrepancies.
    • Ensure material-related transactional issues are addressed promptly to prevent supply disruption or inaccurate financial records.
  • Productivity and Cost Improvement
    • Identify and implement cost-reduction, inventory-improvement, and productivity initiatives aligned with corporate goals.
    • Maintain an active pipeline of improvement projects and accurate financial records for productivity reporting and benefit tracking.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 5+ years of prior people management experience, ideally managing buyer/planner, purchasing, materials, planning, scheduling, or similar supply chain teams. 
  • 5+ years’ experience working in a manufacturing environment, such as industrial, assembly, machining, purchased-parts-heavy, or engineer-to-order manufacturing. 
  • 4+ years of experience in materials planning, purchasing, buyer/planner functions, master scheduling, and/or supply planning, or related manufacturing supply chain execution. 
  • 3+ years of demonstrated experience using ERP/MRP systems to support materials planning activities such as managing promise dates, purchase orders, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, inventory signals, and planning execution.
  • 2+ years’ experience in Excel skills to include utilizing formulas at an intermediate to advanced level 

Core Competencies
  • Hands-On People Leadership: Ability to coach, support, and hold a buyer/planner team accountable through regular engagement, one-on-ones, clear communication, and a balanced leadership style.
  • Materials Planning & Purchasing Execution: Strong understanding of purchasing, planning, promise dates, past-due POs, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, supplier follow-up, and purchased-parts support in a manufacturing environment.
  • ERP/MRP & Replenishment Systems: Ability to use ERP/MRP systems, Excel, and planning data to interpret demand signals, manage supply gaps, support pull or non-MRP replenishment where applicable, and make sound planning decisions.
  • Manufacturing Operations & Complex Production Environments: Experience supporting manufacturing operations, ideally including assembly, machining, engineer-to-order, job shop, mixed-model, or long lead-time environments.
  • Inventory, Lean & Visual Performance Management: Ability to drive inventory turns, reduce excess or over-entitlement, support lean planning practices, and use visual management tools or performance tracking systems to improve execution and accountability.

Preferences:
  • MBA and/or Bachelor Concentration in Business or Supply Chain Management
  • APICS or CPIM certification
  • ERP Experience in Oracle R12
  • Experience managing a large, diverse, or complex supplier/materials portfolio
  • Experience in engineer-to-order, long lead-time, complex BOM, or mixed-model manufacturing environments
  • Experience driving inventory turns, inventory reduction, excess inventory reduction, or over-entitlement improvement

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This position is based onsite in Mocksville, NC

Job Title:  Field Service Technician, Electromechanical
Location: Blandon, PA  (Hybrid with travel)

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview:
Excelsior Blower Systems, a proud Ingersoll Rand brand, has been a powerhouse in engineered air solutions delivering decades of proven performance, reliability, and innovation. Backed by a legacy of excellence, we’re trusted across industries for systems that perform under pressure and consistently exceed expectations.  We’re looking for a hands-on Field Service Technician who thrives in the field and takes pride in keeping critical equipment running at peak performance. In this role, you’ll be the expert customers rely on—installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing Ingersoll Rand positive displacement (PD) blower systems, including controls and VFDs, directly at customer sites. You’ll play a vital role in delivering responsive, high-impact service that supports customers’ operational needs.  
Your work won’t stop in the field. You’ll also install controls and wiring for PD blower systems at our facility, applying your electromechanical expertise across the full equipment lifecycle. If you already bring PD blower experience, you’ll hit the ground running. If not, you bring a strong foundation in rotating equipment, motor and electrical troubleshooting, alignment, system-level diagnostics, and reading schematics and P&IDs—and the drive to master the rest. This is a role for someone who enjoys solving real-world problems, working independently, and making a visible impact every day. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Install, commission, and start up positive displacement (PD) blower packages, vacuum/pressure systems, and associated rotating equipment per OEM specifications and site requirements.

  • Configure, program, and troubleshoot variable frequency drives (VFDs) and soft starters (parameter setup, PID loops, accel/decel profiles, motor protection, fieldbus/communication interfaces such as Modbus/TCP, EtherNet/IP).

  • Diagnose and repair electrical controls including relays, contactors, motor starters, overloads, interlocks, safety circuits, and control transformers.

  • Perform control panel wiring and field terminations (24 VDC control, 120/480 VAC power, grounding/bonding, signal wiring, shielded cable practices); read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and P&IDs.

  • Install and integrate instrumentation (pressure, temperature, vibration, flow, differential pressure transmitters, proximity sensors, limit switches) and calibrate as required.

  • Execute mechanical service tasks (coupling alignment—laser or dial, belt tensioning, blower timing, bearing replacement, seal changes, lubrication, fastener torque verification).

  • Conduct vibration and performance checks; identify root cause of abnormal noise, heat, vibration, or amperage draw (airflow restrictions, leaks, misalignment, cavitation, resonance).

  • Troubleshoot system issues end-to-end across electrical, mechanical, and controls, including motor diagnostics (insulation resistance, megger testing, continuity), VFD/motor matching, and load-related faults.

  • Perform field measurements and documentation (voltage/current, phase balance, harmonics, airflow/pressure, vibration readings) and produce detailed service reports with parts lists and recommended follow-up.

Requirements:

  • High School diploma or GED
  • 5+ years of relevant / equivalent technical experience: millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service.
  • 2+ years of electromechanical experience
Core Competencies

  • Strong electromechanical troubleshooting skills, including rotating equipment such as motors, gearboxes, compressors, mixers, blowers, and pumps; electronic power conversion (AC to DC) and related faults/alarms (GF, OC, OV, UV, OL, OH); and PLC troubleshooting, including I/O, hardware, and software checks.
  • Clear and concise verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, employees, and Sales Representatives.
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot issues, resolve conflicts, make sound decisions, and appropriately escalate problems in dynamic environments.
  • Strong organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills with the ability to meet deadlines and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Valid driver’s license held for at least 12 months with a satisfactory driving record. No major or frequent violations, including DUI within the past 5 years, hit-and-run, license suspension, reckless/careless driving, or multiple minor violations/preventable collisions within the past 3 years.
Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is 40% onsite shop repairs and up to 60% travel for field work
  • Possible minimal travel to Canada, Puerto Rico, and/or Mexico
  • Paid travel time at full hourly rate
  • Company vehicle and gas provided

Manager, Materials

Location: West Chester, PA
Job Type: Full-Time | On-Site

About Ingersoll Rand

At Ingersoll Rand, we are driven by an ownership mindset and a commitment to making life better for our employees, customers, and communities. With more than 160 years of innovation and industry leadership, we develop mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions that help improve productivity, efficiency, and sustainability across a wide range of industries.

Our portfolio of more than 80 trusted brands serves customers in life sciences, food and beverage, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, clean energy, and many other markets worldwide. Join us and become part of a team that is shaping the future through innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Position Summary

We are seeking a strategic and results-driven Materials Manager to lead all aspects of materials planning, inventory control, and materials management for our West Chester manufacturing facility. This role plays a critical part in ensuring uninterrupted production through effective supply chain execution, inventory optimization, and continuous improvement initiatives.

The Materials Manager will lead a team responsible for planning, procurement, inventory management, and material flow within a high-volume, lean manufacturing environment. Success in this role will be measured through key performance indicators including inventory turns, on-time delivery, service levels, and inventory accuracy.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead materials planning, inventory control, and replenishment activities to support production and customer demand.
  • Manage raw material inventory using SAP/MRP systems while optimizing inventory levels and material flow.
  • Develop and execute materials strategies that support business objectives, operational performance, and inventory targets.
  • Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to increase efficiency and reduce waste.
  • Oversee new product introductions, material lifecycle management, and inventory compliance processes.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the materials team while fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Promote a safe work environment and ensure compliance with company safety standards and OSHA regulations.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Materials Management, Business, Operations, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of experience in materials management within a manufacturing environment.
  • 3+ years of leadership or management experience.
  • Experience working with MRP systems and inventory control processes.
  • Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing principles and materials planning.
  • Proven ability to lead teams, drive performance, and improve operational processes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Materials Management, Supply Chain, Business Management, or related discipline.
  • APICS CPIM certification.
  • Experience implementing Kanban or other Lean inventory systems.
  • Strong background in inventory management, operations, and supply chain planning.
  • Experience with visual management and daily management systems.
  • SAP experience preferred.

At Ingersoll Rand, we believe in empowering employees to take ownership of their careers and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package includes:
