Job Overview: 
The Field Service Technician is responsible for providing field technical support for IR products, striving to be customer focused, fully responsive, and successful in meeting the 24/7 technical service needs of customers. Develop a collaborative relationship with the balance of IR to establish this area as the “go-to” place for technical field service knowledge.  Focus on providing valued solutions to customers, utilizing IR services as well as IR’s products. The job also carries a variety of incentive plans that are paid out annually. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Provide technical support during repair and/or installation, at customers’ sites, of IR’s equipment to ensure standards are met and the integrity of the equipment is maintained.
  • Ensure safe work practices are followed, reporting all safety incidents and near misses on a timely basis and maintaining the goal of “zero” lost time incidents
  • Work to improve responsiveness to customers by being available to make sales calls, perform technical walk downs, and provide solutions to customers that distinguish IR’s proposals and capabilities
  • Complete required reports, including Service Reports, Customer Call Reports, Expense Reports and Time Sheets, on a timely basis in order to provide appropriate follow-up to customers, including accurate invoicing for services.
  • Suggest improvements to processes and procedures in order to improve customer response time and accuracy of all data
  • Comply with Department Guidelines and Procedures in order to maintain appropriate standards of service provided to customers
  • Maintain proficiencies using vibration analysis and laser alignment equipment for balancing, testing, etc.
  • Generate sales leads from customers who could benefit from additional support in order to improve solutions provided, improve relationships, and grow IR installed base, collect information for the Customer Relationship Management [CRM] system and provide information to Sales for additional opportunities; and improve global visibility of IR Aftermarket in the CRM system

Requirements:

  • 3 years of relevant technical background including millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service experience, or equivalent experience
  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • The job includes an assigned vehicle for work use, so the candidate must have a valid license and be able to pass a Motor Vehicle background check.

Core Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Clear and concise communicator (both oral and written) 
  • Excellent collaboration skills
  • Strong computer skills in Microsoft® Word, Excel, PowerPoint 
  • Proven time management, organizational, problem solving, and prioritization skills to successfully complete responsibilities in a timely manner
  • Ability to resolve conflict, to apply critical thinking to solve problems and to escalate when needed
  • Highly organized with ability to work independently as well as part of a team
  • Ability to create and maintain strong relationships with customers, employees and Sales Reps
  • High moral and ethical standards; integrity is continuously apparent
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Comfortable and effective working in the “virtual world” 

Preferences:

  • Bilingual in Spanish is highly desired
  • Some technical schooling, classwork toward a degree in a technical area
  • Background evidencing positions with increasing responsibility and leadership
  • Experience specifying replacement parts for highly engineered equipment and products
  • Experience in industrial sales or technical selling
  • Troubleshoot vibration, system, and aerodynamic problems in equipment
 

Physical Requirements:

  • Heavy Lifting: Must be able to lift up to 50–75 pounds regularly.
  • Prolonged Standing: Ability to stand for 8–12 hours daily.
  • Frequent Bending: Regular kneeling, crouching, crawling, and stooping.
  • Climbing Ability: Safely ascend ladders, scaffolding, and stairs while wearing fall protection.
  • Manual Dexterity: Fine motor skills to handle small tools.
  • Awkward Positions: Working in tight, cramped, or confined spaces.
  • Overhead Reaching: Extending arms overhead for extended periods.
  • Visual Acuity: Close vision, color vision, and depth perception.
  • Weather Exposure: Working in extreme heat, cold, or rain.
  • Driving Endurance: Operating a service vehicle for long hours.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position is remote. The selected candidate will need to be based in Indiana, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, or Kentucky near a major airport.
  • Up to 80% travel, with possibility of international travel 

Pay Range: The pay range for this role is $65,000k - $85,000k annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:

 

Serve as the primary point of contact for a sales region within the BioPharma segment of ILC Dover. This role represents the BioPharma Solutions to the customer and leads all commercial activities specific to the life sciences and pharmaceutical manufacturing environment. The RSM combines sales, business development expertise with strong relationship management skills to advance partnerships, increase profitable sales, and deliver customized solutions that meet stringent regulatory requirements and align with client goals in the BioPharma industry. Responsibilities include driving supporting customers in achieving operational excellence and sustainability objectives while improving business objectives.

 

Responsibilities:

 

  • Client Relationship Management: Build and maintain strong, long-term relationships with key clients, decision-makers, and influencers to drive trust, loyalty, and business growth.
  • Strategic Account Planning: Develop and execute customized customer strategies focused on co-value creation, aligned with client objectives and company goals.
  • Customer Advocacy & Problem Resolution: Serve as the primary point of contact for customer needs, addressing issues, complaints, technical support, and service concerns to ensure a positive experience.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Coordinate with sales, marketing, product, engineering, logistics, Field Application Specialists, and other teams to effectively meet customer requirements and communicate RACI responsibilities.
  • Revenue & Opportunity Development: Identify, develop, and pursue upselling, cross-selling, and new business opportunities with targeted customers, including opportunities for IR Solutions.
  • Commercial & Contract Management: Negotiate contracts, renewals, pricing, terms and conditions, NDAs, incentives, rebates, and other commercial programs to support mutually beneficial partnerships.
  • Account Data, Pipeline & Reporting: Maintain customer relationship maps and account information in SFDC, manage pipeline opportunities, and provide monthly updates on activities, forecasts, account status, and revenue performance.
  • Account Management & Channel Support: Utilize established account management processes, tools, and resources while resolving distribution-channel and aftermarket service issues and maintaining strong customer partnerships.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Sales, Marketing, or Engineering required 
  • 5+ years of direct sales experience required.

 

Core Competencies:

  • Ability to build and maintain strong professional relationships with customers, key institutions, and team members.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including verbal, written, and presentation capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively both independently and within a team environment.
  • Mechanical and electrical knowledge applicable to industrial equipment.
  • Capability to assess customer needs, analyze data, perform basic equipment performance calculations, and recommend technical solutions.
  • Proficiency with technology tools; experience with Salesforce preferred.
  • Proven business and sales acumen, including account prospecting, organizational navigation, value-based selling, and competitive account acquisition.
  • Strong prioritization and time management skills.

 

 

Preferences:

  • 3+ years of direct sales account management experience desired.
  • Prior territory sales management and/or channel management experience. Prior industrial sales experience preferred.
  • Proven record of ability in strategic thinking and growth leadership.
  • Strong communication and analytical skills both verbal and written.
  • Strong people skills, ability to influence customers.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to:
    • DUI in the previous 5 years
    • Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • Travel 50 to 60% monthly across the customer sites regionally.
  • Remote position, however interested candidates should have access to a major airport for travel and be located within the Northeast US region

 

Pay Range: 
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $150,000-$160,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Title:  Field Service Technician, Electromechanical
Location: Blandon, PA  (Hybrid with travel)

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview:
Excelsior Blower Systems, a proud Ingersoll Rand brand, has been a powerhouse in engineered air solutions delivering decades of proven performance, reliability, and innovation. Backed by a legacy of excellence, we’re trusted across industries for systems that perform under pressure and consistently exceed expectations.  We’re looking for a hands-on Field Service Technician who thrives in the field and takes pride in keeping critical equipment running at peak performance. In this role, you’ll be the expert customers rely on—installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing Ingersoll Rand positive displacement (PD) blower systems, including controls and VFDs, directly at customer sites. You’ll play a vital role in delivering responsive, high-impact service that supports customers’ operational needs.  
Your work won’t stop in the field. You’ll also install controls and wiring for PD blower systems at our facility, applying your electromechanical expertise across the full equipment lifecycle. If you already bring PD blower experience, you’ll hit the ground running. If not, you bring a strong foundation in rotating equipment, motor and electrical troubleshooting, alignment, system-level diagnostics, and reading schematics and P&IDs—and the drive to master the rest. This is a role for someone who enjoys solving real-world problems, working independently, and making a visible impact every day. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Install, commission, and start up positive displacement (PD) blower packages, vacuum/pressure systems, and associated rotating equipment per OEM specifications and site requirements.

  • Configure, program, and troubleshoot variable frequency drives (VFDs) and soft starters (parameter setup, PID loops, accel/decel profiles, motor protection, fieldbus/communication interfaces such as Modbus/TCP, EtherNet/IP).

  • Diagnose and repair electrical controls including relays, contactors, motor starters, overloads, interlocks, safety circuits, and control transformers.

  • Perform control panel wiring and field terminations (24 VDC control, 120/480 VAC power, grounding/bonding, signal wiring, shielded cable practices); read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and P&IDs.

  • Install and integrate instrumentation (pressure, temperature, vibration, flow, differential pressure transmitters, proximity sensors, limit switches) and calibrate as required.

  • Execute mechanical service tasks (coupling alignment—laser or dial, belt tensioning, blower timing, bearing replacement, seal changes, lubrication, fastener torque verification).

  • Conduct vibration and performance checks; identify root cause of abnormal noise, heat, vibration, or amperage draw (airflow restrictions, leaks, misalignment, cavitation, resonance).

  • Troubleshoot system issues end-to-end across electrical, mechanical, and controls, including motor diagnostics (insulation resistance, megger testing, continuity), VFD/motor matching, and load-related faults.

  • Perform field measurements and documentation (voltage/current, phase balance, harmonics, airflow/pressure, vibration readings) and produce detailed service reports with parts lists and recommended follow-up.

Requirements:

  • High School diploma or GED
  • 5+ years of relevant / equivalent technical experience: millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service.
  • 2+ years of electromechanical experience

Core Competencies

  • Strong electromechanical troubleshooting skills, including rotating equipment such as motors, gearboxes, compressors, mixers, blowers, and pumps; electronic power conversion (AC to DC) and related faults/alarms (GF, OC, OV, UV, OL, OH); and PLC troubleshooting, including I/O, hardware, and software checks.
  • Clear and concise verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, employees, and Sales Representatives.
  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot issues, resolve conflicts, make sound decisions, and appropriately escalate problems in dynamic environments.
  • Strong organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills with the ability to meet deadlines and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Valid driver’s license held for at least 12 months with a satisfactory driving record. No major or frequent violations, including DUI within the past 5 years, hit-and-run, license suspension, reckless/careless driving, or multiple minor violations/preventable collisions within the past 3 years.

Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is 40% onsite shop repairs and up to 60% travel for field work
  • Possible minimal travel to Canada, Puerto Rico, and/or Mexico
  • Paid travel time at full hourly rate
  • Company vehicle and gas provided

What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

  • Questions accepted practices, develops creative approaches, mitigates resistance to change and encourages others to do the same to promote progress through change. Previous experience conducting training is an advantage.

  • Cultivates strong, mutually beneficial customer relationships and works to earn the trust of the customer by ensuring that the company delivers value and acquires customer-driven insights to effectively address issues, needs and opportunities.

À propos de nous

Ingersoll Rand est une entreprise Fortune 500 passionnée par l'amélioration de la vie. Nous y parvenons en incarnant nos valeurs, en nous concentrant sans relâche sur la réussite de nos clients et en collaborant avec nos employés pour penser et agir comme des propriétaires. Aperçu du poste
Le ou la titulaire du poste doit effectuer différents types d’opérations de peinture, incluant la préparation, le masquage, l’application de la peinture et le nettoyage de composants et d’équipements fabriqués, à l’aide de divers types de peintures et revêtements liquides, tout en respectant les normes de qualité établies.

Des tâches additionnelles peuvent inclure la finition des pièces, la préparation du matériel avant expédition ainsi que l’emballage.

Responsabilités :

  • Peindre des composants et des équipements fabriqués à l’aide d’un pistolet de pulvérisation à assistance pneumatique,
  • Préparer les surfaces (nettoyage, lavage, ponçage, masquage, etc.),
  • Sélectionner le type de peinture ou le mélange approprié selon les spécifications prédéterminées,
  • Nettoyer et entretenir les équipements de peinture, de ventilation et les équipements de protection individuelle (EPI),
  • Gérer et maintenir les inventaires de peinture,
  • Effectuer le nettoyage manuel à l’aide de brosses métalliques ou de tampons abrasifs afin d’enlever les saletés tenaces, dépôts de carbone ou autres résidus sur les pièces de soufflerie,
  • Exécuter diverses tâches connexes, telles que la réception et la préparation des expéditions,
  • Opérer un chariot élévateur

Compétences et exigences:

  • DEP en carrosserie ou AEP en peinture industrielle
  • Toute autre combinaison équivalente de qualifications et d’expérience pertinente sera considérée
  • Maîtrise des machines techniques et des équipements de levage
  • Minimum de 6 mois d’expérience de travail dans un atelier de peinture industrielle
  • Familiarité avec divers équipements et outils propres au métier
  • Rigueur et souci du détail
  • Bon sens de l’organisation et capacité à travailler sous pression
  • Rigueur et souci du detail
  • Bonnes habiletés interpersonnelles et attitude positive
  • Excellente dextérité et très bonne coordination œil?main
  • Capacité de lever occasionnellement des charges lourdes (jusqu’à 50 lb)

 

Ce que nous offrons
Chez Ingersoll Rand, nous promouvons une culture de responsabilité personnelle — en prenant soin de notre entreprise, de nos communautés et de notre environnement, ainsi que de notre santé et bien-être individuels. Notre programme complet d'avantages est conçu pour vous offrir les outils et le soutien nécessaires pour prendre en main votre santé, afin qu'ensemble, nous puissions continuer à améliorer la vie.

Notre gamme d'avantages comprend :

  • Culture responsabilisante : Encourager la responsabilité personnelle dans la réussite de notre entreprise, l'engagement communautaire et la protection de l'environnement.
  • Options de soins de santé : Plans complets de couverture médicale, dentaire et visuelle, ainsi que des assurances vie pour répondre à divers besoins de santé.
  • Programmes de bien-être : Ressources et initiatives pour soutenir votre bien-être global.
  • Plan d'épargne-retraite : Un plan solide avec des contributions de l'employeur pour sécuriser votre avenir.
  • Attribution d'actions aux employés : Une opportunité de partager la croissance et le succès de l'entreprise.
  • Congés payés : Pour vous assurer d'avoir le temps de vous ressourcer et de profiter de la vie en dehors du travail.
  • Environnement de soutien : Un programme d'avantages conçu pour vous aider à donner le meilleur de vous-même au travail et dans la vie.

job.description:
Description du poste : Spécialiste SSE niveau I

Emplacement du bureau : 190 Av. du Voyageur #100, Pointe-Claire, Québec H9R 6A

Résumé du poste :

Le spécialiste EHS I joue un rôle crucial dans la promotion d'une culture de sécurité et de responsabilité environnementale au sein de l'organisation. Cette personne collabore avec divers départements pour garantir que toutes les activités sont menées de manière sûre et respectueuse de l'environnement. Il aide à développer et à faire respecter les politiques et procédures de l'entreprise conformément aux exigences réglementaires et aux meilleures pratiques de l'industrie.

Horaire de travail : 40 heures/semaine du lundi au vendredi.

 Responsabilités :

  • Développer, mettre en œuvre et superviser les politiques, programmes et procédures de santé et sécurité environnementale (SSE).
  • Assurer l'application et le respect des normes et réglementations en matière d'SSE.
  • Promouvoir la culture SSE de l'entreprise.
  • Formation et sensibilisation des employés.
  • Mise en œuvre du Travail Standard d'Entreprise.
  • Évaluation des risques annuelle.
  • Travailler avec les entrepreneurs et sous-traitants pour assurer le respect des politiques et procédures de l'entreprise.
  • Gérer le comité SSE et le comité Green X (environnement durable).
  • Rapporter et examiner les accidents/incidents SSE, y compris les enquêtes de cause première et la mise en œuvre des actions correctives.
  • Inspections des locaux et gestion du calendrier de conformité dans Gensuite.
  • Rapport des métriques SSE et mise en œuvre des actions pour réduire les risques SSE pour l'entreprise.

Tâches liées à la qualité :

  • Mise à jour des documents de qualité (procédures et manuel) et mise en œuvre des standards d'entreprise.
  • Support lors des audits internes et externes ISO 9001.
  • Formation initiale qualité/SSE des nouveaux employés.
  • Révision des rapports de préoccupations initiales.
  • Ouverture, suivi et gestion des actions correctives (base de données Access, ETQ).

Expérience Requises :

•            Connaissance des produits Microsoft Office et bonnes compétences en informatique.

•            Une expérience d'un à deux ans dans le domaine de l'expédition et de la réception est souhaitable.

•            Anglais - Français - Bilingue

•            Fait preuve de précision et d'attention aux détails

•            Être en bonne forme physique pour rester debout pendant une longue période

•            Expérience dans l'utilisation de chariots élévateurs et d'équipements de levage

•            La connaissance d'un système ERP est un plus

 

Compétences/Exigences:

  • Licence en sciences de l'environnement, santé et sécurité au travail, hygiène industrielle, ingénierie ou domaine connexe.
  • Bilingue anglais - français.
  • Connaissance des réglementations EHS du Canada telles que OSHA, EPA et autres lois environnementales, de santé et de sécurité applicables.
  • Compréhension de la reconnaissance des dangers, de l'évaluation des risques et des mesures de contrôle.
  • Connaissance des pratiques de gestion de l'environnement, y compris la gestion des déchets, la qualité de l'air et de l'eau.
  • Maîtrise des logiciels de gestion EHS et des applications de bureau courantes (par exemple, la suite Microsoft Office).
  • Capacité à interpréter et à appliquer les politiques et procédures EHS.
  • Expérience dans la conduite d'audits et d'inspections EHS.
  • Compétences dans l'enquête d'incident et l'analyse de la cause première.
  • Démontre de la précision et une attention aux détails.
  • En bonne condition physique pour rester debout pendant de longues périodes.
  • Expérience de l'utilisation de chariots élévateurs et d'équipements de levage.
  • La connaissance d'un système ERP sera un plus.
  • Solides compétences en communication, à l'écrit et à l'oral, pour transmettre efficacement des informations aux employés, à la direction et aux parties prenantes externes.
  • Capacité à former et à impliquer les employés sur les sujets EHS.
  • Compétences analytiques et de résolution de problèmes pour identifier les dangers et développer des stratégies préventives.
  • Compétences en organisation et en gestion du temps pour gérer plusieurs tâches et échéances.
  • Capacité à travailler en équipe et à collaborer avec différents départements et niveaux de l'organisation.

Job Overview:

The EHS Specialist I plays a critical role in promoting a culture of safety and environmental responsibility within the organization. This individual collaborates with various departments to ensure that all activities are conducted in a safe and environmentally sound manner. They help to develop and enforce company policies and procedures that are in compliance with regulatory requirements and best practices in the industry

Responsibilities:

  • Developing, implementing and overseeing environment health and safety (EHS) policies, programs and procedures
  • Ensure the application and compliance with the standards and regulations regarding EHS
  • Promoting the company's EHS culture
  • Employee Training and Awareness
  • Implementation of Corporate Standard Work
  • Annual risk assessment
  • Work with contractors and subcontractors to ensure adherence to company policies and procedures.
  • Management EHS Committee and Green X Committee (sustainable environment)
  • Report and review EHS accidents/incidents including investigations of root cause and implement corrective actions
  • Premises Inspections and mange Compliance calendar in Gensuite
  • EHS Metrics Reporting and implement actions to reduce EHS risk to the business

Connected quality tasks:

  • Update of quality documents (procedures and manual) and implementation of corporate standards
  • Support during ISO 9001 internal and external audits
  • Initial quality/EHS training of new employees
  • Review of the initial concern reports
  • Opening, monitoring and management of corrective actions (Access DB, ETQ)

 

Skills/Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in environmental science, occupational health and safety, industrial hygiene, engineering, or related field
  • English - French – Bilingual
  • Familiarity with EHS Canada regulations such as OSHA, EPA, and other applicable environmental, health, and safety laws.
  • Understanding of hazard recognition, risk assessment, and control measures.
  • Knowledge of environmental management practices, including waste management, air quality, and water quality.
  • Proficiency in using EHS management software and common office applications (e.g., Microsoft Office Suite).
  • Ability to interpret and apply EHS policies and procedures.
  • Experience conducting EHS audits and inspections.
  • Skills in incident investigation and root cause analysis
  • Demonstrates accuracy and attention to detail
  • Physically fit to stand for a long period of time
  • Experience in using Forklifts and lifting equipment
  • Knowledge of an ERP system will be a plus
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, to effectively convey information to employees, management, and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to train and engage employees on EHS topics.

Emplacement du bureau: 190 Av. du Voyageur #100, Pointe-Claire, Québec H9R 6A

 

À propos de nous

Ingersoll Rand est une entreprise Fortune 500 passionnée par l'amélioration de la vie. Nous y parvenons en incarnant nos valeurs, en nous concentrant sans relâche sur la réussite de nos clients et en collaborant avec nos employés pour penser et agir comme des propriétaires. Nous croyons en la durabilité grâce au développement et à la distribution d'une large gamme de marques mondiales conçues pour répondre aux besoins de nos clients de manière efficace et responsable. Ingersoll Rand valorise un environnement diversifié et inclusif. Pour plus d'informations, visitez : www.irco.com.

Aperçu du poste
L’Électromécanicien spécialisé en machines rotatives est responsable de l’installation, l’entretien, la réparation et le diagnostic d’équipements tels que moteurs électriques, soufflantes, pompes, ventilateurs, compresseurs et autres systèmes rotatifs industriels.

Il effectue également la maintenance préventive et corrective, l’analyse vibratoire et contribue à l’amélioration de la fiabilité des équipements.

Responsabilités :

  • Installer, inspecter et réparer les équipements électromécaniques.
  • Effectuer l’entretien préventif et correctif des machines rotatives.
  • Effectuer des diagnostics de défaillance mécaniques, électriques, hydrauliques et pneumatiques.
  • Réaliser l’alignement laser ou au comparateur.
  • Lire et interpréter des plans mécaniques et schémas électriques.
  • Assurer les tests de fonctionnement après réparation.
  • Rédiger des rapports de maintenance et de service.
  • Respecter les normes de santé et de sécurité au travail.
  • Collaborer avec les équipes de production et d’ingénierie.
  • Utiliser des équipements de levage pour manipuler des pièces lourdes.
Compétences et exigences:

  • DEP en électromécanique, Mécanique industrielle, ou diplôme équivalent.
  •  2 à 5 ans d’expérience en maintenance industrielle (atout).
  •  Excellentes compétences en dépannage mécanique et électrique.
  •  Maîtrise des outils comme multimètre, analyseur de vibrations, tachymètre.
  •  Expérience en alignement laser (atout).
  •  Bonne condition physique
  • Compétences informatiques de base (Microsoft Office).
Ce que nous offrons
Chez Ingersoll Rand, nous promouvons une culture de responsabilité personnelle — en prenant soin de notre entreprise, de nos communautés et de notre environnement, ainsi que de notre santé et bien-être individuels. Notre programme complet d'avantages est conçu pour vous offrir les outils et le soutien nécessaires pour prendre en main votre santé, afin qu'ensemble, nous puissions continuer à améliorer la vie.

Notre gamme d'avantages comprend :

  • Culture responsabilisante : Encourager la responsabilité personnelle dans la réussite de notre entreprise, l'engagement communautaire et la protection de l'environnement.
  • Options de soins de santé : Plans complets de couverture médicale, dentaire et visuelle, ainsi que des assurances vie pour répondre à divers besoins de santé.
  • Programmes de bien-être : Ressources et initiatives pour soutenir votre bien-être global.
  • Plan d'épargne-retraite : Un plan solide avec des contributions de l'employeur pour sécuriser votre avenir.
  • Attribution d'actions aux employés : Une opportunité de partager la croissance et le succès de l'entreprise.
  • Congés payés : Pour vous assurer d'avoir le temps de vous ressourcer et de profiter de la vie en dehors du travail.
  • Environnement de soutien : Un programme d'avantages conçu pour vous aider à donner le meilleur de vous-même au travail et dans la vie.

Job Overview:

Ingersoll Rand has an exciting opportunity for a Project Manager at our Bentleyville, PA location. This position directly supports the Marine Division to ensure timely and effective project execution for new equipment and rebuilds per contract requirements.  

Responsibilities: 
    
Planning and Strategy Development:  Support sales on new project requests, align schedules & provide preliminary review of contract specifics prior to award.  Upon receipt of contracts, review to determine/finalize scope and related requirements, obtain necessary clarifications, communicate new orders to cross-functional team, monitor schedules to guide the team and stakeholders effectively, drive on-time delivery of documentation & equipment.  
Team Leadership and Coordination:  Guide cross-functional team through project execution from contract award to final acceptance, assign & drive completion of tasks, develop new processes & tools for improved management of contracts, clarify roles & responsibilities of team members including setting priorities, and ensure collaboration among team members, customers, and suppliers.

Risk Identification and Mitigation:  Identify & manage risks to cost, schedule, and revenue, develop & implement contingency, corrective action, and preventative action plans while driving process improvement & efficiency.

Quality Assurance and Documentation:  Identify contract requirements & communicate to team, support quality team to ensure quality requirements are being met internally & at suppliers, work to implement corrective actions when quality deficiencies arise, and review/certify final quality documentation prior to submittal to ensure timely acceptance.
Other responsibilities as assigned or required.

Aperçu du poste
L’Électromécanicien spécialisé en machines rotatives est responsable de l’installation, l’entretien, la réparation et le diagnostic d’équipements tels que moteurs électriques, soufflantes, pompes, ventilateurs, compresseurs et autres systèmes rotatifs industriels.

  •  Maîtrise des outils comme multimètre, analyseur de vibrations, tachymètre.

Job Title: Mechanical Engineer, Design Development               
Location:  Bentleyville, PA
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a Mechanical Engineer, Design Development role with Ingersoll Rand’s Bentleyville, Pennsylvania site—a key North American engineering and packaging hub for Nash and MD Kinney liquid-ring vacuum pumps and compressors. The team supports a broad portfolio of rotating-equipment designs, global manufacturing, and U.S. service operations, with responsibility spanning product engineering, design support, packaging, and lifecycle support.

In this role, you’ll take meaningful ownership of complex rotating equipment within two established, market-leading product brands. You will support the design, development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of commercial liquid-ring vacuum pumps and compressors, including engineering changes, product data and documentation, manufacturing support, and technical collaboration with Quality, Operations, Service, Sales, and Product Management. You’ll contribute to both current product support and new product development, helping improve performance, reduce cost without compromising reliability, expand CFD capability, and advance proven technology into its next generation. Whether you’re early in your engineering career and ready for greater development ownership, or you’ve taken a broader path into mechanical/product design, this role offers room to grow your technical depth and impact.

What makes you an instant-yes candidate? You take ownership, work independently, stay organized, communicate effectively across teams, and keep projects moving with the right priorities and attention to detail. Technically, you bring a strong mechanical foundation and an interest in understanding the mechanics, assembly, and operation of rotating equipment. You can perform engineering calculations and analysis and are proficient in 3D CAD. Experience with FEA/CFD, vibration, fluid dynamics, troubleshooting, ERP/BOM ownership, or Ansys adds value. Direct Nash or MD Kinney experience is not required—a strong mechanical design and problem-solving foundation, combined with the ability to quickly develop deeper analytical skills, can be equally valuable.

Bring your mechanical design development expertise, curiosity, and ownership mindset—and help take proven Nash and MD Kinney technology into its next generation.

Responsibilities:
  • Support commercial liquid-ring vacuum pump and compressor product lines through product engineering, design improvements, performance evaluation, manufacturing support, and documentation.
  • Develop and maintain strong product knowledge across assigned configurations, components, applications, engineering data, and legacy/current platforms.
  • Execute product design and development activities from concept and design review through prototype support, validation, implementation, and release.
  • Improve product designs to enhance performance, reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, and cost effectiveness.
  • Create and maintain 3D CAD models, drawings, specifications, design layouts, bills of material, and supporting engineering records.
  • Prepare and implement ECRs, ECNs, drawing revisions, BOM updates, and product data changes, maintaining accurate engineering change histories.
  • Analyze test results, product performance, manufacturing feedback, field service data, and quality concerns to drive troubleshooting, corrective actions, and design improvements.
  • Partner with Manufacturing, Quality, Operations, Sourcing, Customer Service, Field Service, Sales, and Product Management, while managing multiple priorities and supporting authorized government, defense, or export-controlled projects as assigned.

Requirements
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive experience in rotating equipment design, mechanical product design, industrial equipment design, or manufacturing engineering.
  • 2+ years experience maintaining engineering data within an ERP system, such as SAP.
  • 2+ years working knowledge of manufacturing processes to include machining, casting, fabrication, assembly, and rotating equipment design principles.
  • 1+ year of experience using 3D CAD software, ideally Autodesk Inventor.

Core Competencies 
  • Ownership & Accountability – Takes responsibility for assigned products, including design integrity, documentation accuracy, product performance, and continuous improvement.
  • Analytical Problem Solving – Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate technical issues, interpret data, and apply sound engineering judgment.
  • Mechanical Engineering Judgment – Applies sound mechanical engineering principles to balance performance, reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, and cost.
  • Data-Driven Decision Making – Uses engineering analysis, testing, manufacturing feedback, and field performance data to guide decisions and improvements.
  • Attention to Detail – Maintains accuracy across engineering documentation, bills of material, technical records, and change management.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Communicates effectively and works collaboratively with engineering, manufacturing, quality, service, sourcing, and other stakeholders.

Preferences: 
  • Experience with vacuum pumps, compressors, liquid ring equipment, or other rotating fluid machinery.
  • Experience applying mechanical products to customer operating conditions, performance requirements, or industrial process applications.
  • Experience with Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) software, including ANSYS and/or Simerics MP+.
  • Experience with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools; Windchill preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and compressible flow principles.
  • Experience with vibration analysis and/or acoustic analysis.

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • On-site position based in Bentleyville, PA.
  • Must hold US Citizenship due to assigned government engineering activies
  • Occasional travel may be required to support customers, suppliers, manufacturing facilities, or project activities.
  • Support for global product initiatives may be required as business needs dictate.

What We Offer 
Our benefits –At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Job Overview:
Step into a Quality Engineer role with Gardner Denver – Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, a division of Ingersoll Rand, where your work directly impacts product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia operation. You’ll help ensure products meet exacting quality standards while supporting the transformation of metal castings and raw materials into high-performing products used around the world.  In this highly collaborative role, you’ll serve as a key problem-solving partner across manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, and purchasing. Using the plant Quality Management System, you’ll respond to quality issues, lead root cause analysis, identify risks, and drive corrective and preventive actions that strengthen product reliability, reduce defects, and support continuous improvement across the plant.

Responsibilities:

  • Process Development and Improvement: Develop, implement, and document process improvements to ensure quality and reliability. Quality project lead representative, as assigned, for new product introductions. Identifies production concerns and take proactive steps to correct problems. 
  • Documentation: Initiates and maintains documentation as needed to support process and manufacturing improvements (i.e. Process Control, Inspection logs, Visual Work Instructions, ECN's) 
  • Quality: Develops and maintains all departmental procedures supporting and maintaining ISO certification. Participate in internal and external periodic plant audits. Support plant internal corrective actions. 
  • Suppliers: Respond/ investigate quality related issues found on the production floor, or at the customer's location. Communicate with suppliers on non-conforming material, and issue/ manage supplier corrective actions as necessary. 
  • Other responsibilities as assigned or directed. 

Requirements:
  • 5+ years of relevant progressive quality experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree.
  • 3+ years of relevant quality experience within a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years experience with MS Office Suite, to include intermediate Excel skills
  • 1+ year of experience working with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Core Competencies:
  • Quality Systems & Compliance
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, maintain, and support quality procedures, documentation, and plant-level quality systems in alignment with ISO certification, regulatory requirements, and customer expectations.
  • Structured Problem Solving & Root Cause Analysis
  • Ability to respond to quality issues as they occur, investigate non-conformances, apply root cause analysis tools, and drive corrective and preventive actions that improve product reliability and reduce defects.
  • Process Improvement & Manufacturing Support
  • Experience identifying production concerns, developing and documenting process improvements, and partnering with manufacturing teams to strengthen quality, reliability, and operational performance.
  • Cross-Functional & Supplier Collaboration
  • Ability to work effectively with manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, purchasing, and suppliers to resolve quality concerns, manage supplier corrective actions, and ensure customer quality requirements are met.
  • Documentation, Data & Systems Proficiency
  • Strong ability to create, maintain, and manage quality-related documentation, including process controls, inspection logs, visual work instructions, ECNs, and corrective action records, while utilizing MS Office, Excel, and ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors Degree or some college with relevant quality engineering experience
  • Experience with Lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement initiatives
  • ASQ certification (e.g., CQT, CQE, CQM, or CRE)
  • Six Sigma Green Belt certification

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This is based onsite in Sedalia, MO
  • Travel anticipated is less than 10%

The team supports a broad portfolio of rotating-equipment designs, global manufacturing, and U.S. service operations, with responsibility spanning product engineering, design support, packaging, and lifecycle support.

In this role, you’ll take meaningful ownership of complex rotating equipment within two established, market-leading product brands. You will support the design, development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of commercial liquid-ring vacuum pumps and compressors, including engineering changes, product data and documentation, manufacturing support, and technical collaboration with Quality, Operations, Service, Sales, and Product Management. You’ll contribute to both current product support and new product development, helping improve performance, reduce cost without compromising reliability, expand CFD capability, and advance proven technology into its next generation. Whether you’re early in your engineering career and ready for greater development ownership, or you’ve taken a broader path into mechanical/product design, this role offers room to grow your technical depth and impact.

What makes you an instant-yes candidate? You take ownership, work independently, stay organized, communicate effectively across teams, and keep projects moving with the right priorities and attention to detail. Technically, you bring a strong mechanical foundation and an interest in understanding the mechanics, assembly, and operation of rotating equipment. You can perform engineering calculations and analysis and are proficient in 3D CAD. Experience with FEA/CFD, vibration, fluid dynamics, troubleshooting, ERP/BOM ownership, or Ansys adds value. Direct Nash or MD Kinney experience is not required—a strong mechanical design and problem-solving foundation, combined with the ability to quickly develop deeper analytical skills, can be equally valuable.

Bring your mechanical design development expertise, curiosity, and ownership mindset—and help take proven Nash and MD Kinney technology into its next generation.

  • Create and maintain 3D CAD models, drawings, specifications, design layouts, bills of material, and supporting engineering records.
  • Prepare and implement ECRs, ECNs, drawing revisions, BOM updates, and product data changes, maintaining accurate engineering change histories.
  • Analyze test results, product performance, manufacturing feedback, field service data, and quality concerns to drive troubleshooting, corrective actions, and design improvements.
  • Partner with Manufacturing, Quality, Operations, Sourcing, Customer Service, Field Service, Sales, and Product Management, while managing multiple priorities and supporting authorized government, defense, or export-controlled projects as assigned.

Job Overview:
Step into a Quality Engineer role with Gardner Denver – Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, a division of Ingersoll Rand, where your work directly impacts product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia operation. You’ll help ensure products meet exacting quality standards while supporting the transformation of metal castings and raw materials into high-performing products used around the world.  In this highly collaborative role, you’ll serve as a key problem-solving partner across manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, and purchasing. Using the plant Quality Management System, you’ll respond to quality issues, lead root cause analysis, identify risks, and drive corrective and preventive actions that strengthen product reliability, reduce defects, and support continuous improvement across the plant.

Responsibilities:

  • Process Development and Improvement: Develop, implement, and document process improvements to ensure quality and reliability. Quality project lead representative, as assigned, for new product introductions. Identifies production concerns and take proactive steps to correct problems. 
  • Documentation: Initiates and maintains documentation as needed to support process and manufacturing improvements (i.e. Process Control, Inspection logs, Visual Work Instructions, ECN's) 
  • Quality: Develops and maintains all departmental procedures supporting and maintaining ISO certification. Participate in internal and external periodic plant audits. Support plant internal corrective actions. 
  • Suppliers: Respond/ investigate quality related issues found on the production floor, or at the customer's location. Communicate with suppliers on non-conforming material, and issue/ manage supplier corrective actions as necessary. 
  • Other responsibilities as assigned or directed. 

Requirements:
  • 5+ years of relevant progressive quality experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree.
  • 3+ years of relevant quality experience within a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years experience with MS Office Suite, to include intermediate Excel skills
  • 1+ year of experience working with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Core Competencies:
  • Quality Systems & Compliance
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, maintain, and support quality procedures, documentation, and plant-level quality systems in alignment with ISO certification, regulatory requirements, and customer expectations.
  • Structured Problem Solving & Root Cause Analysis
  • Ability to respond to quality issues as they occur, investigate non-conformances, apply root cause analysis tools, and drive corrective and preventive actions that improve product reliability and reduce defects.
  • Process Improvement & Manufacturing Support
  • Experience identifying production concerns, developing and documenting process improvements, and partnering with manufacturing teams to strengthen quality, reliability, and operational performance.
  • Cross-Functional & Supplier Collaboration
  • Ability to work effectively with manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, purchasing, and suppliers to resolve quality concerns, manage supplier corrective actions, and ensure customer quality requirements are met.
  • Documentation, Data & Systems Proficiency
  • Strong ability to create, maintain, and manage quality-related documentation, including process controls, inspection logs, visual work instructions, ECNs, and corrective action records, while utilizing MS Office, Excel, and ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or similar platforms.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors Degree or some college with relevant quality engineering experience
  • Experience with Lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement initiatives
  • ASQ certification (e.g., CQT, CQE, CQM, or CRE)
  • Six Sigma Green Belt certification

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This is based onsite in Sedalia, MO
  • Travel anticipated is less than 10%

Job Overview:
Step into a Mechanical Engineer, Design Development role with Ingersoll Rand’s Bentleyville, Pennsylvania site—a key North American engineering and packaging hub for Nash and MD Kinney liquid-ring vacuum pumps and compressors. The team supports a broad portfolio of rotating-equipment designs, global manufacturing, and U.S. service operations, with responsibility spanning product engineering, design support, packaging, and lifecycle support.

In this role, you’ll take meaningful ownership of complex rotating equipment within two established, market-leading product brands. You will support the design, development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of commercial liquid-ring vacuum pumps and compressors, including engineering changes, product data and documentation, manufacturing support, and technical collaboration with Quality, Operations, Service, Sales, and Product Management. You’ll contribute to both current product support and new product development, helping improve performance, reduce cost without compromising reliability, expand CFD capability, and advance proven technology into its next generation. Whether you’re early in your engineering career and ready for greater development ownership, or you’ve taken a broader path into mechanical/product design, this role offers room to grow your technical depth and impact.

What makes you an instant-yes candidate? You take ownership, work independently, stay organized, communicate effectively across teams, and keep projects moving with the right priorities and attention to detail. Technically, you bring a strong mechanical foundation and an interest in understanding the mechanics, assembly, and operation of rotating equipment. You can perform engineering calculations and analysis and are proficient in 3D CAD. Experience with FEA/CFD, vibration, fluid dynamics, troubleshooting, ERP/BOM ownership, or Ansys adds value. Direct Nash or MD Kinney experience is not required—a strong mechanical design and problem-solving foundation, combined with the ability to quickly develop deeper analytical skills, can be equally valuable.

Bring your mechanical design development expertise, curiosity, and ownership mindset—and help take proven Nash and MD Kinney technology into its next generation.

Responsibilities:
  • Support commercial liquid-ring vacuum pump and compressor product lines through product engineering, design improvements, performance evaluation, manufacturing support, and documentation.
  • Develop and maintain strong product knowledge across assigned configurations, components, applications, engineering data, and legacy/current platforms.
  • Execute product design and development activities from concept and design review through prototype support, validation, implementation, and release.
  • Improve product designs to enhance performance, reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, and cost effectiveness.
  • Create and maintain 3D CAD models, drawings, specifications, design layouts, bills of material, and supporting engineering records.
  • Prepare and implement ECRs, ECNs, drawing revisions, BOM updates, and product data changes, maintaining accurate engineering change histories.
  • Analyze test results, product performance, manufacturing feedback, field service data, and quality concerns to drive troubleshooting, corrective actions, and design improvements.
  • Partner with Manufacturing, Quality, Operations, Sourcing, Customer Service, Field Service, Sales, and Product Management, while managing multiple priorities and supporting authorized government, defense, or export-controlled projects as assigned.

Requirements
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive experience in rotating equipment design, mechanical product design, industrial equipment design, or manufacturing engineering.
  • 2+ years experience maintaining engineering data within an ERP system, such as SAP.
  • 2+ years working knowledge of manufacturing processes to include machining, casting, fabrication, assembly, and rotating equipment design principles.
  • 1+ year of experience using 3D CAD software, ideally Autodesk Inventor.

Core Competencies 
  • Ownership & Accountability – Takes responsibility for assigned products, including design integrity, documentation accuracy, product performance, and continuous improvement.
  • Analytical Problem Solving – Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate technical issues, interpret data, and apply sound engineering judgment.
  • Mechanical Engineering Judgment – Applies sound mechanical engineering principles to balance performance, reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, and cost.
  • Data-Driven Decision Making – Uses engineering analysis, testing, manufacturing feedback, and field performance data to guide decisions and improvements.
  • Attention to Detail – Maintains accuracy across engineering documentation, bills of material, technical records, and change management.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Communicates effectively and works collaboratively with engineering, manufacturing, quality, service, sourcing, and other stakeholders.

Preferences: 
  • Experience with vacuum pumps, compressors, liquid ring equipment, or other rotating fluid machinery.
  • Experience applying mechanical products to customer operating conditions, performance requirements, or industrial process applications.
  • Experience with Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) software, including ANSYS and/or Simerics MP+.
  • Experience with Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools; Windchill preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and compressible flow principles.
  • Experience with vibration analysis and/or acoustic analysis.

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • On-site position based in Bentleyville, PA.
  • Must hold US Citizenship due to assigned government engineering activies
  • Occasional travel may be required to support customers, suppliers, manufacturing facilities, or project activities.
  • Support for global product initiatives may be required as business needs dictate.

Job Overview:
As the Quality Manager, you'll lead the Quality Department, playing a pivotal role in the local leadership team. Your primary responsibility will be ensuring compliance with ISO-9001 International Quality Standards, developing and maintaining all ISO 9001 procedures and audits at our facility. Collaborating closely with Procurement, you'll guarantee that external suppliers, both domestic and international, deliver raw materials and components that meet our engineering and purchasing specifications. We're seeking a candidate who can serve as a player-coach in a dynamic machining manufacturing environment, fostering effective collaboration with key stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Supervise Quality Team and oversee plant warranty administration.
  • Create and foster a highly engaged and performing team, through strategic talent and engagement plans.
  • Manage plant compliance with ISO-9001 and ISO-14001 Quality System standards, coordinating ISO visits and managing corrective actions from external audits.
  • Drive improvement of First Pass-Yield data, supplier scorecards, warranty trends, and other quality metrics.
  • Manage key processes such as 4D/8D, SCAR, CAPA to enhance Customer Satisfaction and improve Supplier performance.
  • Develop and implement effective quality control processes aligned with customer needs and requirements.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Operations, Purchasing, Engineering, and Customer Service Teams to address customer and production issues for product portfolio (legacy and/or new products).
  • Partner with Manufacturing Engineers to troubleshoot and resolve quality-related production issues.
  • Collaborate with external vendors to enhance manufacturing processes for purchased components.
  • Actively engage in Kaizen Events and Lean activities to improve quality and reduce manufacturing waste and costs.
  • Utilize advanced Quality Assurance techniques (FMEA, CMM Inspection, GD&T, Gage R&R Studies, Process Capability Studies, Six Sigma, statistical quality/process control methods) to proactively manage product quality.
Requirements:

  • Bachelor's Degree in related field (Mechanical/Industrial Engineering).
  • 8+ years of quality assurance experience, ideally in a machining/assembly facility.
  • 5+ years of progressive leadership, managing quality assurance programs and leading audits.
  • 1+ years of experience in Manufacturing/Quality Engineering in machining manufacturing, utilizing Lean Six Sigma techniques.
  • 1+ years of experience in regulatory accreditation processes (UL, CE, ATEX, IECEx, CSA, CSA-UK, TUV, NSF, RoHS, REACH, Prop 65, ITAR, and related).
  • 1+ years of experience in managing and implementing quality control procedures and relevant standards.
  • 1+ years of experience with ERP systems.

Preferences:
  • Engineering Management preferred
  • SAP experience preferred
Core Competencies:

  • Demonstrated mechanical aptitude and knowledge of general machinery.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with advanced proficiency in Microsoft Suite.
  • Leads Authentically: Exhibits a poised and calm demeanor that instills confidence and respect, while embodying humility and consideration for others. Advocates for the organization's mission and values authentically.
  • Project Management: Proven track record in effectively managing projects, adept at organizing tasks and optimizing time management to handle multiple assignments concurrently within set timelines and budget constraints.
  • Decisiveness and Results Orientation: Demonstrates the ability to make timely decisions with creativity and sound judgment. Utilizes rigorous logic and problem-solving methods to devise effective solutions for complex issues. Capable of articulating rationale clearly and compellingly, ensuring understanding and buy-in from stakeholders. Consistently delivers on commitments.
  • Customer Focus: Committed to meeting the needs and expectations of both internal and external customers, ensuring their satisfaction remains a top priority.

  • Onsite

Job title: Supplier Quality Engineer
Location: Bentleyville, PA


Job Overview:

Our Ingersoll Rand/Nash Marine Division In Bentleyville, PA, is looking for a Supplier Quality Engineer III? to join our team!  The Supplier Quality Engineer III works under limited supervision, responsible for performing a variety of duties efficiently with high-quality results. The Supplier Quality Engineer will be expected to perform duties as Supplier Quality Engineer and Quality Engineer.  

Responsibilities:

  • Review commercial and DoD contracts for quality/compliance requirements, including customer flow-down clauses and coded notes.
  • Maintain quality documentation, certifications, and order control folders; verify and file Certificates of Conformance (CoC) and material certifications.
  • Process non-conforming material reports, quality notifications, root cause investigations, and corrective/preventive actions.
  • Prepare and maintain First Article Inspection (FAI) documentation.
  • Partner with Engineering and Assembly teams to troubleshoot issues, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions.
  • Perform final inspections to ensure products meet customer, contract, and quality requirements.
  • Process SAP Warehouse Management and Inventory transactions; maintain accurate material storage locations.

This sales role will focus on the selling of lifecycle-centric service agreements, aftermarket part subscriptions, and long-term maintenance programs specifically targeting municipalities and large corporate accounts. The Business Development Manager will serve as a strategic contributor in growing aftermarket services through recurring revenue programs, strengthening customer relationships, and increasing share of wallet through long-term value creation. This sales position plays a critical role in advancing PFT’s aftermarket strategy and improving customer retention, and will partner cross functionally with Sales, Aftermarket, Service Operations, Product Management, and Engineering personnel to identify, develop, and scale value-added recurring revenue opportunities across new and existing customers.

  • Meet or exceed assigned recurring revenue targets, profitability objectives, and growth metrics.
  • Engage strategically with key accounts to position PFT as a lifecycle partner, not solely an equipment provider, to influence customer decision-making by articulating the value of recurring offerings tied to reliability, uptime, efficiency, and total cost of ownership.

  • Strong understanding of maintenance strategies, reliability-centered service solutions, lifecycle asset management, long-term value creation and contract renewal management.

Job Overview:
The Business Development Manager (BDM), Data Centers for the Fluid Transfer Technologies (FTT) business unit is responsible for driving growth with a primary focus on expanding  presence in the data center liquid cooling market.  This role leads business development efforts for pumps and fluid transfer solutions used in applications such as Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs), liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air cooling systems, secondary coolant loops, and facility-level thermal management.

The BDM, Data Centers builds and develops relationships across the data center value chain to drive specification wins, new business opportunities, and long-term growth in mission-critical cooling applications. While the role is predominantly data center–focused, it also supports select strategic channel expansion initiatives aligned with broader FTT growth priorities.

The ideal candidate has direct experience in the data center market, particularly in liquid cooling, thermal systems, HVAC/mechanical infrastructure, pumps, or flow control technologies.

Responsibilities:
Data Center Market Development & Specification Influence

  • Build and grow relationships with CDU builders, mechanical engineers, consulting engineering firms, and facility engineering teams to drive specification of FTT components in data center cooling systems.
  • Identify opportunities across hyperscale, colocation, enterprise, and HPC data centers.
  • Influence early-stage design for primary and secondary coolant loops, pump skids, thermal transfer systems, dielectric fluid platforms, and facility water systems.
  • Map buying centers across owner/operators, OEMs, integrators, and EPC firms to maximize influence on infrastructure design and procurement.

Channel Expansion & Strategic Partnerships

  • Identify, evaluate, and onboard distribution partners, system integrators, resellers, and strategic partners aligned with FTT’s growth strategy in data center infrastructure and thermal management.
  • Develop and execute channel strategies and development plans that support stocking models, demand forecasting, service capabilities, and technical readiness to drive market penetration and revenue growth across North America.
  • Analyze the competitive landscape to identify differentiation opportunities, underserved markets, and whitespace for FTT’s thermal solutions.
  • Establish partner agreements, performance expectations, and incentive programs to ensure profitable and scalable growth.

Commercial Execution & Sales Enablement

  • Build go-to-market strategies tailored to data center liquid cooling applications.
  • Train sales teams, distributors, and OEM partners on performance characteristics, coolant compatibility, reliability metrics, flow requirements, and key data-center specific use cases.
  • Partner closely with Sales, Product Management, and Marketing to support customer engagement, proposal development, and major project pursuit.

Strategic Growth & Portfolio Expansion

  • Build and maintain a strong pipeline of growth opportunities across OEMs, EPC firms, liquid cooling integrators, industrial distribution, specialty resellers, mechanical contractors, and facility upgrades.

Job Overview:
The Quality Manager is responsible for managing and implementing the Quality Management System and processes across the site. This position oversees quality assurance, and compliance functions and ensures integration throughout departments to ensure the Quality Management System (QMS) is compliant to standards and products meet quality specifications. The Quality Manager supervises and guides team members following Flexan LLC performance management practices and policies. Assures consistent quality of production by developing and enforcing good systems, validating processes, providing good documentation, and managing staff.

Responsibilities:

  • Develops, maintains and executes quality procedures to inspect and report quality issues 
  • Oversees maintenance of the requirements and monitors the effectiveness of the ISO quality system as well as continually proposing improvements to the system 
  • Oversee the management of the QMS to ensure compliance with relevant regulatory bodies. 
  • Accomplishes quality assurance human resource objectives by recruiting, selecting, orienting, training, scheduling, coaching, counseling, and disciplining employees; communicates job expectations and leads team in talent and performance management processes 
  • Responsible for understanding customer needs and requirements to develop effective quality control processes 
  • Hosts customer and regulatory audits, as well as coordinates and performs internal quality and supplier audits as needed 
  • Leads all internal and external CAPAs, Non-Conforming Reports, and customer complaints including investigation, root cause analysis, and other related documentation. 
  • Ensures all document control and revision control activities are carried out to ensure compliance 
  • Ensures all products conform to validated processes and Device Master Records, as well as performs lot release and related functions 
  • Assures the reliability and consistency of production by checking processes and final output 
  • Provides oversight of calibration and preventive maintenance program to ensure compliance 
  • Collaborates with purchasing department and co-manages the approved supplier list and evaluates them to ensure product compliance 
  • Monitors approved supplier list and rates suppliers through score card ratings 
  • Ensures all SOP’s and process documentation are created in accordance with the QMS and works with all departments to ensure effectiveness 
  • Provide resources, support, ideas and recommendations to facilitate growth of a “culture of quality” 
  • Living the IR Values

 
Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.  A degree in quality, mechanical, or industrial engineering preferred.
  • 8+ years minimum overall experience in quality assurance and quality control
  • 1+ years of experience within medical device, pharmaceutical or related highly regulated environments required

Job title: Electrical Engineer

Location: Monroe, LA (On-site) 

 

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview: 

The Electrical Engineer is responsible for the development, optimization, troubleshooting, and long-term support of manufacturing test systems used in end-of-line (EOL) testing of pumps, compressors, motors, and related products. The position also supports laboratory instrumentation including pressure, temperature, flow, and electrical measurement systems and provides electrical and controls engineering support to plant maintenance and manufacturing teams. This role partners closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, and Operations teams to improve product validation processes, increase test system reliability, enhance data collection capabilities, and ensure products consistently meet customer and quality requirements. 

 

Responsibilities: 

  • Design, develop, implement, and maintain electrical and automated end-of-line test systems used to validate product performance, safety, and quality requirements prior to shipment.
  • Develop and support LabVIEW, National Instruments, PLC-based, and data acquisition systems used for manufacturing and laboratory testing.
  • Troubleshoot and improve electrical test equipment, instrumentation, sensors, controls, drives, and data collection systems to maximize uptime and test accuracy.
  • Support pressure, temperature, flow, electrical, vibration, and performance measurement systems used in manufacturing and product qualification testing.
  • Partner with Quality and Manufacturing teams to investigate test failures, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions to improve product quality and first-pass yield.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on test automation, process capability, cycle-time reduction, reliability, and operational efficiency.
  • Support new product introductions by developing test methodologies, validation plans, fixtures, work instructions, and production support processes.
  • Provide electrical engineering support to plant operations, maintenance, and capital projects, including equipment upgrades and modernization initiatives. 

 

Requirements: 

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in manufacturing, automation, controls, or test/industrial electrical engineering, including hands-on development, maintenance, or troubleshooting of automated test equipment and electrical measurement systems.
  • 3+ years with LabVIEW and National Instruments hardware/software platforms, with hands-on exposure to industrial instrumentation (pressure, temperature, flow, vibration, power measurement)
  • 1+ years supporting end-of-line testing in a high-volume manufacturing environment


Core Competencies:  

  • Manufacturing Test System Expertise
  • Continuous Improvement
  • Root Cause Analysis and Problem Solving
  • Data-Driven Decision Making
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Customer and Quality Focus 

 

Preferences: 

  • Experience supporting end-of-line testing in a high-volume manufacturing environment.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, project management, and cross-functional communication skills. 
  • Knowledge of electrical controls, PLCs, VFDs, motors, sensors, industrial communications, and data acquisition systems.
  • Experience with pumps, compressors, rotating equipment, or industrial machinery.
  • Knowledge of electrical safety standards, risk assessments, system validation, and design verification testing.

 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position is fully site-based at the Monroe, Louisiana manufacturing facility.
    • Occasional travel may be required to support equipment suppliers, training activities, customer requirements, or other business needs.
