Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.

  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.

Requirements:

  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required. 

Core Competencies: 

  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner.

Preferences:

  • 2 years+ industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • Degree program in Electrical/Electronic Technology or HVAC with basic knowledge of some or all of the following: AC/DC circuits, wiring diagrams/schematics, motors/controls, PLCs, HVAC electricity, controls, refrigeration systems and/or refrigerant certification or EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply. 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • This position may require occasional travel for training.  1-2 times per year for one week at a time.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Job Title: IoT Field Engineer

Location: Remote, US

About Us
Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry's most difficult problems.

EcoPlant is our pioneering SaaS technology division and is at the forefront of innovation. Harnessing the power of Internet of Things (IoT) technology and predictive analytics, we seamlessly automate air compressor systems, elevating energy efficiency, boosting system reliability, and enhancing off-site productivity. We're leading the charge in a sustainable industrial revolution, where cutting-edge technology meets eco-friendly solutions, transforming the very essence of how factories operate.

Job Overview: 
There's a sustainability movement underway in manufacturing that leverages control systems to proactively monitor mission-critical equipment, evaluating and improving efficiency while predicting and preventing downtime and equipment failures. If you're looking to be at the leading edge of that progress, we're seeking a technically skilled and self-driven IoT Field Engineer to join our growing EcoPlant deployment team.

As an IoT Field Engineer, you will own the on-site installation and commissioning of EcoPlant hardware, ensuring each system is properly installed, connected, and communicating data before you leave the customer site. A strong mechanical and technical aptitude, as well as familiarity with computers and networking fundamentals, and the ability to work independently and resolve issues on your own, is necessary in this position as you will frequently be the sole Ecoplant representative on-site.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the On-Site Installation: Take ownership of each EcoPlant installation, delivering high-quality workmanship that performs reliably in demanding industrial environments. You will frequently work independently as the on-site EcoPlant representative.
  • Install Instrumentation and Sensors: Install the field instrumentation that feeds data to the EcoPlant platform, including air sensors and power monitoring equipment. Terminate and land wiring to its respective locations in accordance with provided documents for Ethernet, Modbus, discrete I/O, etc., while maintaining clean connections and reliable signal integrity.
  • Deploy Edge Hardware: Mount and install edge devices, provision power, and position cellular antennas for optimal signal quality,
  • Commission and Verify Connectivity: Configure network settings, confirm each device is communicating as expected, validate that data is flowing into the platform, and coordinate with technical support to resolve any connectivity issues prior to site departure.
  • Maintain Documentation: Produce accurate records, redlines, and photographs to support the development and maintenance of each site’s P&ID and system diagram.
  • Adhere to Safety Standards: Follow site and standard electrical safety practices, including lockout/tagout (LOTO) and appropriate PPE, when working around energized equipment and pressurized compressed air systems.


Requirements

  • High School Diploma and/or combination of education
  • 2+ years’ related industrial controls installation experience required.
  • 2+ years’ experience deploying IoT and/or edge hardware in industrial environments.



Core Competencies:

  • Demonstrated mechanical and technical aptitude, with the ability to work hands-on and reason through how systems integrate. Relevant experience may come from field service, a technical degree, and/or substantial hands-on technical experience.
  • Familiarity with computers and networking fundamentals, including configuring network interfaces (i.e. understanding of how IP addressing/subnetting works), and basic Linux/ Windows command-line navigation.
  • Demonstrated understanding of IoT communication protocols (such as Modbus, CANbus, Profibus, and discrete I/O), networking, and data security.
  • Ability to read and work from schematics, P&IDs, and wiring diagrams, including terminating and landing wiring to terminals per drawings.
  • Understanding of network communications and protocols, switches, routers, and mobile equipment.
  • Electrical troubleshooting experience and comfort working with low-voltage control wiring.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and resolve issues independently in the field.
  • Exceptional customer service skills coupled with the ability to work collaboratively with internal teams to achieve a shared mission.
  • Proven ability to work independently — self-driven, organized, and able to manage an installation from start to finish with minimal supervision.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Physical demands: This position requires working in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, heights, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage).  This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.


Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related technical field, such as Engineering or Engineering Technology.
  • Experience with industrial compressed air systems.
  • Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) certification.
  • A genuine interest in developing technically within the industrial automation and IoT space.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position is eligible for remote work in the continental United States.
  • Interested candidates should have access to a major airport for travel.
  • Extensive travel across North America required (up to 75%)


Pay Range 
The total pay range for this role is $85,000 - $135,000. The actual pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. Shift: 1st Shift (Monday-Friday 6am-2:30pm)
Pay: Starting rate at $23.00-$28.00 per hour 

 

Job Summary

We are seeking a skilled Assembler to perform a variety of tasks associated with the rebuilding and assembly of Gas End compressors. This position is responsible for ensuring all parts fit correctly, meet quality standards, and are suitable for the final product.

The ideal candidate will possess strong technical knowledge, excellent manual dexterity, and the ability to interpret and follow instructions from manuals, drawings, blueprints, and schematics with precision. This role also requires the use of computer systems to record safety test data, inspection reports, and production-related information. Assignments may vary based on business needs.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Disassemble, clean, inspect, and rebuild Gas End compressors using a combination of new and reusable parts.
  • Read, understand, and follow method sheets, assembly diagrams, blueprints, and technical drawings.
  • Identify quality defects and unsafe conditions.
  • Follow all applicable safety rules, policies, and procedures.
  • Interpret print drawings to determine dimensions, design specifications, and required materials.
  • Safely operate pneumatic, power, and hand tools required to perform job duties.
  • Use measuring devices such as tape measures, levels, and other inspection tools.
  • Maintain and inspect tools and equipment and create work orders for necessary repairs.
  • Load and unload materials using conveyors, carts, forklifts, hoists, and other material-handling equipment.
  • Collaborate with team members and support other departments as needed.
  • Suggest process improvements that enhance safety, quality, and productivity.
  • Maintain a safe, clean, and organized work environment.
  • Monitor inventory levels and assist with material replenishment and receiving activities.
  • Assemble components and subassemblies by examining connections for proper fit and fastening parts securely.
  • Perform general housekeeping duties within the work area.
  • Complete production-related tasks, including but not limited to pipe bending, sledging, operating presses, hanging and unhanging parts, and conducting quality inspections and tests.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Supervisor or Team Leader.
 

Requirements

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • Fully trained and qualified to train others on multiple products in accordance with the company training matrix.
  • Ability to participate in 5 Why root cause analyses and implement corrective actions for process and product-related issues.
 

Core Competencies

  • Commitment to following all company policies, procedures, and safety guidelines.
  • Ability to use sound judgment and prior experience to plan and accomplish assigned tasks.
  • Ability to learn and safely operate equipment associated with the role, including power hand tools, forklifts, skyjacks, cranes, and measuring devices.
  • Ability to identify routine issues, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions.
  • Working knowledge of standard work instructions and manufacturing processes.
  • Strong teamwork and collaboration skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a manufacturing environment.
  • Detail-oriented and self-motivated with a strong work ethic.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, multitasking environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in a LeRoi manufacturing environment preferred; equivalent experience with compressor or air recovery product assembly will also be considered.
  • Proficient in the use of hand tools, including wrenches, sockets, hammers, tape measures, crimpers, cutters, steel banding tools, pipe benders, saws, and threading equipment.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and understanding of manufacturing processes.
  • Experience using power tools safely and effectively.
  • Proficiency with computer systems and material management processes.

job.title: Technical Inside Sales Western Canada
job.description:
Job Title: Technical Inside Sales Representative, Western Canada
Location: Acheson, Alberta (Edmonton Area)
Employment Type: Full-Time | Onsite

About Us
Ingersoll Rand is a Fortune 500 company driven by an ownership mindset and a commitment to making life better for our employees, customers, and communities. Through our portfolio of industry-leading brands, we deliver mission-critical solutions that help customers improve productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Learn more at www.irco.com.

Job Overview
The Technical Inside Sales Representative serves as a trusted technical and customer support resource for aftermarket products, parts, repairs, and service solutions across Western Canada. This role combines technical expertise, customer engagement, and inside sales responsibilities to support distributors, OEMs, engineering firms, service providers, and end users. As a key member of the team, you will work closely with Sales, Operations, Engineering, and Service teams to provide technical guidance, develop quotations, coordinate repair and field service activities, manage warranty claims, and support customers with troubleshooting and equipment-related inquiries. The ideal candidate brings a strong mechanical aptitude, exceptional customer service skills, and a passion for helping customers solve complex industrial equipment challenges. This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to expand their technical expertise, gain exposure to industrial equipment solutions, and build a long-term career with a global industry leader.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary technical support resource for aftermarket customers, providing guidance on repairs, replacements, upgrades, and service solutions.
  • Prepare and manage quotations for aftermarket parts, repairs, field service work, and industrial equipment solutions.
  • Process customer purchase orders, generate order acknowledgments, create work orders, and support order fulfillment activities.
  • Coordinate repair activities and field service projects with customers, technicians, operations teams, and service partners.
  • Provide troubleshooting support for blower systems, controls, maintenance requirements, and operational issues.
  • Evaluate warranty claims, manage Return Material Authorization (RMA) processes, and coordinate corrective actions when required.
  • Identify replacement equipment options and recommend solutions for discontinued or obsolete products.
  • Support customers with technical inquiries and product selection while delivering a high level of responsiveness and professionalism.
  • Utilize ERP systems to manage quotes, orders, inventory transactions, backlogs, and customer records.
  • Partner with Operations, Engineering, Sales, and Service teams to ensure customer expectations are met and business objectives are achieved.
  • Monitor order status and proactively communicate updates, ensuring customers remain informed throughout the process.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance customer experience, operational efficiency, and service performance.
Qualifications
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in technical inside sales, industrial customer service, aftermarket support, equipment service, or a related industrial environment.
  • Experience supporting industrial, mechanical, or rotating equipment customers.
  • Strong customer service orientation with the ability to build trust and deliver solutions in fast-paced situations.
  • Experience preparing quotations, processing customer orders, creating work orders, and managing customer transactions.
  • Proficiency with ERP systems such as Oracle, SAP, Epicor, or similar business systems.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to learn technical equipment, applications, and troubleshooting processes.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple customer requests while maintaining attention to detail and follow-through.
  • Self-motivated and able to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Diploma in Mechanical Engineering Technology or a related technical discipline.
  • Experience supporting aftermarket parts, repairs, warranties, or service operations.
  • Background as a mechanic, millwright, industrial equipment technician, product support specialist, or industrial customer service representative.
  • Experience with blower systems, compressors, pumps, rotating equipment, or related industrial technologies.
  • Experience using Oracle ERP systems.
What Makes a Successful Candidate?
  • Responds quickly and accurately to customer inquiries.
  • Demonstrates urgency and ownership when resolving customer challenges.
  • Maintains professionalism during high-pressure equipment or service-related situations.
  • Learns technical products and troubleshooting processes quickly.
  • Balances customer needs, business priorities, and operational requirements effectively.
  • Consistently delivers exceptional customer experiences through proactive communication and follow-through.
Career Growth Opportunities At Ingersoll Rand, we invest in our people and provide opportunities for continued development and advancement. This role offers potential career paths into:
  • Technical Sales
  • Product Support
  • Service Management
  • Commercial Operations
Work Arrangement
  • Onsite position based in Acheson, Alberta (Edmonton Area).
  • Standard business hours.

What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we foster a culture of ownership, innovation, and growth. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support employees both professionally and personally and includes:
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
  • Life and Disability Insurance
  • Retirement Savings Program with Company Contributions
  • Employee Stock Programs
  • Paid Time Off and Company Holidays
  • Wellness Programs and Employee Assistance Resources
  • Professional Development and Career Advancement Opportunities
  • Collaborative and Inclusive Work Environment

Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic under applicable law. Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE: IR) is a global leader in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.

Job Title: Service Supervisor, PAC - Centrifugal Product
Location: Great Lakes Region
(Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend)

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 
The Service Supervisor, PAC – Centrifugal Product is a highly visible leadership role responsible for the full service lifecycle of compressed-air equipment—from installation and commissioning through ongoing maintenance, repair, and long-term customer support. Leading a team of skilled Service Technicians, this individual plays a critical role in delivering an exceptional customer experience while driving service performance, business growth, and profitability.  Working closely with Sales and Service Coordination, the Service Supervisor ensures seamless execution across the customer lifecycle while maintaining full accountability for the Customer Center Service P&L. The role combines people leadership, customer engagement, operational ownership, and commercial responsibility—balancing customer satisfaction with strong service execution and financial performance.

This position is specifically aligned to the PAC centrifugal product line, a technically sophisticated and highly engineered segment of the compressed-air business. The supervisor serves as a key customer-facing leader, supports technicians in the field, manages service-team performance, and takes ownership of escalated customer, technical, and on-call situations requiring leadership beyond the initial service level.  The role spans a broad Great Lakes territory and offers a unique opportunity to help shape a newly expanded two-supervisor regional coverage model. Depending on the locations of the selected candidates, territories may be structured north/south or east/west—giving the new supervisors an opportunity to help establish the most effective service coverage strategy for the region.

This is a hybrid, field-oriented leadership opportunity offering significant autonomy, direct customer interaction, and meaningful influence over the success of the service organization. Travel is approximately 40%–50%, typically involving one or two overnight stays per week. While direct compressed-air or centrifugal-equipment experience is highly valued, candidates with strong technical aptitude and learning agility may also bring relevant experience from engineering, engineering technology, HVAC, industrial equipment, technical service, or industrial sales.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
 
Requirements: 
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 7+ years of relevant services experience (primarily with industrial equipment).
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 

Core Competencies:
  • Solid professional communication skills both verbal and written.
  • Advanced operating knowledge with Microsoft Office and general business applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of handheld and mobile technologies (smartphones, tablets) and network-based systems.
  • Demonstrated understanding of financial impacts related to process efficiency, cost control, and business performance.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requires interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.  

Preference: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or a relevant area
  • Managing budgets and processes strongly preferred

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • This role is Hybid / Remote US from Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend
  • Company vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Travel approximately 40 - 50% with one to two overnight stays per week. 
  • Regular daily travel to customer sites, including work outdoors and in mechanical or equipment rooms 
  • This position will have physical demands and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.

Pay Range: The range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is $115,000 - $140,000. The total pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Project Manager

Location: Ocala, FL

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
Responsible for the coordination and completion of Engineering, Sales, Operations, Manufacturing or Construction projects. Tracks project status for life of project from order intake thru engineering, follows up on material supply with purchasing to meet production demands and tracks projects thru production to hit delivery targets. Sets deadlines, monitors and summarizes progress of project. Prepares reports for upper management regarding status of project. Prepares schedules for customers and tracks billing milestones.

Responsibilities: 

  • Reviews project plan to determine time frame, funding limitations, procedures for accomplishing project and allotment of available resources to various phases of project.
  • Establishes project schedule by determining required time by department for project, coordinating with managers and supervisors to determine staff that will be working on projects. 
  • Coordinates with staff from multiple departments to keep simultaneous projects on schedule.
  • Review status reports prepared by project personnel and modified schedules or plans as required.
  • Works with customer’s inspectors and expeditors to review project status, documentation, customer change orders, etc.
  • Manages milestone billing based on project progression and agreed upon terms.
  • Documents, tracks and drives resolution to internal and external punch list items to maintain project schedules. 
  • Prepares project reports and schedules for management, customers, or others as required.
  • Confers with project personnel to resolve problems.
  • Performs post-project meetings to best practices and areas of potential improvement for future projects.
  • Other duties performed as assigned by supervisor.

Requirements: 

  • 5+years Project Management experience
  • BS- Engineering or equivalent education

Preferred:

  • Knowledge of industry codes, symbols and ASME code standards. 
  • Ability to understand engineering environment and terminology. 
  • Knowledge of compressed air equipment
  • SAP experience
  • Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office tools, especially Excel and MS Project.
  • Ability to effectively communicate in English both orally and in written form. 
  • Ability to learn. 
  • Use of standard computer and office equipment. 
  • Strong interpersonal skills – will have constant communication interdepartmentally as well as to external customers.

Competencies: 

  • Aligning Performance for Success    Focusing and guiding others in accomplishing work objectives.
  • Building a Successful Team    Using appropriate methods and a flexible interpersonal style to help build a cohesive team; facilitating the completion of team goals.
  • Building Trust    Interacting with others in a way that gives them confidence in one’s intentions and those of the organization.
  • Coaching and Developing Others    Providing feedback, instruction, and development guidance to help others excel in their current or future job responsibilities; planning and supporting the development of individual skills and responsibilities.
  • Communication    Clearly and succinctly conveying information and ideas to individuals and groups in a variety of situations; communicating in a focused and compelling way that drives others’ thoughts and actions.  Engages the audience and helps them understand and retain the message.
  • Continuous Improvement    Originating action to improve existing conditions and processes; identifying improvement opportunities; generating ideas and implementing solutions.
  • Continuous Learning    Actively identifying new ideas for learning; regularly creating and taking advantage of learning opportunities; using newly gained knowledge and skill on the job and learning through their application.
  • Customer Focus    Ensuring that the customer perspective is a driving force behind business decisions and activities; crafting and implementing service practices that meet customers’ and own organization’s needs.
  • Delegating Responsibility    Allocating decision-making authority and/or task responsibility to appropriate others to maximize the organizations and individuals’ effectiveness.
  • Facilitating Change    Encouraging others to seek opportunities for different and innovative approaches to addressing problems and opportunities; facilitating the implementation and acceptance of change within the workplace.
  • Gaining Commitment    Using appropriate interpersonal styles and techniques to gain acceptance of ideas and plans; modifying one’s own behavior to accommodate tasks, situations, and individuals involved.
  • Planning and Organizing    Establishing courses of action for self and others to ensure that work is completed efficiently.

  • Fully Onsite
  • Minimal lifting of up to 25 pounds. Occasional travel required

Job Overview:
We are seeking a highly motivated Cooling System Design Engineer to support the design, development, and delivery of cooling infrastructure for hyperscale, enterprise, and colocation data center projects. This role is responsible for designing efficient, reliable, and sustainable thermal management solutions that support mission-critical environments.

The successful candidate will collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams, equipment vendors, construction partners, and project stakeholders to develop cooling system designs that meet performance, energy efficiency, scalability, and operational requirements throughout the project lifecycle.



Responsibilities

  • Develop conceptual, preliminary, and detailed data center cooling system designs.
  • Design and optimize chilled water, DX, liquid cooling, and air-/water-side economization systems.
  • Perform cooling load calculations, thermal analyses, system sizing, and energy modeling.
  • Develop HVAC layouts, piping schematics, flow diagrams, equipment specifications, and CFD/airflow analyses.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies, including direct-to-chip and immersion cooling.
  • Ensure designs comply with applicable codes, standards, best practices, and resiliency requirements.
  • Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams and support design reviews, procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover.
  • Review vendor submittals, shop drawings, equipment specifications, and resolve design/field issues.
  • Optimize energy efficiency, PUE, lifecycle costs, and sustainability/carbon-reduction objectives.
  • Prepare engineering calculations, reports, specifications, design documentation, and maintain cooling design standards.
 


Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline is preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in HVAC, mission-critical facilities, or data center infrastructure design.
 

Core Competencies

  • Data Center Thermal Management
  • HVAC Design Engineering
  • Mission-Critical Infrastructure
  • Cooling System Optimization
  • Energy Efficiency & Sustainability
  • CFD Analysis
  • Technical Documentation
  • Vendor & Stakeholder Management
  • Risk Assessment & Problem Solving
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting hyperscale or large-scale data center projects.
  • Familiarity with ASHRAE Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments.
  • Experience with CFD modeling tools such as 6SigmaDCX, Future Facilities, or equivalent.
  • Knowledge of liquid cooling technologies for AI/HPC workloads.
  • Experience with Uptime Institute Tier standards and TIA-942 requirements.
  • LEED Accreditation or experience with sustainable design initiatives.
  • Project management experience in multi-disciplinary engineering environments.
  • Experience performing HVAC load calculations and system sizing.
  • Proficiency with engineering design software such as:
    • AutoCAD
    • Revit
    • BIM platforms
    • HVAC modeling tools
  • Strong knowledge of:
    • Air-cooled and water-cooled chillers
    • Chilled water systems
    • Cooling towers
    • CRAH and CRAC systems
    • Pumping systems
    • Heat exchangers
    • Building Management Systems (BMS)

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview

We are seeking a skilled Data Center Thermal Application Engineer to support the design, integration, and deployment of advanced cooling solutions in modern data centers. This role will play a critical part in enabling high-density workloads (AI/ML, HPC) by working closely with Coolant Distribution Unit (CDU), Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and Fan Array/Wall system suppliers to deliver efficient, scalable, and reliable cooling architectures. This position requires strong expertise in liquid cooling systems, airflow management, and system-level thermal integration, along with the ability to collaborate with external partners and internal cross-functional teams.

 


Responsibilities:

  • Design and implement thermal solutions leveraging liquid cooling (CDUs, direct-to-chip) and high-performance air-cooling systems (Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler, fan walls/arrays)
  • Candidate would need to be familiar with chiller sizing criteria and the refrigeration cycle, as that is definitely a major part of the need here.
  • Define system-level cooling architectures integrating CDU loops, facility water systems, and rack-level cooling solutions
  • Evaluate and optimize airflow strategies, including cold aisle/hot aisle containment and fan wall deployment
  • Perform thermal calculations, system sizing, and redundancy planning
  • Support site-specific solution design by assessing customer requirements, heat loads, and facility constraints
  • Provide technical guidance during installation, commissioning, and troubleshooting
  • Collaborate with field teams and customers to resolve thermal performance issues and optimize system operation
  • Develop application notes, design guides, and best practices for deployment

 

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering or Thermal Engineering
  • 5+ years of experience in data center cooling, thermal engineering, or HVAC systems
  • 1+ years of experience hands-on experience with at least one of the following:
    • CDUs and liquid cooling systems (direct-to-chip, liquid loops)
    • Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler
    • Fan arrays/walls or large-scale airflow systems
 


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with hyperscale or colocation data center environments
  • Candidate would need to be familiar with chiller sizing criteria and the refrigeration cycle, as that is definitely a major part of the need here.
  • Familiarity with AI/HPC high-density rack (>30–100kW+) cooling challenges
  • Knowledge of controls and monitoring of CDU systems (BMS/DCIM integration)
  • Experience in commissioning and field deployment of cooling systems
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or certifications in data center design (CDCDP/CDCS)
  • Proficiency in CFD and thermal simulation tools
  • Strong understanding of heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and chilled water systems
  • Experience working with external suppliers or OEM partners in a technical capacity
  • Knowledge of ASHRAE TC9.9 guidelines and data center standards
  • Strong communication skills with ability to work across internal teams and external vendors

 

Core Competencies

  • Strong program and project management capability
  • Leadership and influence across matrixed organizations
  • Financial and commercial acumen
  • Risk management and problem-solving
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management
  • High attention to detail and execution discipline
  • Use CFD and system modeling tools (e.g., 6SigmaDCX, ANSYS Icepak, FloTHERM) to validate thermal performance
  • Analyze liquid flow characteristics, pressure drops, and heat exchanger performance
  • Conduct lab and field validation, including thermal testing of CDU, Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and airflow systems
  • Continuously improve system efficiency, energy usage (PUE), and reliability
  • Work closely with mechanical, electrical, controls, and data center infrastructure teams
  • Support procurement and quality teams in supplier selection and qualification
  • Contribute to product development and roadmap planning for next-generation cooling solutions
  • Act as the primary technical interface with CDU, Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and fan array/wall system suppliers
  • Review vendor designs, specifications, and performance data to ensure alignment with system requirements
  • Coordinate integration testing, factory acceptance testing (FAT), and site acceptance testing (SAT)

 

 Travel & Work Requirements

  • 25%-40% travel (project sites, factory inspections, FAT/SAT, customer reviews

 

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $130,000-$150,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title: Sourcing Engineer                
Location: Sedalia, MO 
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a highly visible sourcing role where no two days are the same. The Sourcing Engineer will balance forward-looking supply chain improvement with hands-on support of the Sedalia manufacturing operation. Approximately half of the role will focus on strengthening the supply chain and supplier partnerships, while the other half will involve working closely with the materials team to address supplier escalations and help ensure the plant has the components needed to meet production and revenue commitments. The balance will shift as business priorities change, giving this individual exposure to a wide range of challenges and opportunities.

Working across Sedalia’s diverse product lines and active global supply network, the Sourcing Engineer will turn complex data into practical business strategies, build productive supplier relationships, and help navigate issues ranging from delayed materials to broader supply disruptions and resourcing needs. This is not a transactional purchasing position—the individual will serve as a trusted problem-solver who connects suppliers, materials, operations, and other internal partners to keep critical work moving forward.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys variety, thrives on solving new problems, and wants to see the direct impact of their work on both plant performance and long-term supply chain success. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to take ownership of meaningful initiatives within the first few months, expand their knowledge of Sedalia’s products and operations, and grow into a fully integrated member of a collaborative, fast-moving team.

Responsibilities

Cost Reduction & Sourcing Projects
  • Identify, develop, and manage sourcing projects that reduce material costs and achieve savings goals.
  • Analyze spend, purchase price variance, materials, and other data to identify new savings opportunities.
  • Maintain sourcing/savings project tracking and lead cross-functional reviews to drive projects to completion.
  • Track sourcing activity, savings, and performance results to ensure accurate and timely reporting.
Supplier Sourcing & Commercial Negotiations
  • Identify and develop new suppliers and improve the value delivered by existing suppliers.
  • Lead RFP/RFQ activities in partnership with internal stakeholders.
  • Negotiate supplier pricing, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, and other commercial terms.
  • Monitor purchase price variances and resolve discrepancies with suppliers and internal teams.
Supplier Development & Performance
  • Partner with suppliers and internal teams to qualify new parts and support sourcing transitions.
  • Address significant or systemic supplier performance issues involving quality, delivery, warranty, cost, or other concerns.
  • Work with suppliers to improve overall performance and support sourcing objectives.
Market Intelligence & Special Projects
  • Monitor commodity pricing, market trends, and domestic/international events that may affect supplier pricing or supply.
  • Participate in special projects and perform additional responsibilities as assigned.

Requirements:
  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 3+ years of progressive experience in sourcing, procurement, supply chain, or supplier management.
  • 2+ years of experience negotiating directly with suppliers on pricing, cost increases, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, or other commercial terms.
  • 2+ years of experience analyzing sourcing, spend, pricing, PPV, or supplier data to identify savings opportunities and support business decisions.
  • 2+ years of experience using Excel for data analysis, including pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, financial or logical functions, and multiple worksheets/workbooks.
  • 1+ years of experience leading sourcing initiatives, such as RFQ/RFP activities, cost-reduction projects, supplier development, resourcing, or new supplier qualification.

Core Competencies:
  • Cost Optimization & Value Creation – Identifies and drives opportunities to reduce material costs and improve supplier value.
  • Sourcing Project Management – Organizes, tracks, and drives sourcing initiatives from identification through completion.
  • Supplier Development & Performance Management – Builds supplier capability and addresses quality, delivery, warranty, and other performance issues.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Coordinates effectively with internal stakeholders to advance sourcing initiatives, RFPs, and new-part qualification.
  • Commercial & Business Acumen – Understands the business impact of pricing, payment terms, lead times, inventory programs, and sourcing decisions.
  • Market & Commodity Awareness – Monitors market conditions, commodity trends, and global events that may affect supplier cost or availability.

Preferences:
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or related field
  • Manufacturing sourcing/procurement experience
  • Global and/or Low-Cost-Country sourcing experience
  • SAP or other ERP/MRP experience
  • APICS or similar certification
  • Excel macros

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is based onsite in Sedalia, MO
  • Minimal travel (<10%), primarily to suppliers if needed.

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Quality Engineer, Site Lead
Location:  Chicago, IL (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a visible, hands-on role with site quality lead responsibilities where your work directly impacts product integrity, customer confidence, and manufacturing performance. The Quality Site Lead is responsible for the full range of Quality Engineering support, including quality systems, process improvement, validation, CAPA, auditing, risk assessment, training, and new product introduction support across the Elastomer Chicago manufacturing site. This role has primary ownership of ISO 9001 compliance and supports ISO 13485 medical device silicone operations as needed. It is a strong opportunity for a quality leader who enjoys being close to production, solving problems at the root, partnering across Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and leadership, and building a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. The position also leads Quality Technicians and Inspectors, ensuring the team is aligned, audit-ready, and focused on consistent product quality across both industrial and medical device environments.

Responsibilities
Quality Management System / Regulatory Compliance: 
  • Develop, maintain, and execute quality procedures and work instructions to streamline processes and ensure compliance with FDA regulations, ISO standards, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Oversee the development, management, maintenance, and effectiveness of the Elastomer BU Quality Management System, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 compliance.
  • Serve as Management Representative for the Elastomer BU Chicago site.
  • Ensure all SOPs and process documentation are created in accordance with the QMS and partner with departments to ensure effectiveness.
  • Ensure document control and revision control activities are maintained in compliance with QMS and regulatory requirements.
  • Responsible for ensuring all cleanroom requirements are met, as applicable.

Audits, CAPA, NCRs, and Customer Complaints:
  • Host customer and registrar audits and coordinate or perform internal quality and supplier audits as needed.
  • Lead and/or support internal and external CAPAs, NCRs, and customer complaints, including investigation, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and related documentation.
  • Change Control, Documentation, and Product Release.
  • Review and assess change requests to ensure proper evaluation of impact on product quality, processes, and regulatory compliance.
    Manage customer-submitted change requests through completion.
  • Review and approve engineering documentation, including validation protocols/reports, sample run requests, and manufacturing procedures, ensuring adherence to customer and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure all products conform to validated processes and DMRs; perform lot release and related quality functions.

Production Quality, Process Control, and Continuous Improvement:
  • Assure reliability and consistency of production by monitoring processes and final output.
  • Implement statistical tools, including SPC, MSA, and GR&R, to ensure process control and measurement system reliability.
  • Leverage ISO 9001 continuous improvement principles to improve process efficiency and effectiveness.
    Monitor key quality metrics and provide regular reporting to leadership.

Supplier Quality and Compliance:
  • Collaborate with Purchasing to co-manage the Approved Supplier List and evaluate suppliers to ensure product compliance.
  • Monitor supplier performance and rate suppliers through scorecard ratings.
  • Calibration, Preventive Maintenance, and Resource Planning
  • Provide oversight of the calibration and preventive maintenance programs to ensure compliance.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify equipment, testing, and resource needs for new or existing products, and communicate requirements to leadership.

Team Leadership, Training, and Talent Management:
  • Achieve quality assurance human resource objectives by recruiting, selecting, orienting, training, scheduling, coaching, counseling, and disciplining employees.
  • Communicate job expectations and lead team talent and performance management processes.
  • Conduct employee training sessions, as applicable.

Professional Development:
  • Maintain current quality management knowledge by studying industry trends, participating in educational opportunities, reading professional publications, and engaging in professional organizations and networking opportunities.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree ideally in industrial, mechanical / manufacturing engineering or similar field
  • 5+ years of significant professional experience in continuous quality improvement with progressive scope and responsibility.
  • 4+ years experience working within an ISO 9001 quality management system, including quality procedures, documentation, audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
  • 3+ years leading teams, ideally in a quality manufacturing environment with proven experience with Good Manufacturing Practices.
  • 2+ years experience with statistical tools, data analysis, SPC, MSA, GR&R, process validation, IQ/OQ/PQ, and root cause analysis.

Core Competencies:
  • Regulatory Quality Leadership: Ability to interpret quality system requirements, maintain audit-ready processes, and guide site compliance in a regulated manufacturing environment.
  • Manufacturing Quality Problem Solving: Strong ability to investigate issues, analyze process variation, identify root cause, and drive practical corrective actions that improve product quality and process performance.
  • Cross-Functional Execution: Ability to work effectively across Quality, Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and leadership teams to align priorities, resolve issues, and support production and NPI needs.
  • Team Leadership & Quality Culture: Ability to lead cross-functional teams, drive issue resolution, train, coach, and hold quality team members accountable while reinforcing a culture of compliance, ownership, and continuous improvement.
  • Quality Systems, Data & Reporting Tools: Proficient in Microsoft Office and able to use quality data, documentation, reports, metrics, and system tools to track performance, support audits, manage corrective actions, and communicate quality trends to leadership.

Preferences:
  • Advanced degree, Engineering degree, or another technical field.
  • Experience working in Master Control QMS System
  • Continuous quality improvement experience in one or more medical product environments.
  • Experience working within an ISO 13485 quality management system, including medical device documentation, audit readiness, CAPA, and regulatory compliance.
  • Experience in silicone or rubber molding, including LSR, compression, or transfer molding.
  • Experience supporting medical device OEM customers.
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR 820 and risk management, including ISO 14971.

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • Position based onsite in Chicago, IL (near O'Hare Airport)
  • Work Authorization: US Citizen or Permanent Resident

Pay Range
The base pay range for this role is $80-110k annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Job Title: Manufacturing Engineer
Location: Mocksville, NC
Schedule: M-F, Day shift

About Us:  
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
In this role as a Manufacturing Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of production processes. The Manufacturing Engineer is tasked with designing and refining manufacturing methods to boost productivity while maintaining high-quality standards and ensuring safety protocols. They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows. 

Responsibilities:

  • Suggests, evaluates, implements & manages multiple manufacturing projects from beginning to end
  • Evaluates, develops and implements machining processes on current or future assets
  • Implements capital equipment including evaluation, selection, run-offs, and implementation
  • Maintains manufacturing best practices including precision machining, lean manufacturing, and machine tool / tooling technologies
  • Evaluates non-conforming material and provides proper disposition
  • Leads special projects including NPD, insourcing, productivity and capital procurement
  • Designs tooling, gages and fixtures using 3D modeling software
  • Develops manufacturing routings internal and sub-con operations
  • Leads machine tool installations throughout the entire process
  • Supports production efforts through troubleshooting manufacturing issues
  • Ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards
  • Supports safety and environmental practices
  • Performs other duties assigned by immediate supervisor


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Industrial or Mechanical engineering. 
  • 2+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering.
  • 2+ years of of CNC Programming, CAD / CAM / CAE
  • 2+ years of engineering drawings including GD&T and tolerance analysis.


Core Competencies:

  • Technical Expertise: knowledge of manufacturing processes and technologies. 
  • Problem-Solving: Analytical skills to develop effective solutions. 
  • Project Management: Ability to manage projects from start to finish efficiently. 
  • Collaboration: Experience working with cross-functional teams. 
  • Attention to Detail: To ensure quality and compliance. 
  • Innovation: Creative thinking to introduce new manufacturing solutions. 
  • Leadership: Ability to train and guide production staff. 
  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols. 
  • Strong analytical ability to solve issues such as: manufacturing problems and dimensional or calculation errors.
  • Solid understanding of machining processes and overall business operations.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • Comprehensive understanding of machine tool operations.
  • In-depth knowledge of MS Office Software, and MS Project.


Preferences:

  • Ability to prioritize tasks, and carry out root cause analysis.
  • Continuous Improvement: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.  
  • Ability to communicate at all levels internally, customers and suppliers.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Techniques and ability to create standard work.
  • Fluent using inspection tools, techniques and their application to the engineering requirements.
  • Proficient in gear or helical grinding.
  • Understanding of rotary screw compressors and/or centrifugal compressors.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Onsite with up to 15% travel.

Job Title: Supply Chain Leader                
Location: Southern Pines, NC 
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Are you a supply chain leader who enjoys owning the full picture—people, materials, suppliers, schedules, inventory, and customer delivery? This role offers the opportunity to lead a buyer/planner/scheduler team supporting a defined value stream within the Southern Pines manufacturing operation. You’ll have the autonomy to run your portion of the business, partner closely with operations and supply chain peers, and directly impact on-time shipment, inventory performance, supplier accountability, and production execution. The Supply Chain Leader will own supply chain activities for a defined value stream/product family, ensuring customer demand is supported with the right material at the right time while balancing inventory and operational priorities. You’ll lead a team of buyers, planners, and schedulers responsible for material availability, production scheduling, supplier follow-up, inventory management, and customer shipment commitments. 

This is a highly visible, hands-on leadership role working across supply chain, manufacturing operations, suppliers, and business-unit stakeholders to keep production moving, reduce past-due backlog, improve on-time shipment, and strengthen inventory and supplier performance. The ideal candidate will bring strong buying, planning, scheduling, or materials experience within a manufacturing environment—preferably assembly-based—with exposure to bills of material, ERP systems, supplier constraints, production schedules, and customer delivery requirements. Experience with the company’s specific ERP system is not required, but you should understand how ERP supports plant supply chain operations and be comfortable using data, Excel, and disciplined follow-up to drive results. Success will also require strong communication, organization, follow-through, and the ability to build effective relationships with direct reports and cross-functional partners.

For a supply chain professional seeking autonomy, team leadership, and visible impact, this is an opportunity to strengthen performance and drive meaningful improvement within an established business.

Responsibilities:

Production Planning & Scheduling:
  • Translate the monthly SIOP consensus plan by product family into a detailed weekly Master Production Schedule (MPS) with a 12–18-month planning horizon in the ERP for weekly MRP generation.
  • Maintain the material plan within the time fence to ensure continuity of supply.
  • Identify and resolve capacity, resource, and material constraints.
  • Facilitate long-term capacity assessments (RCCP) and develop countermeasure/action plans.
  • Conduct lead-time analysis, measure gaps against published lead times, drive corrective actions, and update published lead times as needed.
  • Coordinate with planners to achieve assigned serviceability and inventory goals.
  • Interface with required functional groups to resolve challenging delivery requirements.
ERP / MRP Management & Data Integrity:
  • Monitor and drive resolution of MRP processing errors.
  • Manage ERP-generated exception messages in a timely manner.
  • Serve as the factory subject matter expert (SME) for ERP production planning and scheduling modules within the assigned business unit.
  • Maintain the integrity of ERP planning parameters, including lead times, lot sizes, safety stock, delivery times, and order file data for all master-scheduled items.
  • Maintain item master lead-time information based on process improvements, current constraints, total demand by product family, and priority requirements.
Supplier Management & Material Availability:
  • Engage with suppliers to secure inventory flow needed to support plant shipment goals.
  • Communicate forecasts and replenishment plans to suppliers.
  • Review open requirements, monitor supplier performance, and expedite deliveries as needed.
  • Expedite deliveries to meet or exceed critical schedule requirements.
  • Ensure supplier issues related to delivery, quality, or pricing are communicated and resolved promptly.
  • Coordinate with Quality Assurance to resolve supplier quality issues.
  • Resolve invoicing discrepancies with suppliers and Accounting.
  • Develop effective methods for monitoring supplier agreements that support future cost savings and inventory goals.
Customer Delivery & Service Support:
  • Support Customer Service with exception-request analysis and expediting resolution.
  • Help drive delivery performance, reduce supply disruptions, and support customer shipment commitments.
  • Apply root-cause problem solving to resolve supply disruptions and achieve inventory targets.
Reporting & Performance Management:
  • Create and publish daily, weekly, and monthly reports covering factory schedule adherence, capacity, and inventory.
  • Analyze and report key performance indicators, including delivery performance, backlog, performance to master schedule, and inventory turns.
  • Maintain productivity pipelines and financial records used to report and track improvement initiatives.
Continuous Improvement & Cost Productivity:
  • Drive continuous process improvement and identify opportunities to increase efficiency.
  • Challenge existing processes when more effective alternatives are available.
  • Identify and implement cost-reduction and productivity projects aligned with corporate initiatives and goals.
Team Leadership & Development:
  • Develop, coach, and mentor team members to achieve outstanding results.
  • Lead and direct others as needed to accomplish organizational objectives.
Project & Cross-Functional Support: Manage projects and perform other duties as needed.

Requirements:
  • BS/BA degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • 5+ years of manufacturing supply chain experience, including materials management, buying, planning, production control, master scheduling, inventory, and customer delivery support.
  • 3+ years supporting material availability, production schedules, MRP/ERP-driven planning, inventory performance, customer demand, and plant shipment targets.
  • 3+ years working directly with suppliers to manage material availability, delivery performance, follow-up, issue resolution, and accountability.
  • 2+ years leading, coaching, mentoring, or providing day-to-day direction to buyers, planners, schedulers, materials, or other supply chain team members.
  • Strong working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems and proficiency with Microsoft Excel required.

Core Competencies
  • Decision-Making & Prioritization: Able to make sound, complex decisions with limited time and information, using business priorities to establish clear decision criteria.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Builds effective partnerships across functions and works successfully with internal teams, external resources, suppliers, and business partners.
  • Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: Strong analytical capability with the ability to evaluate data, identify root causes, and independently resolve problems; working knowledge of basic statistical analysis techniques.
  • Leadership & Influence: Proven ability to lead, influence, and manage competing requirements while effectively guiding discussions with peers, matrix partners, operational teams, and leadership.
  • Communication & Interpersonal Effectiveness: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to lead productive discussions, challenge perspectives, and drive alignment.
  • Organization & Follow-Through: Demonstrated ability to stay organized, manage competing priorities, follow up consistently, work cross-functionally, and drive actions through completion.
  • Data Analysis & Reporting: Proficient in accessing, manipulating, and analyzing data using Microsoft Excel and other available reporting tools.
  • ERP Systems Knowledge: Working knowledge of ERP systems and their application within planning, materials, and manufacturing operations.

Preferences:
  • Demonstrated success improving on-time delivery, customer service levels, inventory performance, and/or past-due backlog.
  • Experience working with bills of material (BOMs) within a manufacturing supply chain environment.
  • Machining and castings experience.
  • Experience with QAD and/or Oracle ERP systems.
  • Experience within rate-based, flow-line, non-MRP, and/or job shop manufacturing environments.
  • Experience with lean manufacturing practices and visual management systems.
  • Experience supporting new product introductions and/or value stream/product family supply chain activities.

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • CPIM certification
  • Minimal travel (<10%), primarily to suppliers as needed.
  • Required PPE includes safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toe shoes, and gloves when handling parts. 
  • Office and manufacturing environment with occasional exposure to moving equipment and permissible levels of coolant/oil mist. Moderate noise levels.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions.
