Job Title: Regional Sales Manager
Location: Remote - Territory - TX, LA, OK, AR, KS, CO, WY, MS

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) role within its Industrial Technologies and Services (ITS) Business Unit will be responsible for sales growth and business development activities for air treatment solutions, to include air dryers, process chillers, nitrogen generators, oil-water separators, both new sales and rentals in the Southwestern US. The Regional Sales Manager will utilize their technical expertise in how the equipment is utilized in the market and will work closely with channel partners to cultivate, foster, and grow the presence of our products in the marketplace. Establishing and growing the distributor and OEM business relationships, growing revenue and market share for the portfolio, and maintaining profit margins are key for this role. Join us in making the ITS division of Ingersoll Rand an outstanding place to work where both our team and our company thrive! 

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement comprehensive sales strategies to expand market presence and achieve sales targets in the Southwest region.
  • Analyze market trends, customer needs, and competitive landscape to identify new business opportunities and areas for growth.
  • Follow established visitation frequencies for channel partners and achieve a cadence structure for reporting new opportunities, forecasting, revenue progress, etc.
  • Regularly track sales performance and key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess progress towards targets and identify areas for improvement.
  • Identify and recruit new distribution/channel partners and acquire new distribution/channel partners to expand market reach and penetration. This includes establishing and growing synergistic channel partners throughout the region.
  • Oversee the Distribution/Channel Partner network in the Southwest territory: act as the main point of contact for distributors, including business owners, sales teams, and service leaders and guide their activities and priorities. 
  • Partner with the ITS Support teams (manufacturing, service and warranty, customer service, e-commerce, etc.) to improve collaboration, establish best practices, and grow the channel partner and organizations market share.
  • Develop, mentor and coach channel partner sales team in fostering customer relationships, train distribution personnel, and assess their proficiency in supporting products and services.
  • Establish performance benchmarks for individual product lines to gauge distributor effectiveness and drive sales outcomes.
  • Identify underserved areas and geographies, devising business plans to expand coverage.
  • Spot gaps in market/industry coverage and competition and emerging market trends and refocus existing or new channels to address these gaps.
  • Resolve conflicts within the channel and region.
  • Maintain ongoing distribution engagement that supports consistent, high-impact activities.
  • Develop and manage an active opportunity pipeline with all partner organizations, collecting regular feedback to monitor progress.
  • Actively pursue and support competitive conversion opportunities identified in the pipeline.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales Enablement & Product Management to capitalize on pricing, product specifications, and new product potential.
  • Provide hands-on feedback to sales team, sharing insights on trends, competition, economics, and other factors to help identify and prioritize strategic opportunities.
  • Lead, motivate, and work with other members of the sales team and channel partners to meet revenue targets, ensure high level of new customer activity, and focus resources to achieve strategic account penetration.
  • Seek and communicate the voice of the customer (VOC) to build strong customer relationships, understand their needs, and communicate risks and opportunities to the ITS leadership team.
  • Collaborate with marketing & product management to establish market pricing and develop sales strategies to realize sales of existing and new products to meet or exceed revenue and profit targets.
  • Establish sales forecasts, plans & objectives for your region and by product line and provide weekly / monthly / yearly forecasting to update the business on short and long-term trends.
  • Track regional metrics to communicate key performance indicators relating to sales, profitability, market share and competitor activities.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, engineering technology, or business
  • 5+ years of industrial sales ideally in industrial equipment, compressed air, air treatment solutions (dryers, filtration, condensate management) or related sectors.

Core Competencies:

  • Formulate a clear and compelling regional sales strategy that aligns with the overall business objectives. This includes identifying market opportunities, defining target customer segments, and outlining a roadmap to achieve sales goals.
  • Optimizing the sales process, including following best practices, implementing sales methodologies, and continuously improving workflows through standard operating procedures. 
  • Ability to gather, interpret and effectively communicate product information in a clear, concise, way, using multiple communication channels (verbal, written, email, chat) to various internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical specifications, product technical literature, construction plans/drawings, commercial terms and conditions, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries from internal or external customers or suppliers.
  • Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of practical problems.
  • Uses technical knowledge to assess the potential application of company products, recommending solutions that meet customer needs, and advance the sales process.

Preferences:

  • Experience with air compressors and/or air dryers preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience using data to drive distributors behavior and success.
  • Understanding of principles of air compression and/or air treatment, and applications.
  • Understanding of commercial terms including payment terms, receivables, shipping terms, and contract terms and conditions review.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
Remote with the ability to travel up to 50% within the Southwest region.

Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $110,000 - $130,000. The total pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

What We Offer:
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Success in this role requires strong channel development capability, strategic sales planning, and hands-on dealer engagement to expand Champion Pneumatics’ presence and market share.

Responsibilities:
 

  • Manage, develop, and grow existing dealers and distributors within the assigned territory.
  • Identify, recruit, and onboard new dealers, including those currently representing competing product lines.
  • Deliver ongoing product training and sales skills training to dealer sales teams to improve selling capabilities and technical knowledge.
  • Provide training as needed for dealer technicians, office personnel, and internal support roles.
  • Partner with dealer sales teams on account and project strategies to position Champion Pneumatic for maximum success.
  • Work closely with dealer leadership teams to assess business performance, improve organizational structure, and elevate their effectiveness in selling Champion Pneumatic products.
  • Conduct annual business planning, market development planning, and risk assessments with each dealer.
  • Collaborate on written gap-closure plans to address performance issues where necessary.
  • Quickly onboard and integrate new personnel within dealer organizations to accelerate productivity.
  • Identify and resolve dealer issues or obstacles that hinder sales performance.
  • Achieve bookings, revenue, dealer activation, and market share growth targets for assigned dealers.

Requirements:
 

  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • 3+ years of experience in industrial equipment Sales, HVAC Sales or Sales Equivalent.

Key Competencies
 

  • Proven leadership and the ability to influence across multiple teams within dealer organizations.
  • Strong strategic thinking and business planning skills, including the ability to assist dealers in developing long-term growth plans.
  • Ability to cultivate a collaborative, partnership-driven dealer culture that prioritizes customer success.
  • Strong communication, training, and problem solving skills.
  • High level of ownership and accountability for territory performance, dealer development, and market share growth.
  Preferences:
  • 3+ years of experience in industrial equipment sales, with compressed air industry experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience recruiting and developing new dealers or distributors, including those selling competitive lines.
  • Bachelor’s degree Engineering, Technical, Marketing, or Business preferred.

Travel & Work Requirement:

Remote-based position. Approximately 50% travel is required (visiting each dealer location at least once per quarter)
Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is Min - 100000 - Max - 120000 . The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Title: Regional Sales Manager
Location: Remote - Territory - TX, LA, OK, AR, KS, CO, WY, MS

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) role within its Industrial Technologies and Services (ITS) Business Unit will be responsible for sales growth and business development activities for air treatment solutions, to include air dryers, process chillers, nitrogen generators, oil-water separators, both new sales and rentals in the Southwestern US. The Regional Sales Manager will utilize their technical expertise in how the equipment is utilized in the market and will work closely with channel partners to cultivate, foster, and grow the presence of our products in the marketplace. Establishing and growing the distributor and OEM business relationships, growing revenue and market share for the portfolio, and maintaining profit margins are key for this role. Join us in making the ITS division of Ingersoll Rand an outstanding place to work where both our team and our company thrive! 

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement comprehensive sales strategies to expand market presence and achieve sales targets in the Southwest region.
  • Analyze market trends, customer needs, and competitive landscape to identify new business opportunities and areas for growth.
  • Follow established visitation frequencies for channel partners and achieve a cadence structure for reporting new opportunities, forecasting, revenue progress, etc.
  • Regularly track sales performance and key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess progress towards targets and identify areas for improvement.
  • Identify and recruit new distribution/channel partners and acquire new distribution/channel partners to expand market reach and penetration. This includes establishing and growing synergistic channel partners throughout the region.
  • Oversee the Distribution/Channel Partner network in the Southwest territory: act as the main point of contact for distributors, including business owners, sales teams, and service leaders and guide their activities and priorities. 
  • Partner with the ITS Support teams (manufacturing, service and warranty, customer service, e-commerce, etc.) to improve collaboration, establish best practices, and grow the channel partner and organizations market share.
  • Develop, mentor and coach channel partner sales team in fostering customer relationships, train distribution personnel, and assess their proficiency in supporting products and services.
  • Establish performance benchmarks for individual product lines to gauge distributor effectiveness and drive sales outcomes.
  • Identify underserved areas and geographies, devising business plans to expand coverage.
  • Spot gaps in market/industry coverage and competition and emerging market trends and refocus existing or new channels to address these gaps.
  • Resolve conflicts within the channel and region.
  • Maintain ongoing distribution engagement that supports consistent, high-impact activities.
  • Develop and manage an active opportunity pipeline with all partner organizations, collecting regular feedback to monitor progress.
  • Actively pursue and support competitive conversion opportunities identified in the pipeline.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales Enablement & Product Management to capitalize on pricing, product specifications, and new product potential.
  • Provide hands-on feedback to sales team, sharing insights on trends, competition, economics, and other factors to help identify and prioritize strategic opportunities.
  • Lead, motivate, and work with other members of the sales team and channel partners to meet revenue targets, ensure high level of new customer activity, and focus resources to achieve strategic account penetration.
  • Seek and communicate the voice of the customer (VOC) to build strong customer relationships, understand their needs, and communicate risks and opportunities to the ITS leadership team.
  • Collaborate with marketing & product management to establish market pricing and develop sales strategies to realize sales of existing and new products to meet or exceed revenue and profit targets.
  • Establish sales forecasts, plans & objectives for your region and by product line and provide weekly / monthly / yearly forecasting to update the business on short and long-term trends.
  • Track regional metrics to communicate key performance indicators relating to sales, profitability, market share and competitor activities.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, engineering technology, or business
  • 5+ years of industrial sales ideally in industrial equipment, compressed air, air treatment solutions (dryers, filtration, condensate management) or related sectors.

Core Competencies:

  • Formulate a clear and compelling regional sales strategy that aligns with the overall business objectives. This includes identifying market opportunities, defining target customer segments, and outlining a roadmap to achieve sales goals.
  • Optimizing the sales process, including following best practices, implementing sales methodologies, and continuously improving workflows through standard operating procedures. 
  • Ability to gather, interpret and effectively communicate product information in a clear, concise, way, using multiple communication channels (verbal, written, email, chat) to various internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical specifications, product technical literature, construction plans/drawings, commercial terms and conditions, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries from internal or external customers or suppliers.
  • Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of practical problems.
  • Uses technical knowledge to assess the potential application of company products, recommending solutions that meet customer needs, and advance the sales process.

Preferences:

  • Experience with air compressors and/or air dryers preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience using data to drive distributors behavior and success.
  • Understanding of principles of air compression and/or air treatment, and applications.
  • Understanding of commercial terms including payment terms, receivables, shipping terms, and contract terms and conditions review.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
Remote with the ability to travel up to 50% within the Southwest region.

Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $110,000 - $130,000. The total pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

job.title: Import/Export Administrator
job.description:
Job Title: Import/Export Administrator
Location: Ivyland, Pennsylvania, USA
Employment Type: Full-Time

About Us
Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and ownership, committed to improving the lives of our employees, customers, and communities. With more than 80 leading brands, we provide mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions that perform in the most demanding environments. Our success is built on empowering employees to think and act like owners while delivering exceptional customer experiences. For more information, visit www.irco.com.

Job Overview:
The Import/Export Administrator is responsible for supporting international trade and logistics activities while ensuring compliance with applicable import and export regulations. This role serves as a key liaison between customers, freight forwarders, suppliers, shipping teams, and internal departments to facilitate the timely and compliant movement of goods worldwide. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, customer-focused, and capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate import and export logistics activities with customers, freight forwarders, shipping teams, and customer service representatives.
  • Review, approve, and release international sales orders while ensuring transaction accuracy and regulatory compliance.
  • Prioritize customer orders and shipments to meet business and customer requirements.
  • Support investigations and resolution of customer disputes related to shipping, documentation, and logistics activities.
  • Classify products and materials using Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) codes and maintain classification records.
  • Maintain import/export compliance records and supporting documentation.
  • Prepare, process, and manage AES and EEI filings in accordance with government regulations.
  • Create and maintain import/export documentation, including commercial invoices, shipping papers, certificates, and related records.
  • Support the development and maintenance of standard operating procedures related to international trade compliance.
  • Audit and monitor transactions with vendors, suppliers, customers, and logistics providers to ensure accuracy and compliance.
  • Coordinate with internal departments to ensure shipments are completed accurately and on schedule.
  • Stay current with import/export regulations, trade compliance requirements, and customer-specific requirements.
  • Conduct or support compliance-related training and awareness initiatives.
  • Perform quality checks in accordance with established procedures and ISO standards.
  • Maintain a clean, organized work environment and support continuous improvement initiatives, including 5S methodologies.
  • Adhere to all company safety, environmental, and quality policies and procedures.
Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in International Business, Foreign Trade, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in import/export administration, logistics, trade compliance, or a related field.
  • Strong knowledge of import/export classification, HTS codes, country of origin requirements, free trade agreements, and international trade regulations.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. Customs regulations, including Title 19 CFR.
  • Understanding of applicable import/export laws and regulations administered by government agencies.
  • Experience preparing and managing import/export documentation and regulatory filings.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with external partners.
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Strong attention to detail and data accuracy.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, and Excel.
  • Experience working with ERP systems such as JD Edwards is preferred.
  • Customer-focused mindset with the ability to adapt to changing business needs.
Core Competencies:
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent organizational and time management abilities.
  • High attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Problem-solving and analytical thinking.
  • Integrity and commitment to compliance.
  • Customer-focused approach to service and support.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.
  • Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on efficiency and quality.
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • This position is fully site-based in Ivyland, Pennsylvania.
  • Work is performed within a climate-controlled manufacturing environment.
  • Protective eyewear and safety footwear are required in designated areas.
  • Participation in ongoing safety and environmental health training is required.
What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership, taking responsibility for our company, our communities, our environment, and our well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to provide the support and resources needed to help employees thrive both personally and professionally.

Please note our hiring process does not use AI at any stage to screen, assess, or select candidates.

Our Range of Benefits Includes:
  • Empowering Culture: Encouraging personal ownership, innovation, and community involvement.
  • Health Care Options: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and prescription coverage.
  • Wellness Programs: Resources and programs supporting physical, emotional, and financial well-being.
  • Retirement Savings: Competitive 401(k) program designed to help secure your future.
  • Employee Stock Grant: Opportunity to share in the company's continued growth and success.
  • Paid Time Off: Generous time off programs that support work-life balance.
  • Learning & Development: Access to training resources, professional development opportunities, and LinkedIn Learning.
  • Career Growth: Internal advancement opportunities and individualized development planning.
  • Employee Recognition: Employee appreciation programs, service celebrations, and team-building activities.
  • Supportive Environment: A culture committed to collaboration, development, and employee success.


At Milton Roy – Ivyland, we foster a workplace culture focused on employee appreciation, development, and growth. Team members enjoy employee recognition events, community engagement activities, and opportunities to participate in team-building programs that strengthen collaboration and workplace engagement. We are committed to promoting from within and supporting long-term career success through training, mentorship, and development opportunities.

Our employees build customers for life through their commitment to expertise, productivity, and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

job.title: Key Account & Regional Sales Manager
job.description:
Job Title: Key Account & Regional Sales Manager – BioPharma Solutions (Canada)
Location: Remote – Canada (Must reside near a major airport)
Employment Type: Full-Time
Travel: Approximately 50–60% (Global Travel Required)
Reports To: Director of Sales


About Us
Ingersoll Rand is a Fortune 500 company driven by an ownership mindset and a commitment to making life better for our employees, customers, and communities. Through innovation, sustainability, and customer-focused solutions, we deliver mission-critical technologies across more than 40 trusted brands worldwide.

Job Overview
The Key Account & Regional Sales Manager is a strategic commercial leader responsible for driving profitable growth across Canada while serving as the Global Key Account Manager for one of ILC Dover's most important BioPharma customers. This role combines strategic account management, regional sales leadership, and business development within the life sciences and pharmaceutical manufacturing markets.
The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of key BioPharma accounts throughout Canada while leading the global growth strategy for Johnson & Johnson across its worldwide manufacturing network. The position requires a consultative, relationship-driven sales professional with deep BioPharma industry knowledge, experience navigating complex customer organizations, and a proven ability to influence stakeholders across multiple functions and geographies.
This is a highly visible role that works cross-functionally with sales, engineering, operations, customer service, and executive leadership to drive customer success, revenue growth, and long-term strategic partnerships.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute strategic growth plans for assigned BioPharma customers and regional accounts.
  • Serve as the Global Key Account Manager for Johnson & Johnson, coordinating growth initiatives across approximately 34 global sites.
  • Manage and grow a Canadian territory valued at approximately $3M+ in annual revenue.
  • Establish and strengthen executive-level relationships with decision-makers and influencers at customer organizations.
  • Identify new business opportunities, drive account penetration, and expand existing customer partnerships.
  • Collaborate with Regional Sales Managers globally to implement key account strategies and accelerate growth.
  • Lead customer business reviews, strategic planning sessions, and commercial negotiations.
  • Coordinate internal resources including engineering, operations, technical support, marketing, and customer service to deliver customer solutions.
  • Maintain accurate opportunity pipelines, forecasts, account plans, and customer information within Salesforce.
  • Develop commercial programs including pricing strategies, contract renewals, incentive programs, and NDAs.
  • Resolve customer issues and drive continuous improvement initiatives that support customer operational excellence.
  • Achieve and exceed revenue, profitability, and market-share objectives.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related discipline; equivalent experience considered.
  • 5+ years of direct sales or strategic account management experience.
  • Mandatory experience within the BioPharma, pharmaceutical manufacturing, bioprocessing, or life sciences industry.
  • Proven success managing strategic accounts and driving revenue growth.
  • Experience engaging with executive-level stakeholders within complex customer organizations.
  • Strong business acumen, negotiation skills, and consultative selling capabilities.
  • Experience using Salesforce CRM or similar CRM platforms.
  • Ability to travel extensively throughout Canada, North America, and internationally.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with single-use technologies, bioprocessing solutions, or pharmaceutical manufacturing environments.
  • Global account management experience.
  • Experience managing large enterprise accounts within multi-site organizations.
  • Demonstrated success working across matrix organizations and influencing without direct authority.
  • Bilingual English/French is considered an asset.
Core Competencies
  • Strategic Account Management
  • Executive Relationship Building
  • Business Development & Hunting Mindset
  • Complex Sales & Negotiation
  • Cross-Functional Leadership
  • Customer-Centric Problem Solving
  • Forecasting & Pipeline Management
  • Influence Without Authority
  • Communication & Presentation Skills
  • Organizational & Project Management Skills
Travel & Work Arrangement
  • Home-based remote position within Canada.
  • Approximately 50–60% travel, including customer visits and strategic business meetings.
  • International travel expected 2–4 times annually, primarily throughout North America and EMEA.
  • Candidate must have access to a major airport and be able to travel globally.
What We Offer
  • Competitive Compensation
  • Management Incentive Plan (MIP) Eligibility
  • Comprehensive Benefits Package
  • Retirement Savings Programs
  • Employee Stock Programs
  • Paid Time Off
  • Career Growth Opportunities
  • Inclusive and Collaborative Environment

Job Title: Regional Sales Manager
Location: Remote - Territory - TX, LA, OK, AR, KS, CO, WY, MS

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) role within its Industrial Technologies and Services (ITS) Business Unit will be responsible for sales growth and business development activities for air treatment solutions, to include air dryers, process chillers, nitrogen generators, oil-water separators, both new sales and rentals in the Southwestern US. The Regional Sales Manager will utilize their technical expertise in how the equipment is utilized in the market and will work closely with channel partners to cultivate, foster, and grow the presence of our products in the marketplace. Establishing and growing the distributor and OEM business relationships, growing revenue and market share for the portfolio, and maintaining profit margins are key for this role. Join us in making the ITS division of Ingersoll Rand an outstanding place to work where both our team and our company thrive! 

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement comprehensive sales strategies to expand market presence and achieve sales targets in the Southwest region.
  • Analyze market trends, customer needs, and competitive landscape to identify new business opportunities and areas for growth.
  • Follow established visitation frequencies for channel partners and achieve a cadence structure for reporting new opportunities, forecasting, revenue progress, etc.
  • Regularly track sales performance and key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess progress towards targets and identify areas for improvement.
  • Identify and recruit new distribution/channel partners and acquire new distribution/channel partners to expand market reach and penetration. This includes establishing and growing synergistic channel partners throughout the region.
  • Oversee the Distribution/Channel Partner network in the Southwest territory: act as the main point of contact for distributors, including business owners, sales teams, and service leaders and guide their activities and priorities. 
  • Partner with the ITS Support teams (manufacturing, service and warranty, customer service, e-commerce, etc.) to improve collaboration, establish best practices, and grow the channel partner and organizations market share.
  • Develop, mentor and coach channel partner sales team in fostering customer relationships, train distribution personnel, and assess their proficiency in supporting products and services.
  • Establish performance benchmarks for individual product lines to gauge distributor effectiveness and drive sales outcomes.
  • Identify underserved areas and geographies, devising business plans to expand coverage.
  • Spot gaps in market/industry coverage and competition and emerging market trends and refocus existing or new channels to address these gaps.
  • Resolve conflicts within the channel and region.
  • Maintain ongoing distribution engagement that supports consistent, high-impact activities.
  • Develop and manage an active opportunity pipeline with all partner organizations, collecting regular feedback to monitor progress.
  • Actively pursue and support competitive conversion opportunities identified in the pipeline.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales Enablement & Product Management to capitalize on pricing, product specifications, and new product potential.
  • Provide hands-on feedback to sales team, sharing insights on trends, competition, economics, and other factors to help identify and prioritize strategic opportunities.
  • Lead, motivate, and work with other members of the sales team and channel partners to meet revenue targets, ensure high level of new customer activity, and focus resources to achieve strategic account penetration.
  • Seek and communicate the voice of the customer (VOC) to build strong customer relationships, understand their needs, and communicate risks and opportunities to the ITS leadership team.
  • Collaborate with marketing & product management to establish market pricing and develop sales strategies to realize sales of existing and new products to meet or exceed revenue and profit targets.
  • Establish sales forecasts, plans & objectives for your region and by product line and provide weekly / monthly / yearly forecasting to update the business on short and long-term trends.
  • Track regional metrics to communicate key performance indicators relating to sales, profitability, market share and competitor activities.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, engineering technology, or business
  • 5+ years of industrial sales ideally in industrial equipment, compressed air, air treatment solutions (dryers, filtration, condensate management) or related sectors.

Core Competencies:

  • Formulate a clear and compelling regional sales strategy that aligns with the overall business objectives. This includes identifying market opportunities, defining target customer segments, and outlining a roadmap to achieve sales goals.
  • Optimizing the sales process, including following best practices, implementing sales methodologies, and continuously improving workflows through standard operating procedures. 
  • Ability to gather, interpret and effectively communicate product information in a clear, concise, way, using multiple communication channels (verbal, written, email, chat) to various internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical specifications, product technical literature, construction plans/drawings, commercial terms and conditions, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries from internal or external customers or suppliers.
  • Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of practical problems.
  • Uses technical knowledge to assess the potential application of company products, recommending solutions that meet customer needs, and advance the sales process.

Preferences:

  • Experience with air compressors and/or air dryers preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience using data to drive distributors behavior and success.
  • Understanding of principles of air compression and/or air treatment, and applications.
  • Understanding of commercial terms including payment terms, receivables, shipping terms, and contract terms and conditions review.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
Remote with the ability to travel up to 50% within the Southwest region.

Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $110,000 - $130,000. The total pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

What We Offer:
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Ingersoll Rand is a Fortune 500 company with a passion for making life better.  We do this by living our values, and through a relentless focus on the success of our customers and partnering with our employees to think and act like owners. We believe in sustainability through the development and distribution of a broad range of global brands designed to meet the needs of our customers in both efficient and responsible ways. Ingersoll Rand is a diverse and inclusive environment.  For more information visit: www.irco.com.


Job Summary:

The Territory Sales Manager – Champion Pneumatic is responsible for driving growth with dealers and distributors within an assigned regional territory. This role focuses on both managing and developing existing dealers and aggressively recruiting, onboarding, training, and activating new dealers, particularly those operating in the industrial market space. Success in this role requires strong channel development capability, strategic sales planning, and hands-on dealer engagement to expand Champion Pneumatics’ presence and market share.

Responsibilities:
 

  • Manage, develop, and grow existing dealers and distributors within the assigned territory.
  • Identify, recruit, and onboard new dealers, including those currently representing competing product lines.
  • Deliver ongoing product training and sales skills training to dealer sales teams to improve selling capabilities and technical knowledge.
  • Provide training as needed for dealer technicians, office personnel, and internal support roles.
  • Partner with dealer sales teams on account and project strategies to position Champion Pneumatic for maximum success.
  • Work closely with dealer leadership teams to assess business performance, improve organizational structure, and elevate their effectiveness in selling Champion Pneumatic products.
  • Conduct annual business planning, market development planning, and risk assessments with each dealer.
  • Collaborate on written gap-closure plans to address performance issues where necessary.
  • Quickly onboard and integrate new personnel within dealer organizations to accelerate productivity.
  • Identify and resolve dealer issues or obstacles that hinder sales performance.
  • Achieve bookings, revenue, dealer activation, and market share growth targets for assigned dealers.

Requirements:
 

  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • 3+ years of experience in industrial equipment Sales, HVAC Sales or Sales Equivalent.

Key Competencies
 

  • Proven leadership and the ability to influence across multiple teams within dealer organizations.
  • Strong strategic thinking and business planning skills, including the ability to assist dealers in developing long-term growth plans.
  • Ability to cultivate a collaborative, partnership-driven dealer culture that prioritizes customer success.
  • Strong communication, training, and problem solving skills.
  • High level of ownership and accountability for territory performance, dealer development, and market share growth.
  Preferences:
  • 3+ years of experience in industrial equipment sales, with compressed air industry experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience recruiting and developing new dealers or distributors, including those selling competitive lines.
  • Bachelor’s degree Engineering, Technical, Marketing, or Business preferred.

Travel & Work Requirement:

Remote-based position. Approximately 50% travel is required (visiting each dealer location at least once per quarter)
Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is Min - 100000 - Max - 120000 . The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Title: Service Supervisor, PAC - Centrifugal Product
Location: Great Lakes Region
(Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend)

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 
The Service Supervisor, PAC – Centrifugal Product is a highly visible leadership role responsible for the full service lifecycle of compressed-air equipment—from installation and commissioning through ongoing maintenance, repair, and long-term customer support. Leading a team of skilled Service Technicians, this individual plays a critical role in delivering an exceptional customer experience while driving service performance, business growth, and profitability.  Working closely with Sales and Service Coordination, the Service Supervisor ensures seamless execution across the customer lifecycle while maintaining full accountability for the Customer Center Service P&L. The role combines people leadership, customer engagement, operational ownership, and commercial responsibility—balancing customer satisfaction with strong service execution and financial performance.

This position is specifically aligned to the PAC centrifugal product line, a technically sophisticated and highly engineered segment of the compressed-air business. The supervisor serves as a key customer-facing leader, supports technicians in the field, manages service-team performance, and takes ownership of escalated customer, technical, and on-call situations requiring leadership beyond the initial service level.  The role spans a broad Great Lakes territory and offers a unique opportunity to help shape a newly expanded two-supervisor regional coverage model. Depending on the locations of the selected candidates, territories may be structured north/south or east/west—giving the new supervisors an opportunity to help establish the most effective service coverage strategy for the region.

This is a hybrid, field-oriented leadership opportunity offering significant autonomy, direct customer interaction, and meaningful influence over the success of the service organization. Travel is approximately 40%–50%, typically involving one or two overnight stays per week. While direct compressed-air or centrifugal-equipment experience is highly valued, candidates with strong technical aptitude and learning agility may also bring relevant experience from engineering, engineering technology, HVAC, industrial equipment, technical service, or industrial sales.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
 
Requirements: 
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 7+ years of relevant services experience (primarily with industrial equipment).
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 

Core Competencies:
  • Solid professional communication skills both verbal and written.
  • Advanced operating knowledge with Microsoft Office and general business applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of handheld and mobile technologies (smartphones, tablets) and network-based systems.
  • Demonstrated understanding of financial impacts related to process efficiency, cost control, and business performance.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requires interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.  

Preference: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or a relevant area
  • Managing budgets and processes strongly preferred

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • This role is Hybid / Remote US from Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend
  • Company vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Travel approximately 40 - 50% with one to two overnight stays per week. 
  • Regular daily travel to customer sites, including work outdoors and in mechanical or equipment rooms 
  • This position will have physical demands and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.

Pay Range: The range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is $115,000 - $140,000. The total pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. Job Title: Quality Engineer, Site Lead
Location:  Chicago, IL (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a visible, hands-on role with site quality lead responsibilities where your work directly impacts product integrity, customer confidence, and manufacturing performance. The Quality Engineer, Site Lead is responsible for the full range of Quality Engineering support, including quality systems, process improvement, validation, CAPA, auditing, risk assessment, training, and new product introduction support across the Elastomer Chicago manufacturing site. This role has primary ownership of ISO 9001 compliance and supports ISO 13485 medical device silicone operations as needed. It is a strong opportunity for a quality leader who enjoys being close to production, solving problems at the root, partnering across Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and leadership, and building a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. The position also leads Quality Technicians and Inspectors, ensuring the team is aligned, audit-ready, and focused on consistent product quality across both industrial and medical device environments.

Responsibilities
Quality Management System / Regulatory Compliance:

  • Develop, maintain, and execute quality procedures and work instructions to streamline processes and ensure compliance with FDA regulations, ISO standards, and other applicable regulatory requirements.

  • Oversee the development, management, maintenance, and effectiveness of the Elastomer BU Quality Management System, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 compliance.

  • Serve as Management Representative for the Elastomer BU Chicago site.

  • Ensure all SOPs and process documentation are created in accordance with the QMS and partner with departments to ensure effectiveness.

  • Ensure document control and revision control activities are maintained in compliance with QMS and regulatory requirements.

  • Responsible for ensuring all cleanroom requirements are met, as applicable.

Audits, CAPA, NCRs, and Customer Complaints:

  • Host customer and registrar audits and coordinate or perform internal quality and supplier audits as needed.

  • Lead and/or support internal and external CAPAs, NCRs, and customer complaints, including investigation, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and related documentation.

  • Change Control, Documentation, and Product Release

  • Review and assess change requests to ensure proper evaluation of impact on product quality, processes, and regulatory compliance.

  • Manage customer-submitted change requests through completion.

  • Review and approve engineering documentation, including validation protocols/reports, sample run requests, and manufacturing procedures, ensuring adherence to customer and regulatory requirements.

  • Ensure all products conform to validated processes and DMRs; perform lot release and related quality functions.

Production Quality, Process Control, and Continuous Improvement:

  • Assure reliability and consistency of production by monitoring processes and final output.

  • Implement statistical tools, including SPC, MSA, and GR&R, to ensure process control and measurement system reliability.

  • Leverage ISO 9001 continuous improvement principles to improve process efficiency and effectiveness.

  • Monitor key quality metrics and provide regular reporting to leadership.

Supplier Quality and Compliance:

  • Collaborate with Purchasing to co-manage the Approved Supplier List and evaluate suppliers to ensure product compliance.

  • Monitor supplier performance and rate suppliers through scorecard ratings.

  • Calibration, Preventive Maintenance, and Resource Planning

  • Provide oversight of the calibration and preventive maintenance programs to ensure compliance.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify equipment, testing, and resource needs for new or existing products, and communicate requirements to leadership.

Team Training: 

  • Conduct employee training sessions, as applicable.

Professional Development:

  • Maintain current quality management knowledge by studying industry trends, participating in educational opportunities, reading professional publications, and engaging in professional organizations and networking opportunities.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree ideally in industrial, mechanical / manufacturing engineering or similar field
  • 5+ years of significant professional experience in continuous quality improvement with progressive scope and responsibility.
  • 4+ years experience working within an ISO 9001 quality management system, including quality procedures, documentation, audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
  • 3+ years of experience in a quality manufacturing environment, with demonstrated leadership capability and working knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
  • 2+ years experience with statistical tools, data analysis, SPC, MSA, GR&R, process validation, IQ/OQ/PQ, and root cause analysis.


Core Competencies:

  • Regulatory Quality Leadership: Ability to interpret quality system requirements, maintain audit-ready processes, and guide site compliance in a regulated manufacturing environment.

  • Manufacturing Quality Problem Solving: Strong ability to investigate issues, analyze process variation, identify root cause, and drive practical corrective actions that improve product quality and process performance.

  • Cross-Functional Execution: Ability to work effectively across Quality, Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and leadership teams to align priorities, resolve issues, and support production and NPI needs.

  • Team Engagement & Quality Culture: Ability to work with cross-functional teams, drive issue resolution, train, coach, and hold team members accountable while reinforcing a culture of compliance, ownership, and continuous improvement.

  • Quality Systems, Data & Reporting Tools: Proficient in Microsoft Office and able to use quality data, documentation, reports, metrics, and system tools to track performance, support audits, manage corrective actions, and communicate quality trends to leadership.


Preferences:

  • Advanced degree, Engineering degree, or another technical field.

  • Experience working in Master Control QMS System

  • Continuous quality improvement experience in one or more medical product environments.

  • Experience working within an ISO 13485 quality management system, including medical device documentation, audit readiness, CAPA, and regulatory compliance.

  • Experience in silicone or rubber molding, including LSR, compression, or transfer molding.

  • Experience supporting medical device OEM customers.

  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR 820 and risk management, including ISO 14971.

Travel and Work Arrangements 

  • Position based onsite in Chicago, IL

  • Work Authorization: US Citizen or Permanent Resident


Pay Range
The base pay range for this role is $80-110k annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Service Supervisor, PAC - Centrifugal Product
Location: Great Lakes Region
(Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend)

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 
The Service Supervisor, PAC – Centrifugal Product is a highly visible leadership role responsible for the full service lifecycle of compressed-air equipment—from installation and commissioning through ongoing maintenance, repair, and long-term customer support. Leading a team of skilled Service Technicians, this individual plays a critical role in delivering an exceptional customer experience while driving service performance, business growth, and profitability.  Working closely with Sales and Service Coordination, the Service Supervisor ensures seamless execution across the customer lifecycle while maintaining full accountability for the Customer Center Service P&L. The role combines people leadership, customer engagement, operational ownership, and commercial responsibility—balancing customer satisfaction with strong service execution and financial performance.

This position is specifically aligned to the PAC centrifugal product line, a technically sophisticated and highly engineered segment of the compressed-air business. The supervisor serves as a key customer-facing leader, supports technicians in the field, manages service-team performance, and takes ownership of escalated customer, technical, and on-call situations requiring leadership beyond the initial service level.  The role spans a broad Great Lakes territory and offers a unique opportunity to help shape a newly expanded two-supervisor regional coverage model. Depending on the locations of the selected candidates, territories may be structured north/south or east/west—giving the new supervisors an opportunity to help establish the most effective service coverage strategy for the region.

This is a hybrid, field-oriented leadership opportunity offering significant autonomy, direct customer interaction, and meaningful influence over the success of the service organization. Travel is approximately 40%–50%, typically involving one or two overnight stays per week. While direct compressed-air or centrifugal-equipment experience is highly valued, candidates with strong technical aptitude and learning agility may also bring relevant experience from engineering, engineering technology, HVAC, industrial equipment, technical service, or industrial sales.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
 
Requirements: 
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 7+ years of relevant services experience (primarily with industrial equipment).
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 

Core Competencies:
  • Solid professional communication skills both verbal and written.
  • Advanced operating knowledge with Microsoft Office and general business applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of handheld and mobile technologies (smartphones, tablets) and network-based systems.
  • Demonstrated understanding of financial impacts related to process efficiency, cost control, and business performance.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requires interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.  

Preference: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or a relevant area
  • Managing budgets and processes strongly preferred

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • This role is Hybid / Remote US from Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend
  • Company vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Travel approximately 40 - 50% with one to two overnight stays per week. 
  • Regular daily travel to customer sites, including work outdoors and in mechanical or equipment rooms 
  • This position will have physical demands and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.

Pay Range: The range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is $115,000 - $140,000. The total pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Job Overview: 
The Service Supervisor, PAC – Centrifugal Product is a highly visible leadership role responsible for the full service lifecycle of compressed-air equipment—from installation and commissioning through ongoing maintenance, repair, and long-term customer support. Leading a team of skilled Service Technicians, this individual plays a critical role in delivering an exceptional customer experience while driving service performance, business growth, and profitability.  Working closely with Sales and Service Coordination, the Service Supervisor ensures seamless execution across the customer lifecycle while maintaining full accountability for the Customer Center Service P&L. The role combines people leadership, customer engagement, operational ownership, and commercial responsibility—balancing customer satisfaction with strong service execution and financial performance.

This position is specifically aligned to the PAC centrifugal product line, a technically sophisticated and highly engineered segment of the compressed-air business. The supervisor serves as a key customer-facing leader, supports technicians in the field, manages service-team performance, and takes ownership of escalated customer, technical, and on-call situations requiring leadership beyond the initial service level.  The role spans a broad Great Lakes territory and offers a unique opportunity to help shape a newly expanded two-supervisor regional coverage model. Depending on the locations of the selected candidates, territories may be structured north/south or east/west—giving the new supervisors an opportunity to help establish the most effective service coverage strategy for the region.

This is a hybrid, field-oriented leadership opportunity offering significant autonomy, direct customer interaction, and meaningful influence over the success of the service organization. Travel is approximately 40%–50%, typically involving one or two overnight stays per week. While direct compressed-air or centrifugal-equipment experience is highly valued, candidates with strong technical aptitude and learning agility may also bring relevant experience from engineering, engineering technology, HVAC, industrial equipment, technical service, or industrial sales.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
 
Requirements: 
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 7+ years of relevant services experience (primarily with industrial equipment).
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
