Job Title: Quality Engineer, Site Lead
Location:  Chicago, IL (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a visible, hands-on role with site quality lead responsibilities where your work directly impacts product integrity, customer confidence, and manufacturing performance. The Quality Site Lead is responsible for the full range of Quality Engineering support, including quality systems, process improvement, validation, CAPA, auditing, risk assessment, training, and new product introduction support across the Elastomer Chicago manufacturing site. This role has primary ownership of ISO 9001 compliance and supports ISO 13485 medical device silicone operations as needed. It is a strong opportunity for a quality leader who enjoys being close to production, solving problems at the root, partnering across Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and leadership, and building a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. The position also leads Quality Technicians and Inspectors, ensuring the team is aligned, audit-ready, and focused on consistent product quality across both industrial and medical device environments.

Responsibilities
Quality Management System / Regulatory Compliance: 
  • Develop, maintain, and execute quality procedures and work instructions to streamline processes and ensure compliance with FDA regulations, ISO standards, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Oversee the development, management, maintenance, and effectiveness of the Elastomer BU Quality Management System, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 compliance.
  • Serve as Management Representative for the Elastomer BU Chicago site.
  • Ensure all SOPs and process documentation are created in accordance with the QMS and partner with departments to ensure effectiveness.
  • Ensure document control and revision control activities are maintained in compliance with QMS and regulatory requirements.
  • Responsible for ensuring all cleanroom requirements are met, as applicable.

Audits, CAPA, NCRs, and Customer Complaints:
  • Host customer and registrar audits and coordinate or perform internal quality and supplier audits as needed.
  • Lead and/or support internal and external CAPAs, NCRs, and customer complaints, including investigation, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and related documentation.
  • Change Control, Documentation, and Product Release.
  • Review and assess change requests to ensure proper evaluation of impact on product quality, processes, and regulatory compliance.
    Manage customer-submitted change requests through completion.
  • Review and approve engineering documentation, including validation protocols/reports, sample run requests, and manufacturing procedures, ensuring adherence to customer and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure all products conform to validated processes and DMRs; perform lot release and related quality functions.

Production Quality, Process Control, and Continuous Improvement:
  • Assure reliability and consistency of production by monitoring processes and final output.
  • Implement statistical tools, including SPC, MSA, and GR&R, to ensure process control and measurement system reliability.
  • Leverage ISO 9001 continuous improvement principles to improve process efficiency and effectiveness.
    Monitor key quality metrics and provide regular reporting to leadership.

Supplier Quality and Compliance:
  • Collaborate with Purchasing to co-manage the Approved Supplier List and evaluate suppliers to ensure product compliance.
  • Monitor supplier performance and rate suppliers through scorecard ratings.
  • Calibration, Preventive Maintenance, and Resource Planning
  • Provide oversight of the calibration and preventive maintenance programs to ensure compliance.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify equipment, testing, and resource needs for new or existing products, and communicate requirements to leadership.

Team Leadership, Training, and Talent Management:
  • Achieve quality assurance human resource objectives by recruiting, selecting, orienting, training, scheduling, coaching, counseling, and disciplining employees.
  • Communicate job expectations and lead team talent and performance management processes.
  • Conduct employee training sessions, as applicable.

Professional Development:
  • Maintain current quality management knowledge by studying industry trends, participating in educational opportunities, reading professional publications, and engaging in professional organizations and networking opportunities.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree ideally in industrial, mechanical / manufacturing engineering or similar field
  • 5+ years of significant professional experience in continuous quality improvement with progressive scope and responsibility.
  • 4+ years experience working within an ISO 9001 quality management system, including quality procedures, documentation, audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
  • 3+ years leading teams, ideally in a quality manufacturing environment with proven experience with Good Manufacturing Practices.
  • 2+ years experience with statistical tools, data analysis, SPC, MSA, GR&R, process validation, IQ/OQ/PQ, and root cause analysis.

Core Competencies:
  • Regulatory Quality Leadership: Ability to interpret quality system requirements, maintain audit-ready processes, and guide site compliance in a regulated manufacturing environment.
  • Manufacturing Quality Problem Solving: Strong ability to investigate issues, analyze process variation, identify root cause, and drive practical corrective actions that improve product quality and process performance.
  • Cross-Functional Execution: Ability to work effectively across Quality, Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, and leadership teams to align priorities, resolve issues, and support production and NPI needs.
  • Team Leadership & Quality Culture: Ability to lead cross-functional teams, drive issue resolution, train, coach, and hold quality team members accountable while reinforcing a culture of compliance, ownership, and continuous improvement.
  • Quality Systems, Data & Reporting Tools: Proficient in Microsoft Office and able to use quality data, documentation, reports, metrics, and system tools to track performance, support audits, manage corrective actions, and communicate quality trends to leadership.

Preferences:
  • Advanced degree, Engineering degree, or another technical field.
  • Experience working in Master Control QMS System
  • Continuous quality improvement experience in one or more medical product environments.
  • Experience working within an ISO 13485 quality management system, including medical device documentation, audit readiness, CAPA, and regulatory compliance.
  • Experience in silicone or rubber molding, including LSR, compression, or transfer molding.
  • Experience supporting medical device OEM customers.
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR 820 and risk management, including ISO 14971.

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • Position based onsite in Chicago, IL (near O'Hare Airport)
  • Work Authorization: US Citizen or Permanent Resident

Pay Range

Job Overview:  

The Material Handler under general supervision, works to ensure we are continually shipping the right products to customers in a timely manner. This job’s main responsibility will be for Freight Shipments but occasional small parcel and other work as required.

Responsibilities:  

  • Follow company packing procedures and standards
  • Reviews shipments for quality and accuracy, reviews accompanying documents for accuracy.
  • Confirms shipping details or special instructions
  • Collects and properly disposes of cardboard, and strapping; maintains a safe and clean work environment.
  • Work at different stations as needed
  • Inspect, weigh, and package products
  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment
  • Typical work activities are sealing boxes and placing labels on packages
  • Assemble Skids and use TMS system to determine LTL Carrier
  • Ability to Use MRP system

  • Performs other related duties as assigned. 

Requirements:  

  • High School Diploma or GED  
  • 6+ months of experience in a manufacturing environment
  • Ability to Work overtime as Required

Core Competencies:   

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills

Preferences:  

  • 2+ years of experience in a manufacturing environment
  • Knowledge of inventory processes  
  • Previous Material Handling experience (fork lift experience preferred) 
  • Excellent planning and organizational skills. 
  • Proven ability to follow through on commitments and details. 
  • Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skill. 
  • Proven team player. 
  • Demonstrated Problem Solving Skills

  • This is a fully onsite role requiring the ability to stand or walk for the duration of the shift in a fast-paced environment, with frequent bending and stooping. The role also requires regularly lifting up to 35 pounds unassisted and working in a non-climate-controlled environment.

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 
The Service Supervisor, PAC – Centrifugal Product is a highly visible leadership role responsible for the full service lifecycle of compressed-air equipment—from installation and commissioning through ongoing maintenance, repair, and long-term customer support. Leading a team of skilled Service Technicians, this individual plays a critical role in delivering an exceptional customer experience while driving service performance, business growth, and profitability.  Working closely with Sales and Service Coordination, the Service Supervisor ensures seamless execution across the customer lifecycle while maintaining full accountability for the Customer Center Service P&L. The role combines people leadership, customer engagement, operational ownership, and commercial responsibility—balancing customer satisfaction with strong service execution and financial performance.

This position is specifically aligned to the PAC centrifugal product line, a technically sophisticated and highly engineered segment of the compressed-air business. The supervisor serves as a key customer-facing leader, supports technicians in the field, manages service-team performance, and takes ownership of escalated customer, technical, and on-call situations requiring leadership beyond the initial service level.  The role spans a broad Great Lakes territory and offers a unique opportunity to help shape a newly expanded two-supervisor regional coverage model. Depending on the locations of the selected candidates, territories may be structured north/south or east/west—giving the new supervisors an opportunity to help establish the most effective service coverage strategy for the region.

This is a hybrid, field-oriented leadership opportunity offering significant autonomy, direct customer interaction, and meaningful influence over the success of the service organization. Travel is approximately 40%–50%, typically involving one or two overnight stays per week. While direct compressed-air or centrifugal-equipment experience is highly valued, candidates with strong technical aptitude and learning agility may also bring relevant experience from engineering, engineering technology, HVAC, industrial equipment, technical service, or industrial sales.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
 
Requirements: 
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 7+ years of relevant services experience (primarily with industrial equipment).
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 

Core Competencies:
  • Solid professional communication skills both verbal and written.
  • Advanced operating knowledge with Microsoft Office and general business applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of handheld and mobile technologies (smartphones, tablets) and network-based systems.
  • Demonstrated understanding of financial impacts related to process efficiency, cost control, and business performance.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requires interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.  

Preference: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or a relevant area
  • Managing budgets and processes strongly preferred

Travel & Work Arrangements:
  • This role is Hybid / Remote US from Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Fort Wayne or South Bend
  • Company vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Travel approximately 40 - 50% with one to two overnight stays per week. 
  • Regular daily travel to customer sites, including work outdoors and in mechanical or equipment rooms 
  • This position will have physical demands and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.

Pay Range: The range for this role, including incentive opportunities, is $115,000 - $140,000. Job Overview:

 

The Quality Technician is responsible for supporting product and process quality through accurate inspection, measurement, documentation, and problem-solving activities. This position performs visual, dimensional, and functional inspections to ensure products meet established drawings, specifications, procedures, and quality standards. The Quality Technician will support non-conformance containment, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and continuous improvement initiatives. 

 

Responsibilities:

  • Perform visual, dimensional, and functional inspections of parts and products according to drawings, specifications, procedures, and work instructions.
  • Accurately measure parts, interpret CMM reports, and validate questionable or suspect measurements.
  • Complete First Article Inspections (FAI), receiving inspections, and other required product or process inspections.
  • Identify non-conforming material and initiate appropriate containment activities to prevent further processing or shipment.
  • Participate in root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and structured problem-solving activities.
  • Perform all quality activities in accordance with established Standard Process Instructions (SPIs), Standard Work, and company quality requirements.
  • Support Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement initiatives, and departmental quality projects.
  • Maintain a strong safety focus, follow all safety requirements, and perform additional duties as needed to support business operations.

Requirements:

 
  • 5+ years of related quality inspection experience in a fast-paced machining or manufacturing environment.
  • Strong blueprint reading and interpretation skills, including drawings, specifications, and inspection requirements.
  • Ability to select and properly use appropriate precision measurement and inspection devices.
  • Ability to read and interpret CMM reports and validate measurement results.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ability to accurately complete inspection and quality documentation.
  • Ability to lift up to 40 lbs. repetitively and stand or walk for extended periods throughout the shift.
  • Ability to frequently grasp and handle parts and perform physical activities including reaching, stooping, kneeling, crouching, or crawling as required.
  • Ability to work safely in a manufacturing environment with moving equipment, machining oils/coolants, varying temperatures and humidity, and noise levels that may range from 75–87 dBA; requires close visual acuity for drawings, measurements, inspection documents, and computer screens

Preferences:

  • 2 year Associate’s or technical degree
  • Solid understanding of GD&T and Datum Structures
  • Mechanical aptitude
  • CMM Programming a Plus
  • Understanding of Capability studies and Gage RR

Job Overview: 

This is an Inside Sales & Service Representative - Order Management position based out of one of the following Customer Centers: Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; or Phoenix, AZ. This role includes sales support from the time of inquiry to delivery, which requires parts/equipment identification, quoting, order confirmation/purchase order receipt, pricing, order processing, expediting, and problem solving. As the ISS Representative becomes more experienced, he/she is able to continue to support the outside sales force with lead generation, market intelligence, and contact with current customers. For the most experienced, they may be assigned to special projects, which require hands-on supervision of highly complex orders or those that require significant coordination with external entities. 

Responsibilities:

 
  • Act as key customer contact to provide information to customers on complete sales cycle from order acceptance through delivery.  
  • Accurately enter, manage and balance sales and service agreements. 
  • Follow up with customers and outside sales team to provide order status updates.  
  • Manage inventory to stocking levels. Receive stock and/or service parts, load and/or off load trucks and coordinate the return of equipment as needed.  
  • Ensure the order process is complete and error-free.  
  • Manage outside purchases and product transportation expenses effectively and efficiently.  
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance.  
  • Operate forklift within compliance as needed.  
  • Ensure that all paperwork, purchase orders, etc. are maintained to respond to customer inquiries timely and ensure internal process requirements.  
  • Prepare all sales and activity reports, presentations, studies and research as requested.  
  • Mentor peers and share best practices with those less experienced as needed.


Requirements:

  • 2+ years of experience in customer service-related role
  • 2+ years of experience using Microsoft Office computer applications

  
Core Competencies:

  • Technical background highly preferred  
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills  
  • Customer service focus – understand the need, solve problems, and respond in an efficient manner  
  • Organizational skills – ability to manage time and multi-task.  


Preferences:

  • Associate or bachelor's degree in engineering or a similar technical field 
  • Technical background
  • Experience using Salesforce


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  •  This position will be based in one of the above Customer Centers, and may travel occasionally within the US for meetings, employee training, and other business needs (5-10%).

 The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is [$54,300 – $126,600]. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
Requirements:
  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
Core Competencies:
  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner
Preferences:
  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Pay Range:
Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $35.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

About ILC Dover
ILC Dover is a global leader in engineered products that protect people, products, and brands. From space exploration and defense systems to pharmaceutical and industrial applications, ILC Dover delivers mission?critical solutions where performance, reliability, and safety matter most. ILC Dover offers competitive compensation and benefits within a collaborative, engineering?driven culture that values innovation, teamwork, and technical excellence.

Job Overview: 
The Project Engineer supports the successful execution of engineering and production programs related to Extravehicular Activity (EVA) spacesuit systems by coordinating cross-functional teams, tracking progress, and ensuring timely achievement of key program milestones. This role assists in planning, organizing, and managing projects across spacesuit hardware development, integration, and production activities, working closely with engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to deliver flight-critical hardware on schedule, within scope, and within budget.
This position is based at the Frederica, Delaware manufacturing facility and directly supports the development, assembly, integration, testing, and sustainment of EVA spacesuit systems, with a primary focus on the Space Suit Assembly (SSA) in support of NASA programs. The Project Engineer plays a key role in managing the full hardware lifecycle—from design release through fabrication, production, verification, and delivery—ensuring alignment with NASA requirements and strict adherence to human spaceflight safety and quality standards.


Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and monitor EVA spacesuit hardware projects from design release through production, integration, and delivery
  • Serve as a liaison between engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to ensure alignment on production priorities, requirements, and schedules
  • Support execution of spacesuit assembly and integration activities at the Frederica site, ensuring readiness for build, test, and delivery
  • Ensure hardware fabrication and production efforts are completed on schedule and within budget constraints
  • Gather and manage technical, manufacturing, and program data to support requirements definition, build readiness, and production execution
  • Lead hardware failure investigations for spacesuit components and assemblies; facilitate root cause analysis (RCA) and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) across engineering and factory operations
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication with program managers and stakeholders regarding risks, issues, and impacts to cost, schedule, or technical performance
  • Interface with NASA customers to communicate project status, technical progress, risks, and key milestones through formal reviews, reports, and coordination meetings
  • Support integration, test, and verification activities for EVA hardware, ensuring compliance with NASA program requirements and certification standards
  • Assist with transition of hardware from development into production, including coordination of build plans, work instructions, and configuration control
  • Support project planning activities across proposal, contract execution, and program lifecycle phases for EVA spacesuit programs
  • Conduct routine tasks as directed in support of EVA program execution


*This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.


Qualifications:
  • Must be able to access shared government program databases (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident)
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field

Core Competencies: 
  • Experience in manufacturing, engineering, or product development environment preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and interface control documents (ICDs)
  • Interest in project management and product development (PMP or CAPM a plus)
  • Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking abilities
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic knowledge of project management methodologies and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project)
  • Strong collaboration, problem-solving skills, and ability to work effectively in team environments (including navigating constructive conflict)
  • Experience with hardware development lifecycle including design, build, test, and qualification phases
  • Experience supporting or participating in hardware failure investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation preferred


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
  • Fully Site Based in Frederica, DE
  • Availability to travel up to 25 % of the time (e.g., customer visits, training at our technical centers, trade shows, etc.).
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to wet or humid conditions (non-weather); fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals.  The employee is frequently exposed to work near moving mechanical parts.  The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions.   • Assemble sub-components to create final products in accordance with specifications. 

  • Perform labeling, cleaning, and packaging of assembled products. 

  • Maintain organization and cleanliness within the warehouse and work areas. 

  • Assist with keeping inventory levels of parts and supplies organized and efficiently stocked. 

  • Collaborate with team members to complete assigned tasks and support production goals. 

  • Perform other duties as required by the Production Department. 

 

Requirements 

  • High School Diploma or GED required 

  • 1-2 years of experience in manufacturing, assembly, or warehouse environments 

  • Forklift operation experience and certification 

  • Ability to advise management on inventory levels for parts and supplies 

  • Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and a willingness to learn new processes 

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively as part of a team 

 

Physical Requirements 

  • Ability to lift up to 40 pounds 

  • Ability to sit, stand, walk, and climb stairs as required  

  • Comfort working with chemicals as outlined in Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and using appropriate safety equipment such as dust masks, goggles, UV goggles, sleeve protectors, gloves, and back support

job.description:

Job title: Machine Operator

Location: Springfield, MO (Onsite)


Job Summary

Set up and operate a variety of machine tools to produce precision parts. Applies knowledge of mechanics, shop mathematics, metal properties, and machining procedures.  Construct, assemble, or rebuild machines, such as blowers, pumps, boosters, and similar equipment used in such industries as transportation, manufacturing or wastewater treatment.

Responsibilities

  • Calculate dimensions and tolerances using knowledge of mathematics and instruments such as micrometers and calipers.
  • Create, utilize and improve Standard Work combinations sheets to document machining and assembly processes to ensure consistency and repeatability.
  • Participate in the 5 Why Process to ensure real time problem solving and drive continuous improvement.
  • Align and secure holding fixtures, cutting tools, attachments, accessories, and materials onto machines.
  • Select the appropriate tools, machines, and materials to be used in preparation of machinery work.
  • Machine parts to specifications using machine tools such as lathes, milling machines, shapers, or grinders.
  • Set up, adjust, and operate all of the basic machine tools and many specialized or advanced variation tools to perform precision machining operations.
  • Measure, examine, and test completed parts to detect defects and ensure conformance to specifications, using precision instruments such as micrometers.
  • Set controls to regulate machining, or enter commands to retrieve, input, or edit computerized machine control media.
  • Position and fasten work pieces.
  • Position and align components for assembly, manually or using hoists.
  • Set and verify parts clearances.
  • Rework, repair, and replace damaged parts or assemblies.
  • Reads, interprets and follows Bill of Material to pull parts for assembly and submits corrections as needed.
  • Assemble units of a variety of sizes and models through use of standard work and interpretation of Engineering controlled documents.
  • Check work pieces to ensure that they are properly lubricated and cooled.
  • Confer with engineering, supervisory, and manufacturing personnel to exchange technical information.
  • Operate equipment to verify operational efficiency.
  • Clean and lubricate machines, tools, and equipment to remove grease, rust, stains, and foreign matter.
  • Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned.

 

 Education Requirements / Certifications

  • 1-2 years’ experience working in a manufacturing environment preferred
  • 1-2 years’ assembly and or CNC machining preferred

 
Experience / Skill Requirements         

  • Mechanical - Knowledge of machines and tools, including their designs, uses, and maintenance.
  • Production and Processing - Knowledge of raw materials, production processes, quality control, costs, and other techniques for maximizing the effective manufacture and distribution of goods.
  • Mathematics - Knowledge of arithmetic and algebra.
  • Operation Monitoring - Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.
  • Quality Control Analysis - Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.
  • Operation and Control - Controlling operations of equipment or systems.
  • Troubleshooting - Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.
  • Equipment Maintenance - Performing routine maintenance on equipment.

 

Tools/Technology Requirements: 

  • Ability to read blueprints, including geometric dimensioning and tolerance.
  • Ability to determine and complete offsets through basic mathematics.

 

Key Competencies

  • Knowledge of inventory processes.
  • Process driven and systematic in their approach to completing their work.
  • Ability to identify and solve problems.
  • Ability to pass certification for Powered Industrial Vehicle license.
 

What We Offer

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:

All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.

Requirements:

Preferences:
  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.

  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.

ILC Dover is a global leader in engineered products that protect people, products, and brands. ILC Dover offers competitive compensation and benefits within a collaborative, engineering driven culture that values innovation, teamwork, and technical excellence.

 

Job Overview: 

The Project Engineer supports the successful execution of product development projects by coordinating cross-functional teams, tracking progress, and ensuring timely achievement of key milestones. This role assists in planning, organizing, and managing projects across designated product lines, working closely with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to deliver results on schedule, within scope, and within budget.

This position will directly support the development, integration, and sustainment of Extravehicular Activity (EVA) spacesuit systems, with a primary focus on the Space Suit Assembly (SSA) in support of NASA programs. The Project Engineer will contribute to management of the full hardware lifecycle, from design and fabrication through test, verification, and operational readiness, ensuring alignment with customer requirements and adherence to critical human spaceflight safety standards.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and monitor engineering projects from initiation through delivery
  • Gather required data from end-users to evaluate objectives, goals, and scope to create technical specifications
  • Serve as liaison between engineering and non-engineering departments to ensure that all targets and requirements are met
  • Ensure engineering projects are completed on schedule and within budget
  • Lead hardware failure investigations, facilitate root cause analysis (RCA), and drive implementation of corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) in coordination with engineering, quality, and manufacturing teams
  • Keep program managers and other project stakeholders informed of key issues that may impact project completion, budget, or other results
  • Support project planning activity during pre-bid, proposal, negotiation and contract phases
  • Briefs the NASA customer on the technical aspects of Extra-vehicular Mobility Unit (EMU) projects through project coordination meetings, status reports and other forms of communication
  • Conducts routine tasks as directed


Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field
  • 4+ years of experience in manufacturing, engineering, or product development environment preferred

Preference: 
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and interface control documents (ICDs)
  • Interest in project management and product development (PMP or CAPM a plus)
  • Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking abilities
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic knowledge of project management methodologies and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project)
  • Strong collaboration, problem-solving skills, and ability to work effectively in team environments (including navigating constructive conflict)
  • Experience with hardware development lifecycle including design, build, test, and qualification phases
  • Experience supporting or participating in hardware failure investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation preferred
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Availability to travel up to 25 % of the time (e.g., customer visits, training at our technical centers, trade shows, etc.).
  • Onsite position

Job Overview: 
The Project Engineer supports the successful execution of engineering and production programs related to Extravehicular Activity (EVA) spacesuit systems by coordinating cross-functional teams, tracking progress, and ensuring timely achievement of key program milestones. This role assists in planning, organizing, and managing projects across spacesuit hardware development, integration, and production activities, working closely with engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to deliver flight-critical hardware on schedule, within scope, and within budget.
This position is based at the Frederica, Delaware manufacturing facility and directly supports the development, assembly, integration, testing, and sustainment of EVA spacesuit systems, with a primary focus on the Space Suit Assembly (SSA) in support of NASA programs. The Project Engineer plays a key role in managing the full hardware lifecycle—from design release through fabrication, production, verification, and delivery—ensuring alignment with NASA requirements and strict adherence to human spaceflight safety and quality standards.


Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and monitor EVA spacesuit hardware projects from design release through production, integration, and delivery
  • Serve as a liaison between engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to ensure alignment on production priorities, requirements, and schedules
  • Support execution of spacesuit assembly and integration activities at the Frederica site, ensuring readiness for build, test, and delivery
  • Ensure hardware fabrication and production efforts are completed on schedule and within budget constraints
  • Gather and manage technical, manufacturing, and program data to support requirements definition, build readiness, and production execution
  • Lead hardware failure investigations for spacesuit components and assemblies; facilitate root cause analysis (RCA) and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) across engineering and factory operations
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication with program managers and stakeholders regarding risks, issues, and impacts to cost, schedule, or technical performance
  • Interface with NASA customers to communicate project status, technical progress, risks, and key milestones through formal reviews, reports, and coordination meetings
  • Support integration, test, and verification activities for EVA hardware, ensuring compliance with NASA program requirements and certification standards
  • Assist with transition of hardware from development into production, including coordination of build plans, work instructions, and configuration control
  • Support project planning activities across proposal, contract execution, and program lifecycle phases for EVA spacesuit programs
  • Conduct routine tasks as directed in support of EVA program execution


*This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.


Qualifications:
  • Must be able to access shared government program databases (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident)
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field

Core Competencies: 
  • Experience in manufacturing, engineering, or product development environment preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and interface control documents (ICDs)
  • Interest in project management and product development (PMP or CAPM a plus)
  • Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking abilities
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic knowledge of project management methodologies and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project)
  • Strong collaboration, problem-solving skills, and ability to work effectively in team environments (including navigating constructive conflict)
  • Experience with hardware development lifecycle including design, build, test, and qualification phases
  • Experience supporting or participating in hardware failure investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation preferred


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
  • Fully Site Based in Frederica, DE
  • Availability to travel up to 25 % of the time (e.g., customer visits, training at our technical centers, trade shows, etc.).
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to wet or humid conditions (non-weather); fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals.  The employee is frequently exposed to work near moving mechanical parts.  The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
Requirements:
  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
Core Competencies:
  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner
Preferences:
  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Pay Range:
Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $35.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

Job Overview: 
The Project Engineer supports the successful execution of engineering and production programs related to Extravehicular Activity (EVA) spacesuit systems by coordinating cross-functional teams, tracking progress, and ensuring timely achievement of key program milestones. This role assists in planning, organizing, and managing projects across spacesuit hardware development, integration, and production activities, working closely with engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to deliver flight-critical hardware on schedule, within scope, and within budget.
This position is based at the Frederica, Delaware manufacturing facility and directly supports the development, assembly, integration, testing, and sustainment of EVA spacesuit systems, with a primary focus on the Space Suit Assembly (SSA) in support of NASA programs. The Project Engineer plays a key role in managing the full hardware lifecycle—from design release through fabrication, production, verification, and delivery—ensuring alignment with NASA requirements and strict adherence to human spaceflight safety and quality standards.


Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and monitor EVA spacesuit hardware projects from design release through production, integration, and delivery
  • Serve as a liaison between engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to ensure alignment on production priorities, requirements, and schedules
  • Support execution of spacesuit assembly and integration activities at the Frederica site, ensuring readiness for build, test, and delivery
  • Ensure hardware fabrication and production efforts are completed on schedule and within budget constraints
  • Gather and manage technical, manufacturing, and program data to support requirements definition, build readiness, and production execution
  • Lead hardware failure investigations for spacesuit components and assemblies; facilitate root cause analysis (RCA) and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) across engineering and factory operations
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication with program managers and stakeholders regarding risks, issues, and impacts to cost, schedule, or technical performance
  • Interface with NASA customers to communicate project status, technical progress, risks, and key milestones through formal reviews, reports, and coordination meetings
  • Support integration, test, and verification activities for EVA hardware, ensuring compliance with NASA program requirements and certification standards
  • Assist with transition of hardware from development into production, including coordination of build plans, work instructions, and configuration control
  • Support project planning activities across proposal, contract execution, and program lifecycle phases for EVA spacesuit programs
  • Conduct routine tasks as directed in support of EVA program execution


*This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.


Qualifications:
  • Must be able to access shared government program databases (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident)
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field

Core Competencies: 
  • Experience in manufacturing, engineering, or product development environment preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and interface control documents (ICDs)
  • Interest in project management and product development (PMP or CAPM a plus)
  • Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking abilities
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Basic knowledge of project management methodologies and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project)
  • Strong collaboration, problem-solving skills, and ability to work effectively in team environments (including navigating constructive conflict)
  • Experience with hardware development lifecycle including design, build, test, and qualification phases
  • Experience supporting or participating in hardware failure investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation preferred


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
  • Fully Site Based in Frederica, DE
  • Availability to travel up to 25 % of the time (e.g., customer visits, training at our technical centers, trade shows, etc.).
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to wet or humid conditions (non-weather); fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals.  The employee is frequently exposed to work near moving mechanical parts.  The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Job Title: Sr. Process Engineer

Location: Lincolnshire, IL

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Process Engineer is responsible for the development, optimization and sustaining robust molding processes for liquid silicone rubber (LSR) and high consistency rubber (HCR) utilizing injection, transfer and compression molding processes. The Process Engineer plays a key role in driving process capability, optimizing cycle times, reducing scrap, troubleshooting production issues and ensuring stable manufacturing performance across all molding work centers.

The Process Engineer collaborates closely with the Tooling, Production, Quality, NPI and Maintenance teams to ensure successful product launches, consistent quality and efficient manufacturing processes. 

Responsibilities:
  • Develop, validate, and optimize LSR and HCR molding processes (injection, compression, transfer) using scientific molding principles and DOE methodologies.
  • Establish robust process parameters, including injection/fill profiles, pack/hold strategies, cure cycles, and thermal controls to improve capability (Cp/Cpk) and reduce variation.
  • Troubleshoot complex molding defects (flash, short shots, voids, knit lines, shrinkage, dimensional variation, and cure issues) using structured root cause analysis and corrective actions.
  • Partner with tooling and maintenance teams to qualify molds, optimize gate/vent designs, improve thermal management, and ensure validated equipment performance.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on cycle time reduction, scrap minimization, OEE improvement, material yield optimization, and Lean/Kaizen implementation.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) through feasibility assessments, mold trials, process qualification, production launch, and transition to manufacturing.
  • Develop and maintain process documentation, standardized parameter sheets, work instructions, and SPC-based process monitoring while training operators and technicians on best practices.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Production, Quality, and Estimating teams to improve manufacturability, manage process changes, and ensure quality, customer, and business objectives are achieved.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in an Engineering (Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials, Plastics, Polymer)
  • 5+ years’ direct experience in silicone and/or rubber molding

Competences: 
  • Liquid Silicone Rubber (LSR) injection.
  • High Consistency Rubber (HCR) molding.
  • Compression and transfer molding.
  • Cure cycles, post-cure and material behavior.
  • Tool design elements (cavitation, gating, venting, steel types).
  • Experience using DOE, SPC and statistical tools for process improvement.
  • Strong ability to interpret engineering drawings, GD & T, CAD models, customer and regulatory specifications.
  • Demonstrated success in troubleshooting complex molding issues.

Preferences:
  • Experience with SolidWorks or other 3D modelling software.
  • Experience with mold flow analysis (or ability to interpret results).
  • Background in medical, automotive, aerospace or industrial silicone components.
  • Experience supporting APQP, PPAP and customer audits.
  • Experience with automation, vision inspection and deflashing /trimming technologies.
  • Background with adhesion/bonding techniques, multi-shot molding and over molding.
  • RJG/Paulson certification or silicone-specific molding training.
  • Familiarity with ISO13485 and clean room procedures would be beneficial.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Fully onsite based

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $100,000-$125,000.  The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.
 
Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
 

  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
 
Requirements:

  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.

  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner.
 
Preferences:

  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Job Title: Sr Electro-Mechanical Engineer


Location: Hampton, NJ
 

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

 

Job Overview:

Power tools Electro-Mechanical Engineer dedicated to new product development located in Hampton, NJ.  At Ingersoll Rand Power Tools, we design, engineer and manufacture cordless and corded electric power tools for the assembly, industrial and vehicle repair markets.  This person will work closely with global cross-functional teams comprised of software, firmware, electrical and mechanical engineers as well as strategic sourcing partners, quality, operations, and product management.  The Mechatronics Engineer’s responsibilities are to develop new power tools by creating new product concepts, prototypes, testing and developing final designs ready for commercial launch.  This person must be a team player, form strong ties with others, manage a multitude of tasks, communicate clearly, and be effective and comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop and enhance mechanical, electrical and electro-mechanical systems for innovative new power tools that meet customer needs and global industry standards.
  • Prepare design concepts for analysis and rapid prototype validation.
  • Lead projects while collaborating with global internal team members, suppliers and operations from conceptual design through production launch.
  • Coordinate and drive the completion of testing.  Work closely and cooperatively with lab technicians during test execution to assure that test objectives are met.
  • Develop and maintain documentation including layouts, drawings, specifications, bills of material, test plans, lab reports and technical construction files.
  • Provide support to strategic sourcing partners, manufacturing, customer service, procurement, quality assurance departments and product management.

 

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor degree in Mechanical, Mechatronics, Electro-mechanical or Electrical Engineering
  • 5+ years of experience

 

Core Competencies:  

  • Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and manage multiple concurrent assignments.
  • Knowledge of electronic circuit and electrical design, including microprocessors, sensors, wiring, connectors, and PCBAs; Altium experience preferred.
  • Experience integrating wireless technologies such as Wi-Fi 6, 5G, Zigbee, and Bluetooth into electro-mechanical assemblies preferred.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.

Job Title: Facilities Maintenance Technician

Location: Springfield, MO 
 

Position Summary

The Maintenance Facilities Technician is responsible for maintaining the manufacturing facility, grounds, utilities, and building systems to ensure a safe, reliable, and efficient work environment. This role performs preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, and inspections of facility equipment and infrastructure, including HVAC, plumbing, electrical, lighting, compressed air systems, and general building maintenance. The technician works closely with production, engineering, safety, and maintenance teams to minimize downtime and support operational excellence.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Perform routine inspections, preventive maintenance, and repairs on facility equipment and building systems.
  • Maintain HVAC, plumbing, electrical, lighting, fire protection, compressed air, and utility systems.
  • Troubleshoot and repair facility-related issues to minimize disruptions to manufacturing operations.
  • Conduct building maintenance activities including painting, carpentry, flooring, and general repairs.
  • Monitor facility systems for performance, safety, and regulatory compliance.
  • Support facility improvement projects, equipment installations, and office renovations.
  • Coordinate with outside contractors and vendors for specialized maintenance and service work.
  • Maintain maintenance records, work orders, and preventive maintenance documentation.
  • Respond to emergency maintenance requests and facility-related breakdowns.
  • Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental, company safety, and regulatory requirements.
  • Assist with snow removal, grounds maintenance, waste disposal, and housekeeping activities as needed.
  • Identify opportunities to improve facility reliability, energy efficiency, and cost effectiveness.
  • Participate in safety audits, inspections, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Support production downtime activities and plant shutdown maintenance schedules.

Required Qualifications

  • 3 years of maintenance or facilities experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Working knowledge of electrical, mechanical, plumbing, HVAC, and general building maintenance systems.
  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical manuals, and schematics.
  • Proficiency using maintenance management systems and basic computer applications.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently and prioritize multiple tasks.

Preferred Qualifications

  • HVAC certification.
  • Electrical maintenance experience.
  • Refrigeration or compressed air system experience.
  • Forklift, scissor lift, or aerial lift certification.
  • OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification.
  • Technical certification, vocational training, or associate degree in maintenance, industrial technology, or related field preferred.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.
 
Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
 

  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
 
Requirements:

  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
 
Core Competencies: 

  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner.
 
Preferences:

  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply. 
 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Job Overview:
We are looking for a skilled assembler to perform a variety of tasks as assigned in conjunction with the assembly of our product. You will ensure all parts fit correctly and are suitable for the final product. This position is responsible for safely performing high-level continuous work to quality standards. Assignments may change based on business demands.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform a variety of tasks to support the assembly and test of industrial machinery and compression equipment within the plant, in accordance with predetermined standard work.
  • Read, understand, and apply method sheets, assembly diagrams, and blueprints.  
  • Detect quality defects and unsafe conditions.
  • Be knowledgeable, and follow all applicable safety rules and procedures.
  • Interpretation of drawings and specifications to determine dimensions, identify materials for construction, and assemble components.
  • Operate power pneumatic and hand tools required for performing job duties.
  • Maintain and inspect tools and equipment and create work orders for repaired as needed.
  • Loading and unloading of equipment utilizing fork trucks, and hoists.
  • Work in a team environment, and assist co-workers in other areas as needed/directed, suggesting process improvement ideas.
  • Maintains safe and clean working environment by complying with procedures, rules, and regulations.
  • Material handling activities may include managing inventory levels by checking stock to determine inventory level, anticipating needed supplies, shipping and receipt of supplies.  
  • Assembles components by examining connections for correct fit, fastening parts and subassemblies.
  • Perform general housekeeping of the work area.
  • Tasks can include but are not limited to welding, painting, operating machines and presses, assembly and disassembly of parts, wiring, shipping preparation, and performing quality checks and tests.
  • All other duties as assigned by the supervisor/team leader. 
Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED) is required.
  • Familiar with and ability to utilize all hand tools including wrenches, sockets, hammers, tape measures, crimpers, cutters, and steel banding.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude to use equipment and maintain general understanding of business process.
  • Familiar with and can utilize power tools.
  • Knowledgeable of and able to utilize computer systems.
  • Frequently required to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods.
  • Reaching and handling with high levels of dexterity.
  • Must be able to lift up to 25 pounds from floor to waist.  Occasionally required to lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Occasionally required to work near moving mechanical equipment.
  • Frequent exposure to various chemicals, sealants, and lubricants.
  • Occasionally required to work outside where weather conditions range from moderate cold to moderate heat.
  • Normal exposure to moderate noise levels.  Occasional exposure to high noise, levels where hearing protection will be required.
Core Competences:

  • Knowledge of and willingness to comply with all general work rules, policies and procedures, including safety guidelines and procedures.
  • Able to rely on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals.
  • Ability to learn to operate all equipment associated with the job; including, but not limited to, power hand tools, forklifts, skyjacks, cranes, and measuring devices.
  • Ability to identify routine problem causation, and correct routine problems, and willingness to learn.
  • Broad working knowledge and experience with standard work instructions.
  • Team oriented, must have the ability to work cohesively with others.
  • Must possess ability to work well in a manufacturing environment.
  • Must be detail-oriented and self-motivated.
  • Must be able to work in a multi-tasked environment.
Preferences:

  • Three (3) years in manufacturing experience preferred.
  • Prior experience in mechanical assembly, electrical wiring, precision measurement, blueprint reading and pipefitting is preferred.
