Job title: Service Technician 

Location: Lee's Summit, MO or Aurora, CO 

About Us

Cullum & Brown is an industry leading industrial equipment distributor and service company.  With over 135 years of industry experience, Cullum & Brown is a reliable solutions provider with locations in Kansas City and Springfield. We are an authorized distributor of Gardner Denver, Elmo Rietschle, Hoffman, Lamson, Tuthill pumps, Crane Deming, Travaini vacuum pumps, Graco, Dean Pumps, Grundfos, PowerEx, and Great Lakes. Cullum & Brown is proud to offer 24/7 emergency customer service for not only the brands we sell, but all makes and models. Our 18 factory-trained and certified technicians are prepared and the best in the industry. Join our team!  

 

Job Overview: 

On-site installation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of air compressor equipment. Requires 2-4 years plus of experience in the field. Familiar with electrical, pneumatic and mechanical drawings. Ability to manage time wisely to accomplish required actions quickly and precisely. Performs a variety of tasks. Works under general supervision, reports to a supervisor or manager. A certain degree of creativity and latitude is required. Primary equipment focus is rotary screw and centrifugal compressor technologies.  

Responsibilities: 

  • Conduct on-site installation of compressed air equipment and follow testing procedures to ensure proper working order 
  • Conduct on-site scheduled planned maintenance v 
  • Provide troubleshooting and repair support for customers and other field service personnel 
  • Cultivate and develop positive working relationships with customers, system users and company personnel 
  • Travel, often on short notice, to customer sites to resolve problems or support other field service personnel 
  • Complete and submit field service reports 
  • Provide training for customers and users on system maintenance 
  • Provide input for various reports including identifying and isolating unique problems 
 

Requirements: 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required. 
  • 3+ years’ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems. 
  • 1+ years of experience with Electrical/Electronic Technology or HVAC with basic knowledge of some or all of the following:  
  • AC/DC circuits, wiring diagrams/schematics, motors/controls, PLCs, HVAC electricity, controls, refrigeration systems and/or refrigerant certification.   
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 
 

Core Competencies: 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
 

Preferences: 

  • 3+ years’ experience on compressed air systems/centrifugal technologies/solid controls background is a plus.  While not required, those with knowledge in the service, diagnosis, and startup of both rotary and centrifugal air compressors, including dryers, cooling towers, and filtration systems are encouraged to apply. 
  • Military experience and/or sufficient mechanical working experience is a plus.   
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • The position is onsite based in Lee's Summit, MO or Aurora, CO 
 

Pay Range

  • The pay range for this role is $49,000-$76,200. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview: 
We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Sourcing Engineer to join our Compression Systems & Services Americas Sourcing Organization. This role involves supporting the development, implementation, and management of sourcing strategies to provide optimal supply assurance, pricing, flexibility, quality, and delivery performance. The Sourcing Engineer collaborates with engineering, operations, and quality teams, as well as key suppliers, to meet cost, quality, and delivery targets while fostering positive supplier relationships.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead supplier selection, negotiations, and RFP processes, including pricing, payment terms, lead times, and inventory programs, while fostering strong supplier relationships.
  • Identify and implement cost-saving opportunities through data analysis, hands-on material reviews, and continuous improvement ideation sessions aligned with plant priorities.
  • Collaborate with suppliers and internal teams to qualify new parts, address supplier performance issues, and ensure alignment with operational strategies like localization and plant rationalization.
  • Support new product development (NPD) activities by managing preliminary project costs, driving procurement efforts, and aligning with business cases through product launch.
  • Track and report sourcing activity metrics and savings, ensuring timely and accurate performance measurement while supporting plant teams in resolving escalated issues.
  • Coordinate with cross-functional teams—including commodity, materials, operations, engineering, finance, and quality—to complete projects within timelines and achieve expected benefits.
  • Represent the sourcing function in Value Analysis/Value Engineering (VAVE) and Major Model Review (MMR) events, ensuring post-event actions are executed effectively.
  • Promote continuous improvement through ideation sessions, aligning strategies to business priorities and addressing systemic supplier performance issues in quality, delivery, and warranty.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or equivalent.
  • 5+ years of experience working in an Industrial manufacturing environment with either sourcing experience or experience working with suppliers.
  • 2+ years of experience with vendor assessments and negotiating supplier agreements. 
  • 2+ years of experience with Microsoft Excel.


Core Competencies:

  • Complex decision-making
  • Excellent time management
  • Supply chain acumen
  • Project management
  • Relationship management


Preferences:

  • Lean manufacturing experience.
  • Experience using an ERP or CRM tool, preference is either Oracle, SAP or QLIK.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Onsite with up to 20% travel.

The pay range for this role is $80,000 - $90,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

SEEPEX, an acquisition of Ingersoll Rand in 2021, is a leading worldwide specialist in pump technology. Job Overview:

The Regional Sales Manager is responsible for driving sales growth within the Southeast territory by managing and developing distributor/channel partner relationships, meeting or exceeding booking targets, and serving as the product and technical expert for industrial pump solutions. This role is a highly autonomous, individual contributor position requiring strong technical aptitude, customer-facing skills, and extensive travel.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage and grow distributor/channel partner relationships across the assigned territory

  • Serve as the primary liaison between customers, distributors, and the internal SEEPEX sales and operations teams

  • Achieve or exceed annual bookings and sales targets for the territory

  • Support distributors with technical expertise, product application knowledge, and solution development

  • Collaborate with internal teams to develop quotations, manage opportunities, and support order execution

  • Conduct product presentations, training, and sales meetings for distributors and end users

  • Identify new business opportunities and drive market share growth

  • Accurately forecast sales activity and maintain CRM and reporting expectations

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.

  • 3+ years of field sales experience.

  • 1+ year prior experience selling, supporting, or applying industrial pump solutions in a field sales or technical sales environment.

  • 1+ year working knowledge of pump fundamentals, including applications, sizing considerations, and performance characteristics.

  • 1+ year experience discussing pump solutions with distributors, customers, and engineers, including technical and commercial requirements.

Core Competencies:

  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with the ability to navigate complex technical discussions

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills with the ability to present to both small and large groups

  • Ability to operate independently in a remote, field-based role

  • Strong organizational skills and comfort managing multiple priorities

Preferences:

  • Degree in engineering, business, or a related field

  • Experience within industrial, manufacturing, or process-related markets

  • Prior exposure to highly technical, application-driven sales environments

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This position is fully remote and requires approximately 75% travel within the assigned territory (MI, OH. KY, WV, PA, MD, DE, NJ, NY, CT, VT, RI, MA, NH, ME)
A company vehicle is provided. Candidates must be able to travel by car and air as needed to support customer and distributor demands.

Pay Range:

The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $90,000 – $115,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and geographic location. Hired applicants will be eligible to participate in a Sales Incentive Plan with a target incentive of approximately 30% of base salary.

This role is typically not eligible for relocation. Schedule: Monday – Friday 7:30AM – 4:30 PM
Pay Range: Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $35.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position. $3,000 Sign On Bonus!
 
About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.
 
Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
 

  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
 
Requirements:

  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
 
Core Competencies: 

  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner.
 
Preferences:

  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply. 
 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Title: CNC Machinist
Location: Mocksville, NC (Onsite) (338 Valley Rd. Mocksville, NC 27028) 
Shift: 2nd Shift (Monday - Friday 3PM - 11PM) - Full-time Direct Hire

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
We are looking for a skilled CNC Machinist to perform a variety of tasks as assigned in conjunction with the assembly of our product. You will ensure all parts fit correctly and are suitable for the final product. This position is responsible for safely performing high-level continuous work to quality standards. Assignments may change based on business demands. 

You must have desired technical knowledge and possess great manual dexterity. Ability to interpret instructions represented in manuals, drawings, schematics etc. and follow them with precision.

Responsibilities:

  • Uses blueprints, sketches, drawings, and/or job instruction sheets to produce dimensions and tolerances of finished work-piece and setup requirements.
  • Cutting tools, attachments, accessories, and materials on machines such as mills, lathes, grinders, machining centers, drill presses, and drill machines.
  • Enters commands to retrieve, input, or edit control information for CNC machines.
  • Sets up, operates, and monitors machine operation to detect malfunctions or out-of-tolerance machining, and adjusts machine controls or control media as required.
  • Utilizes a variety of measurement tools and methods to evaluate finished parts against specifications.
  • Reworks parts that don't meet specifications.
  • Confers with supervisor, engineers, and production personnel to resolve machining problems.
  • Follows all ISO procedures and safety rules, including wearing personal safety equipment and performing hoist inspections.
  • Routes completed parts to next machine according to the routing sequence.
  • Performs data entry on the computer to update part locations.
  • Updates work order cover sheets, daily production sheets, status sheets, and quality records.
  • Participates in regular communication among peers and Team Leads to maintain productivity and solve problems as they arise.
  • Operates with the close attention to detail required to meet print specifications, down to 0.0002in tolerances.
  • Maintains 5S standards of organization and housekeeping of work area.
  • Participates in improvement efforts for cell layout, process efficiencies, etc.
  • Attends monthly departmental meetings and quarterly town hall meetings.
  • Other assigned duties

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED
  • 2+ years of CNC machining experience

Key Competencies:
  • Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, blueprints, memos, and procedure manuals. 
  • Ability to effectively share information about job duties in one-on-one and small group situations to supervisor, customers, clients, and other employees of the organization.
  • Ability to perform basic calculations with numbers between 0.0001 and 0.1 
  • Ability to convert between metric and US standard units of measure. 
  • Ability to understand and carry out detailed written or oral instructions. 
  • Ability to deal with problems involving several variables
  • Ability to use standard problem-solving methods (ie. 5 Whys) as trained
  • Ability to stand and walk up to 8 hours continuously during a shift.
  • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs alone, or 70 lbs with assistance, repeatedly over an 8 hour shift
  • Ability to push or pull up to 35 lbs.
  • Ability to see or have vision corrected with glasses/contacts to an evaluated level of no worse than 20/35.

Preferences:
  • Associates degree, or training certification
  • Ability to effectively use tools such as the following: depth gages, bore gages, height gages, feeler gages, micrometers, calipers, deburring tools, die grinders, drill presses, overhead lifting equipment, etc.

This position will be based at our site in Mocksville, NC, with no anticipated travel.

Job Overview:

Power tools Electro-Mechanical Engineer dedicated to new product development located in Hampton, NJ.  At Ingersoll Rand Power Tools, we design, engineer and manufacture cordless and corded electric power tools for the assembly, industrial and vehicle repair markets.  This person will work closely with global cross-functional teams comprised of software, firmware, electrical and mechanical engineers as well as strategic sourcing partners, quality, operations, and product management.  The Mechatronics Engineer’s responsibilities are to develop new power tools by creating new product concepts, prototypes, testing and developing final designs ready for commercial launch.  This person must be a team player, form strong ties with others, manage a multitude of tasks, communicate clearly, and be effective and comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop and enhance mechanical, electrical and electro-mechanical systems for innovative new power tools that meet customer needs and global industry standards.
  • Prepare design concepts for analysis and rapid prototype validation.
  • Lead projects while collaborating with global internal team members, suppliers and operations from conceptual design through production launch.
  • Coordinate and drive the completion of testing.  Work closely and cooperatively with lab technicians during test execution to assure that test objectives are met.
  • Develop and maintain documentation including layouts, drawings, specifications, bills of material, test plans, lab reports and technical construction files.
  • Provide support to strategic sourcing partners, manufacturing, customer service, procurement, quality assurance departments and product management.
 

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor degree in Mechanical, Mechatronics, Electro-mechanical or Electrical Engineering
  • 5+ years of experience
 

Key Competencies:  

  • Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and manage multiple concurrent assignments.
  • Expertise in electronic circuit and electrical design, including microprocessors, sensors, wiring, connectors, and PCBAs; Altium experience preferred.
  • Experience integrating wireless technologies such as Wi-Fi 6, 5G, Zigbee, and Bluetooth into electro-mechanical assemblies.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing processes and product design fundamentals, including tolerance stack-ups, inspections, and reliability-focused design.
  • Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across teams and direct technical resources.
  • Preferred experience with electric motor controls, 3D modeling, Windchill PLM, Creo Parametric, and cordless power tools.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

Job Overview:
Operate, inspect, and clean furnace, as well as set-up die cast machines in relief of primary Furnace Tender. 
 
Responsibilities:

  • Operates furnace or furnaces to melt aluminum ingots or scrap used in die casting.  
  • Regulate furnace temperature and charge furnace with ingots and scrap aluminum as instructed.• Deliver metal, in proper amounts and proportions, to die cast machines for operation without interruption purposes. Will be required to oversee the distribution and supply of molten metal to machines, on a schedule in order to maintain central melt temperature.• Assist in cooling down furnace and inspect: lining for cracks or defects and distribution ladles.  Assist in repairs as instructed. Will be required to do material handling as needed.
  • Maybe required to set-up die casting cell to include ladle, auto-spray, robotic and trim press machines. Including removing and replacing die casting and making necessary adjustments on machines.
  • This position is responsible for the safety of others, as it pertains to filling ladles, driving lift trucks, and pouring metal into furnaces at the machines for machine set-up.

 Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.  Technical diploma preferred
  • 1+ years of Forklift Experience with License


Core Competencies: 

  • Regular exposure to heat, dirt, grease and fumes.
  • Regular exposure to noise levels exceeding 85 db (hearing protection required when exposure exceeds 85db).
  • Lifting/pushing/pulling/carrying up to - 5 lbs. constantly, 35 lbs. frequently, 75 lbs. occasionally
  • Sitting, standing, kneeling, climbing, bending, and stooping frequently
  • Lift truck (power or hand), shovel, furnace cleaning, skimming and fluxing tools, hand tools, hoist, plus required safety clothing and equipment.
  • Hazards are· serious cuts, burns, bruises and possible permanent injury; operator required to wear goggles and heavy gloves. While the job has definite hazards, caution by the operator will reduce hazards to a minimum.


Preferences: 

  • 1+ Years Prior demonstrated knowledge in all aspects of furnace operation required to include: cleaning, operation, and maintenance
  • Works from written or verbal instructions under general supervision, instruction, and guidance on unusual procedures and irregularities.  
  • Experience working in a die cast environment required prior to hiring or appointment to the position.  


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 

  • Fully site based based at our Sheboygan, WI facility.

The Distributor Development Specialist will play a key role in the ownership and oversight of sales compliance and governance of the business structure integrity. The Specialist helps maintain accurate business structure records, drives consistent operational practices, and supports cross-functional teams in executing distributor-related requirements. Additionally, this position is responsible for supporting the Distributor Development team with the creation and management of reports, legal document preparation, data & documentation management, and detailed record keeping.

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain ownership of sales compliance and governance activities to ensure the integrity of distributor business structures. 
  • Create, manage, and maintain reports, dashboards, and data sets to support Distributor Development operations. 
  • Prepare, organize, and track legal documents and agreements related to distributor activities. 
  • Ensure accurate and complete documentation through consistent data management and detailed record keeping. 
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to support distributor-related processes, requirements, and initiatives. 
  • Extract, analyze, and summarize data for reporting, forecasting, and decision-making. 
  • Support the development and communication of standard work, process documentation, and governance materials. 
  • Assist in researching issues, troubleshooting discrepancies, and proposing solutions that improve data accuracy and operational consistency. 
  • Maintain strong working relationships with internal teams and external distributor partners through clear and professional communication. 


Requirements:

  • 3+ years in sales, sales/customer support, or data management. 
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office required. 


Core Competencies:

  • Strong attention to detail, using critical and creative thinking. 
  • Ability to research and solve problems. 
  • Ability to handle multiple tasks in an efficient and professional manner. 
  • Self-directed, assertive, and teamwork-oriented. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
  • High level of communication and interpersonal skills. 
  • Ability to engage internal and external partners persuasively and positively. 
  • Proficiency using Salesforce to understand sales trends, competitive data, pricing, and discount structures. 
  • Capability to use AI tools to pull, analyze, and summarize data. 
  • Ability to write standard work and process documentation, and to audit distribution processes for compliance. 
  • Strong understanding of policy origins and reasoning, organizational culture, and procedural alignment. 


Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business or related field.
  • SAP experience preferred


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be onsite in Quincy, Ill. Possible travel up to 20% to attend scheduled meetings.

Job Title: Manager Materials, Industrial Manufacturing
Location:  West Chester, PA (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Own the Flow. Drive the Operation. Lead What Moves the Business. At the Ingersoll Rand West Chester site, you’ll step into a mission-critical hub where uptime, precision, and real-world impact collide. As Manager, Materials, you own the flow of materials, teams, and execution across a high-velocity manufacturing operation. You’ll lead an integrated network of material planning, buyer/planners, and production scheduling, ensuring seamless alignment from demand through delivery in a fast-paced, just-in-time, make-to-order environment.

This role carries full accountability for materials planning, inventory strategy, and supply execution, making you a key driver of plant performance, scalability, and continuous improvement. You will also own warehouse operations and inventory control end-to-end, ensuring accuracy, discipline, and integrity across physical inventory and cycle count processes. In addition, you will lead shipping and receiving operations through a supervisor and broader team responsible for inbound, outbound, and traffic execution—ensuring materials move with speed and precision across the site.

Deeply embedded in Lean and continuous improvement, this role drives impact across key KPIs including inventory turns, on-time shipping to request date, and days past due, while strengthening overall supply chain performance. You will ensure uninterrupted material availability to support production, proactively closing gaps, removing constraints, and elevating execution across the operation. What sets this role apart is the expectation for hands-on leadership when it matters most—month-end close, peak shipping or receiving volumes, and urgent customer demands. This is not a distance-based leadership role; it is real-time ownership of execution.

If you’re looking to lead broadly, execute deeply, and directly impact plant performance in motion—this is it.

Responsibilities: 
  • Safety: Fosters a safety culture and the implements safety policies and training in compliance with the company safety program and OSHA regulations to eliminate work related injuries. 
  • Inventory Control: Plans, orders, executes and manages storage of critical raw materials in accordance with supplier selections and guidelines provided by Sourcing Operations using SAP/MRP system to achieve the Master Schedule and Service requirements.? Oversees Lean raw material replenishment and storage on the production floor, including initial set up, daily usage estimates, trigger points, and reorder quantities. Coordinates with other facilities to forecast any remanufactured product requirements.? 
  • Strategy: Deploys strategic objectives into annual goals and individual KPIs across the organization by working with teams to set appropriate targets to build daily and monthly routines to manage the business. 
  • Product Lifecycle: Plans for material life cycle management and eliminates obsolete inventory items while working to reduce waste through the value chain. Develops and monitors compliance with requirements related to the introduction of new products. 
  • Management: Develops employees through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives. 
  • Problem solving culture: Develops a culture that is tied to Daily Management by leveraging tools, consulting skills and change management processes. 
  • Other responsibilities as assigned or required. 

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree 
  • 5+ years of experience in the integrated functions of materials management in a manufacturing environment that has embraced lean concepts, MRP manufacturing practices, and progressive supplier relationships. 
  • 5+ years of ERP System experience (SAP, Oracle, etc)
  • 3+ years in managerial experience focusing on standardizing planning & execution, reducing sourcing complexity, and talent development. 
  • 3+ years of experience driving cross-functional alignment across operations, supply chain, and production planning teams to execute on business objectives

Core Competencies: 
  • Integrated Materials & Inventory Leadership: Leads end-to-end materials management across planning, procurement, and inventory in a Lean, MRP environment—ensuring material availability while optimizing flow, replenishment (Kanban), and inventory levels.
  • Operational Execution & Continuous Improvement: Drives disciplined execution in a high-velocity, JIT environment. Identifies gaps, implements Lean improvements, and delivers on KPIs—inventory turns, on-time delivery, and past due reduction.
  • Strategic Planning & Lifecycle Management: Translates business objectives into clear plans and KPIs. Oversees material lifecycle, including new product introduction and obsolescence reduction, to minimize waste and complexity.
  • People Leadership, Culture & Problem Solving: Builds and develops teams through coaching and accountability. Fosters a safety-first, problem-solving culture using data, daily management, and effective change leadership.

Preferences:
  • Bachelor’s concentration (or international equivalent) in materials management, business, management or related degree.
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM). 
  • Experience implementing inventory control systems (Kanban) in a manufacturing environment. 
  • Experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes. 
  • Experience with visual and daily management systems. 

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • Position is based on-site in West Chester, PA

Shift: 3rd Shift, Monday - Friday (11pm - 7am) 
 
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
Operate, inspect, and clean furnace, as well as set-up die cast machines in relief of primary Furnace Tender. 
 
Responsibilities:

  • Operates furnace or furnaces to melt aluminum ingots or scrap used in die casting.  
  • Regulate furnace temperature and charge furnace with ingots and scrap aluminum as instructed.• Deliver metal, in proper amounts and proportions, to die cast machines for operation without interruption purposes. Will be required to oversee the distribution and supply of molten metal to machines, on a schedule in order to maintain central melt temperature.• Assist in cooling down furnace and inspect: lining for cracks or defects and distribution ladles.  Assist in repairs as instructed. Will be required to do material handling as needed.
  • Maybe required to set-up die casting cell to include ladle, auto-spray, robotic and trim press machines. Including removing and replacing die casting and making necessary adjustments on machines.
  • This position is responsible for the safety of others, as it pertains to filling ladles, driving lift trucks, and pouring metal into furnaces at the machines for machine set-up.

 Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.  Technical diploma preferred
  • 1+ years of Forklift Expereince with License


Core Competencies: 

  • Regular exposure to heat, dirt, grease and fumes.
  • Regular exposure to noise levels exceeding 85 db (hearing protection required when exposure exceeds 85db).• Lifting/pushing/pulling/carrying up to - 5 lbs. constantly, 35 lbs. frequently, 75 lbs. occasionally• Sitting, standing, kneeling, climbing, bending, and stooping frequently
  • Lift truck (power or hand), shovel, furnace cleaning, skimming and fluxing tools, hand tools, hoist, plus required safety clothing and equipment.
  • Hazards are· serious cuts, burns, bruises and possible permanent injury; operator required to wear goggles and heavy gloves. While the job has definite hazards, caution by the operator will reduce hazards to a minimum.


Preferences: 

  • 1+ Years Prior demonstrated knowledge in all aspects of furnace operation required to include: cleaning, operation, and maintenance
  • Works from written or verbal instructions under general supervision, instruction, and guidance on unusual procedures and irregularities.  
  • Experience working in a die cast environment required prior to hiring or appointment to the position.  


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
• This position will be based at our Sheboygan, WI facility.

Job Overview:

The Maintenance Technician plays a crucial role in ensuring the smooth operation of facilities. Responsibilities include promptly addressing repair requests, maintaining safety measures (such as alarms and fire systems), and handling emergency maintenance tasks. This role requires communication skills, adaptability, and knowledge of building systems and tools. Maintenance technicians contribute to the overall functionality and safety of the facility.

Responsibilities:

  • Install, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain CNC machinery, electrical systems, and pneumatic and hydraulic equipment
  • Troubleshoot and repair servo drives, motors, computer systems, NC controls, and high-voltage systems up to 480VAC 3-phase
  • Read work orders and specifications to determine machines and equipment requiring repair or maintenance
  • Inspect or test damaged machine parts, mark defective areas, and advise supervisors of repair needs
  • Dismantle and reassemble machines for repair or maintenance, using hand tools, cranes, jacks, or hoists
  • Work with blueprints, diagrams, and schematics to diagnose and remedy mechanical and electronic problems
  • Develop, coordinate, and maintain TPM events in the facility, and coordinate maintenance and PM repairs with production master techs and team leaders
  • Record production, repair, and machine maintenance information, and maintain inventory of machine parts and supplies

Requirements:

  • 2+ years of experience in manufacturing maintenance
Core Competencies:
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair pneumatic, hydraulic, electrical, electronic, CNC machines and controls
  • Ability to interpret schematics and blueprints
  • Ability to maintain mechanical machine tools including lathes, grinders, mills, drills, and machining centers
  • Ability to work with concepts when detailed prints, drawings, and specifications are not available
  • Exhibits teamwork skills
  • Ability to stand and walk up to 8 hours continuously, and lift up to 35 lbs alone or 70 lbs with assistance, repeatedly over an 8-hour shift
Preferences:
  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 3+ years of experience in CNC machine maintenance
  • Technical degree in Industrial Maintenance or equivalent, preferred
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements
  • This position will be based at our site in Sedalia, MO, with no anticipated travel.

Location: Hampton, NJ
 

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:

Power tools Electro-Mechanical Engineer dedicated to new product development located in Hampton, NJ.  At Ingersoll Rand Power Tools, we design, engineer and manufacture cordless and corded electric power tools for the assembly, industrial and vehicle repair markets.  This person will work closely with global cross-functional teams comprised of software, firmware, electrical and mechanical engineers as well as strategic sourcing partners, quality, operations, and product management.  The Mechatronics Engineer’s responsibilities are to develop new power tools by creating new product concepts, prototypes, testing and developing final designs ready for commercial launch.  This person must be a team player, form strong ties with others, manage a multitude of tasks, communicate clearly, and be effective and comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop and enhance mechanical, electrical and electro-mechanical systems for innovative new power tools that meet customer needs and global industry standards.
  • Prepare design concepts for analysis and rapid prototype validation.
  • Lead projects while collaborating with global internal team members, suppliers and operations from conceptual design through production launch.
  • Coordinate and drive the completion of testing.  Work closely and cooperatively with lab technicians during test execution to assure that test objectives are met.
  • Develop and maintain documentation including layouts, drawings, specifications, bills of material, test plans, lab reports and technical construction files.
  • Provide support to strategic sourcing partners, manufacturing, customer service, procurement, quality assurance departments and product management.
 

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor degree in Mechanical, Mechatronics, Electro-mechanical or Electrical Engineering
  • 5+ years of experience
 

Key Competencies:  

  • Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and manage multiple concurrent assignments.
  • Expertise in electronic circuit and electrical design, including microprocessors, sensors, wiring, connectors, and PCBAs; Altium experience preferred.
  • Experience integrating wireless technologies such as Wi-Fi 6, 5G, Zigbee, and Bluetooth into electro-mechanical assemblies.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing processes and product design fundamentals, including tolerance stack-ups, inspections, and reliability-focused design.
  • Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across teams and direct technical resources.
  • Preferred experience with electric motor controls, 3D modeling, Windchill PLM, Creo Parametric, and cordless power tools.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $140,000-$165,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview:

Power tools Electro-Mechanical Engineer dedicated to new product development located in Hampton, NJ.  At Ingersoll Rand Power Tools, we design, engineer and manufacture cordless and corded electric power tools for the assembly, industrial and vehicle repair markets.  This person will work closely with global cross-functional teams comprised of software, firmware, electrical and mechanical engineers as well as strategic sourcing partners, quality, operations, and product management.  The Mechatronics Engineer’s responsibilities are to develop new power tools by creating new product concepts, prototypes, testing and developing final designs ready for commercial launch.  This person must be a team player, form strong ties with others, manage a multitude of tasks, communicate clearly, and be effective and comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop and enhance mechanical, electrical and electro-mechanical systems for innovative new power tools that meet customer needs and global industry standards.
  • Prepare design concepts for analysis and rapid prototype validation.
  • Lead projects while collaborating with global internal team members, suppliers and operations from conceptual design through production launch.
  • Coordinate and drive the completion of testing.  Work closely and cooperatively with lab technicians during test execution to assure that test objectives are met.
  • Develop and maintain documentation including layouts, drawings, specifications, bills of material, test plans, lab reports and technical construction files.
  • Provide support to strategic sourcing partners, manufacturing, customer service, procurement, quality assurance departments and product management.
 

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor degree in Mechanical, Mechatronics, Electro-mechanical or Electrical Engineering
  • 5+ years of experience
 

Key Competencies:  

  • Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and manage multiple concurrent assignments.
  • Expertise in electronic circuit and electrical design, including microprocessors, sensors, wiring, connectors, and PCBAs; Altium experience preferred.
  • Experience integrating wireless technologies such as Wi-Fi 6, 5G, Zigbee, and Bluetooth into electro-mechanical assemblies.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing processes and product design fundamentals, including tolerance stack-ups, inspections, and reliability-focused design.
  • Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across teams and direct technical resources.
  • Preferred experience with electric motor controls, 3D modeling, Windchill PLM, Creo Parametric, and cordless power tools.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $140,000-$165,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title: Manager Materials, Industrial Manufacturing
Location:  West Chester, PA (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Own the Flow. Drive the Operation. Lead What Moves the Business. At the Ingersoll Rand West Chester site, you’ll step into a mission-critical hub where uptime, precision, and real-world impact collide. As Manager, Materials, you own the flow of materials, teams, and execution across a high-velocity manufacturing operation. You’ll lead an integrated network of material planning, buyer/planners, and production scheduling, ensuring seamless alignment from demand through delivery in a fast-paced, just-in-time, make-to-order environment.

This role carries full accountability for materials planning, inventory strategy, and supply execution, making you a key driver of plant performance, scalability, and continuous improvement. You will also own warehouse operations and inventory control end-to-end, ensuring accuracy, discipline, and integrity across physical inventory and cycle count processes. In addition, you will lead shipping and receiving operations through a supervisor and broader team responsible for inbound, outbound, and traffic execution—ensuring materials move with speed and precision across the site.

Deeply embedded in Lean and continuous improvement, this role drives impact across key KPIs including inventory turns, on-time shipping to request date, and days past due, while strengthening overall supply chain performance. You will ensure uninterrupted material availability to support production, proactively closing gaps, removing constraints, and elevating execution across the operation. What sets this role apart is the expectation for hands-on leadership when it matters most—month-end close, peak shipping or receiving volumes, and urgent customer demands. This is not a distance-based leadership role; it is real-time ownership of execution.

If you’re looking to lead broadly, execute deeply, and directly impact plant performance in motion—this is it.

Responsibilities: 
  • Safety: Fosters a safety culture and the implements safety policies and training in compliance with the company safety program and OSHA regulations to eliminate work related injuries. 
  • Inventory Control: Plans, orders, executes and manages storage of critical raw materials in accordance with supplier selections and guidelines provided by Sourcing Operations using SAP/MRP system to achieve the Master Schedule and Service requirements.? Oversees Lean raw material replenishment and storage on the production floor, including initial set up, daily usage estimates, trigger points, and reorder quantities. Coordinates with other facilities to forecast any remanufactured product requirements.? 
  • Strategy: Deploys strategic objectives into annual goals and individual KPIs across the organization by working with teams to set appropriate targets to build daily and monthly routines to manage the business. 
  • Product Lifecycle: Plans for material life cycle management and eliminates obsolete inventory items while working to reduce waste through the value chain. Develops and monitors compliance with requirements related to the introduction of new products. 
  • Management: Develops employees through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives. 
  • Problem solving culture: Develops a culture that is tied to Daily Management by leveraging tools, consulting skills and change management processes. 
  • Other responsibilities as assigned or required. 

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree 
  • 5+ years of experience in the integrated functions of materials management in a manufacturing environment that has embraced lean concepts, MRP manufacturing practices, and progressive supplier relationships. 
  • 5+ years of ERP System experience (SAP, Oracle, etc)
  • 3+ years in managerial experience focusing on standardizing planning & execution, reducing sourcing complexity, and talent development. 
  • 3+ years of experience driving cross-functional alignment across operations, supply chain, and production planning teams to execute on business objectives

Core Competencies: 
  • Integrated Materials & Inventory Leadership: Leads end-to-end materials management across planning, procurement, and inventory in a Lean, MRP environment—ensuring material availability while optimizing flow, replenishment (Kanban), and inventory levels.
  • Operational Execution & Continuous Improvement: Drives disciplined execution in a high-velocity, JIT environment. Identifies gaps, implements Lean improvements, and delivers on KPIs—inventory turns, on-time delivery, and past due reduction.
  • Strategic Planning & Lifecycle Management: Translates business objectives into clear plans and KPIs. Oversees material lifecycle, including new product introduction and obsolescence reduction, to minimize waste and complexity.
  • People Leadership, Culture & Problem Solving: Builds and develops teams through coaching and accountability. Fosters a safety-first, problem-solving culture using data, daily management, and effective change leadership.

Preferences:
  • Bachelor’s concentration (or international equivalent) in materials management, business, management or related degree.
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM). 
  • Experience implementing inventory control systems (Kanban) in a manufacturing environment. 
  • Experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes. 
  • Experience with visual and daily management systems. 

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • Position is based on-site in West Chester, PA

Job Title: Materials Planning Manager
Location:  Mocksville, NC (onsite)
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Job Overview:
This is a high-impact leadership opportunity at our Mocksville manufacturing plant, where the Materials Planning team plays a critical role in keeping production moving and customers supplied. Mocksville is entering an exciting period of growth, with new products and additional Gardner Denver product lines expected to transition into the facility. The Materials Planning Manager will have a visible and direct impact on production flow, inventory health, product-launch success, customer delivery, and the plant’s ability to scale effectively.  

As the Materials Planning Manager, you will lead and develop a team of buyer/planners supporting a diverse operation that includes pack assembly, rotary assembly, remanufacturing, and machine shop activity.  The plant manages a broad supplier base and a complex mix of short lead-time, book-and-turn orders and long lead-time, engineer-to-order projects. This is not a desk-only leadership position. You will remain close to the operation, helping the team anticipate supply gaps and drive execution across promise-date accuracy, past-due purchase orders, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, inventory turns, and over-entitlement reduction. You will also maintain a small hands-on purchasing portfolio supporting gears, pinions, and bull gears.  

We are looking for a hands-on materials, purchasing, or planning leader who can see around corners, bring discipline to a complex ERP/MRP environment, and turn competing priorities into clear execution. The right leader will combine urgency and accountability with empathy—staying connected to the team, coaching both experienced and developing buyer/planners, identifying risks early, and helping employees navigate the daily pressures of manufacturing materials management. If you thrive in a fast-moving manufacturing environment and want your leadership to make a meaningful operational difference, this role offers the opportunity to strengthen planning discipline, improve inventory performance, support successful product launches, and ensure the right parts arrive at the right time.

Responsibilities

Materials Planning and Supply Continuity:
  • Lead site material planning activities to ensure the timely availability of materials required to support production operations.
  • Own the stocking and replenishment strategy for all site raw materials.
  • Lead the site inventory optimization strategy, balancing material availability, inventory investment, and operational requirements.
  • Serve as the escalation point when Material Planners are unable to resolve supply, delivery, inventory, or supplier-related issues effectively.

Team Leadership and Development:
  • Lead, coach, and develop the Materials Planning team, establishing clear expectations for performance, accountability, and execution.
  • Ensure team members are properly trained and effectively utilizing ERP/MRP tools, planning processes, and Ingersoll Rand standard work.
  • Support employee development through regular coaching, structured training, and individual development plans.

Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement:
  • Champion Lean principles and continuous improvement across Materials Planning functions.
  • Strengthen planning discipline, standard work, problem-solving, and root-cause corrective action practices.
  • Drive improvements in material availability, inventory performance, planning accuracy, and overall team productivity.

Cross-Functional Leadership:
  • Serve as the Materials Planning liaison across Production, Procurement, Supplier Quality, Quality Assurance, Engineering, Accounts Payable, Finance, and other functional groups.
  • Coordinate resolution of issues involving supplier quality, goods received not invoiced, invoice discrepancies, engineering changes, new product development, and other material-related business needs.
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to identify supply risks, resolve constraints, and support production, product launches, and customer delivery requirements.

Team's Responsibilities - 
  • Material Planning and Inventory Management
    • Maintain material plans within the planning time fence to ensure continuity of supply.
    • Review open material requirements and proactively identify shortages, supply gaps, and inventory risks.
    • Maintain optimal inventory levels and appropriate safety stock for assigned parts.
    • Maintain accurate ABC classifications and other planning inputs required for the Plan for Every Part process.
    • Communicate forecasts, demand requirements, and replenishment plans to suppliers.
    • Maintain accurate item-master lead times based on supplier performance, process improvements, current constraints, product-family demand, and business priorities. 
  • Purchasing and Supplier Management
    • Perform timely and cost-conscious procurement of production, inventory, and maintenance, repair, and operations materials.
    • Review and analyze requisitions to confirm required quantities, specifications, delivery dates, and other purchasing requirements.
    • Monitor supplier performance related to delivery, quality, responsiveness, and pricing.
    • Expedite, de-expedite, or adjust purchase orders as needed to align material availability with production demand.
    • Promptly communicate supplier delivery, quality, pricing, or capacity concerns and drive timely resolution.
    • Escalate recurring or significant supplier-performance issues to Procurement and Materials Planning leadership.
  • Shortage Management and Production Support
    • Proactively identify and manage material shortages, including documenting root causes and supporting corrective actions.
    • Coordinate with Production Planners when materials cannot be delivered as promised and develop alternative supply or scheduling solutions.
    • Analyze material and capacity availability to support accurate customer promise dates for sales orders.
    • Work with applicable functional groups to resolve complex delivery requirements, competing priorities, and material constraints.
  • Quality, Invoice, and Transaction Resolution
    • Partner with Quality Assurance and Supplier Quality to resolve supplier-related quality issues.
    • Coordinate with suppliers and Accounting to resolve invoicing, receipt, pricing, and payment discrepancies.
    • Ensure material-related transactional issues are addressed promptly to prevent supply disruption or inaccurate financial records.
  • Productivity and Cost Improvement
    • Identify and implement cost-reduction, inventory-improvement, and productivity initiatives aligned with corporate goals.
    • Maintain an active pipeline of improvement projects and accurate financial records for productivity reporting and benefit tracking.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 5+ years of prior people management experience, ideally managing buyer/planner, purchasing, materials, planning, scheduling, or similar supply chain teams. 
  • 5+ years’ experience working in a manufacturing environment, such as industrial, assembly, machining, purchased-parts-heavy, or engineer-to-order manufacturing. 
  • 4+ years of experience in materials planning, purchasing, buyer/planner functions, master scheduling, and/or supply planning, or related manufacturing supply chain execution. 
  • 3+ years of demonstrated experience using ERP/MRP systems to support materials planning activities such as managing promise dates, purchase orders, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, inventory signals, and planning execution.
  • 2+ years’ experience in Excel skills to include utilizing formulas at an intermediate to advanced level 

Core Competencies
  • Hands-On People Leadership: Ability to coach, support, and hold a buyer/planner team accountable through regular engagement, one-on-ones, clear communication, and a balanced leadership style.
  • Materials Planning & Purchasing Execution: Strong understanding of purchasing, planning, promise dates, past-due POs, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, supplier follow-up, and purchased-parts support in a manufacturing environment.
  • ERP/MRP & Replenishment Systems: Ability to use ERP/MRP systems, Excel, and planning data to interpret demand signals, manage supply gaps, support pull or non-MRP replenishment where applicable, and make sound planning decisions.
  • Manufacturing Operations & Complex Production Environments: Experience supporting manufacturing operations, ideally including assembly, machining, engineer-to-order, job shop, mixed-model, or long lead-time environments.
  • Inventory, Lean & Visual Performance Management: Ability to drive inventory turns, reduce excess or over-entitlement, support lean planning practices, and use visual management tools or performance tracking systems to improve execution and accountability.

Preferences:
  • MBA and/orBachelor Concentration in Business or Supply Chain Management
  • APICS or CPIM certification
  • ERP Experience in Oracle R12
  • Experience managing a large, diverse, or complex supplier/materials portfolio
  • Experience in engineer-to-order, long lead-time, complex BOM, or mixed-model manufacturing environments
  • Experience driving inventory turns, inventory reduction, excess inventory reduction, or over-entitlement improvement

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This position is based onsite in Mocksville, NC

Location: Kansas City, MO

 

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

 

Job Overview:

This position is a Service Coordinator supporting the Customer Center and serving the compressed air needs of the industrial sector. The Service Coordinator is responsible for delivering exceptional customer service, and efficiently and effectively coordinating service technicians to meet customer needs.? Service Coordinators will manage and communicate with customers, sales teams, and management, while adhering to all order management and operational requirements of the position. 


Responsibilities: 

  • Answer incoming service calls and schedule technicians to perform preventive maintenance and service repairs. When scheduling and tracking service technicians, maximize operating efficiency and effectiveness.  
  • Guide and develop service technicians as appropriate, assisting in technical issue resolution.  
  • Ensure timely and accurate invoicing.  
  • Manage service inventory and rental fleets (repair status, location, etc.)  
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety, as well as Operational Excellence adherence in the Customer Center. Assist with the auditing process.  
  • Earn customer loyalty by effectively and efficiently managing customer interactions, ensuring customer satisfaction. Generate and follow-up on service quotes and seek new business whenever possible. 
  • Order and receive parts for jobs. Monitor shipping and receiving activities. Conduct service request data entry and management.
  • Submit warranty claims and ship parts to the factory. Ensure SARBOX compliance.  
  • Display team effort and dedication to customer by maintaining flexibility to work overtime and weekends as the business requires.  
 

Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED  
  • 2+ years of operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and working with hand-held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) 

Core Competencies: 

  • Exceptional organization, communication (verbal and written), and follow-up skills with the ability to effectively manage a high volume of priorities and commitments in a highly visible, fast-paced work environment.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, able to follow standard processes and work autonomously while understanding when to escalate issues that require further review.
  • Exceptional customer service skills, including proper phone etiquette and skills.

Preferences:

  • Associate or bachelor’s degree preferred
  • Knowledge of mechanical and electrical systems is preferred.
  • Salesforce experience a plus
  • Forklift certification a plus, not required (we'll certify you!)
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.? It requires employees to regularly lift and or move up to 10 lbs. and occasionally lift and or move 40+ lbs.
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:  

This position will be based in Kansas City, MO, and may travel occasionally within the US for meetings, employee training, and other business needs (5-10%).

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

  Job Title: Field Service Technician

Location: Indiana, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, Kentucky

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.


Job Overview: 
The Field Service Technician is responsible for providing field technical support for IR products, striving to be customer focused, fully responsive, and successful in meeting the 24/7 technical service needs of customers. Develop a collaborative relationship with the balance of IR to establish this area as the “go-to” place for technical field service knowledge.  Focus on providing valued solutions to customers, utilizing IR services as well as IR’s products. The job also carries a variety of incentive plans that are paid out annually. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Provide technical support during repair and/or installation, at customers’ sites, of IR’s equipment to ensure standards are met and the integrity of the equipment is maintained.
  • Ensure safe work practices are followed, reporting all safety incidents and near misses on a timely basis and maintaining the goal of “zero” lost time incidents
  • Work to improve responsiveness to customers by being available to make sales calls, perform technical walk downs, and provide solutions to customers that distinguish IR’s proposals and capabilities
  • Complete required reports, including Service Reports, Customer Call Reports, Expense Reports and Time Sheets, on a timely basis in order to provide appropriate follow-up to customers, including accurate invoicing for services.
  • Suggest improvements to processes and procedures in order to improve customer response time and accuracy of all data
  • Comply with Department Guidelines and Procedures in order to maintain appropriate standards of service provided to customers
  • Maintain proficiencies using vibration analysis and laser alignment equipment for balancing, testing, etc.
  • Generate sales leads from customers who could benefit from additional support in order to improve solutions provided, improve relationships, and grow IR installed base, collect information for the Customer Relationship Management [CRM] system and provide information to Sales for additional opportunities; and improve global visibility of IR Aftermarket in the CRM system

Requirements:

  • 3 years of relevant technical background including millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service experience, or equivalent experience
  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • The job includes an assigned vehicle for work use, so the candidate must have a valid license and be able to pass a Motor Vehicle background check.

Core Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Clear and concise communicator (both oral and written) 
  • Excellent collaboration skills
  • Strong computer skills in Microsoft® Word, Excel, PowerPoint 
  • Proven time management, organizational, problem solving, and prioritization skills to successfully complete responsibilities in a timely manner
  • Ability to resolve conflict, to apply critical thinking to solve problems and to escalate when needed
  • Highly organized with ability to work independently as well as part of a team
  • Ability to create and maintain strong relationships with customers, employees and Sales Reps
  • High moral and ethical standards; integrity is continuously apparent
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Comfortable and effective working in the “virtual world” 

Preferences:

  • Bilingual in Spanish is highly desired
  • Some technical schooling, classwork toward a degree in a technical area
  • Background evidencing positions with increasing responsibility and leadership
  • Experience specifying replacement parts for highly engineered equipment and products
  • Experience in industrial sales or technical selling
  • Troubleshoot vibration, system, and aerodynamic problems in equipment
 

Physical Requirements:

  • Heavy Lifting: Must be able to lift up to 50–75 pounds regularly.
  • Prolonged Standing: Ability to stand for 8–12 hours daily.
  • Frequent Bending: Regular kneeling, crouching, crawling, and stooping.
  • Climbing Ability: Safely ascend ladders, scaffolding, and stairs while wearing fall protection.
  • Manual Dexterity: Fine motor skills to handle small tools.
  • Awkward Positions: Working in tight, cramped, or confined spaces.
  • Overhead Reaching: Extending arms overhead for extended periods.
  • Visual Acuity: Close vision, color vision, and depth perception.
  • Weather Exposure: Working in extreme heat, cold, or rain.
  • Driving Endurance: Operating a service vehicle for long hours.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position is remote. The selected candidate will need to be based in Indiana, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, or Kentucky near a major airport.
  • Up to 80% travel, with possibility of international travel 

Pay Range: The pay range for this role is $65,000k - $85,000k annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.


What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. job.title: QA Inspector
job.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION:
The Quality Inspector performs activities related to quality assurance including, but not limited to: Inspection of components and finished goods, completing associated documentation, and support of other quality-related activities

KEY ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
•    Visual inspection, measurement, and functional testing of components and finished assemblies
•    Perform other inspection activities as needed for process validations
•    Document nonconformance’s when defects are identified
•    Comply with all company policies and procedures
•    General document review, scanning, and filing of quality records
•    Assist in investigations as needed
•    Other duties as assigned
•    Demonstrates all corporate values:
•    We think and act like owners.
•    We are bold in our aspirations while moving forward with humility and integrity.
•    We are committed to making our customers successful.
•    We foster inspired teams.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
•    High school diploma is required
•    2 years of experience performing inspections in a medical device manufacturing environment or equivalent is preferred
•    Ability to read and write in English
•    Experience with MS Office is required
•    Ability to use common gauges and measurement instruments such as calipers, micrometers, vision systems, pin gauges, etc.
•    Ability to follow controlled quality document instructions when performing tasks
•    Ability to interpret blueprints and engineering drawings
•    Knowledge of the application of sampling techniques
•    Knowledge of good documentation practices in a regulated environment
•    Ability to apply basic quality tools for problem-solving and improvement
•    Ability to add, subtract, multiply and divide into all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals
•    Ability to apply a high level of attention to detail and ability to work independently or as a team


PHYSICAL DEMANDS and WORK ENVIRONMENT: 
•    The employee is required to work in a cleanroom environment and is expected to follow the guidelines and rules for working in the cleanroom. This includes following the gowning procedures, covering hair in a hairnet, and wearing personal protective equipment as appropriate.
•    While performing the duties of this position, the employee is frequently/occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts.
•    The employee is occasionally required to sit, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
•    The employee is frequently required to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.



What We Offer

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. Job Title: Manufacturing Engineer
Location: Mocksville, NC

About Us:  
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
In this role as a Manufacturing Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of production processes. The Manufacturing Engineer is tasked with designing and refining manufacturing methods to boost productivity while maintaining high-quality standards and ensuring safety protocols. They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows. 

Responsibilities:

  • Suggests, evaluates, implements & manages multiple manufacturing projects from beginning to end
  • Evaluates, develops and implements machining processes on current or future assets
  • Implements capital equipment including evaluation, selection, run-offs, and implementation
  • Maintains manufacturing best practices including precision machining, lean manufacturing, and machine tool / tooling technologies
  • Evaluates non-conforming material and provides proper disposition
  • Leads special projects including NPD, insourcing, productivity and capital procurement
  • Designs tooling, gages and fixtures using 3D modeling software
  • Develops manufacturing routings internal and sub-con operations
  • Leads machine tool installations throughout the entire process
  • Supports production efforts through troubleshooting manufacturing issues
  • Ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards
  • Supports safety and environmental practices
  • Performs other duties assigned by immediate supervisor

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Industrial or Mechanical engineering. 
  • 4+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering.

Core Competencies:

  • Technical Expertise: knowledge of manufacturing processes and technologies. 
  • Problem-Solving: Analytical skills to develop effective solutions.

  • Exceptional customer service skills, including proper phone etiquette and skills. 

Preferences:
